alternatives.statement: Confirmed design: 5 independent vectors (narrative_format, canon, style, duration, platform); gate cycle (init/intake/check/canon-gate/breakdown/expand_technical/compile/render guide+final/audit/publish); LLM touchpoints limited to check, breakdown, expand_technical, review; assemble_prompts and verify_structure stay pure deterministic; per-block hash-lock with approved-as-content-hash-property invalidation (global style change invalidates everything, local element change invalidates only dependents); MCP exposes 19 CLI commands 1:1, no separate chat tool; generalized viewer is read+annotate+export only (never mutates state, decisions happen in chat), served locally on a fixed greedy-reserved port, localStorage scoped by project+revision+payload slug; publish is purely local (no git/deploy dependency) to adcrush/exports/<name>-<id>/<timestamp>/output/; kie-api-python installed via uv, invoked as an accessory CLI subprocess, never imported. Concrete schemas defined for narrative_format, canon, style_profile (proven with a chibi-comic worked example reusing verbatim 29-razones text), and block.

Reconciled M0-M10 milestone chain for implementing adcrush: M0 uv-managed scaffold + .mcp-adcrush/ workspace (git-style parent walk-up, slugified default name, refuses nesting under an existing ancestor); M1 intake with versioned attachments; M2 provider-agnostic multimodal LLM adapter with retry discipline and an inferred/missing split in check's output; M3 kie-cli as an accessory subprocess reading credentials from adcrush's own .env; M4 canon gate as shared library code (never a blocking synchronous call) plus a dedicated sheet-prompt template; M5 breakdown/expand/compile with three named invalidation scopes (global/local/narrative); M6 render guide/final queue; M7 forked/adapted viewer served locally, browser-launch left to the calling agent; M8 audit/publish with a revision-mixing correctness check; M9 official Python mcp SDK over stdio; M10 style gallery with capped, LLM-assisted iteration. A uniform JSON success/error envelope applies across all 19 commands.

Audio is FOUR independently configured layers but only THREE generators. Speech (audio.speech: auto|none|video_model|tts|both) comes from the video model for lipsync or ElevenLabs for narration. Sound effects (audio.sfx, default ON) come from the VIDEO ENGINE ALWAYS -- user decision, because diegetic sound must land on the action and only the model that generated the action knows when the foil crinkles or the door shuts. suno-sounds exists in kie-cli and is deliberately NOT used, because separately generated sfx would have to be placed against the EDL by hand, trading a real defect (drift) for a cosmetic one. Music (audio.music, default off) comes from suno_music. audio.muted forces all three off. Since Seedance's --generate-audio is one toggle for voice and sfx together, the common voice-over case keeps audio ON to get sfx, instructs the prompt to speak no dialogue, polices the bed with a new UNWANTED_SPEECH code, and ducks it under the narration. Disentanglement is therefore at the level of configuration and mixing, never generation.

A project declares VideoAudioConfig.audio_mode as one of voice_over (muted characters, narration over picture, speech from ElevenLabs), live_lipsync (characters speak on camera, speech from the video model), or voice_over_and_live_lipsync (both, mixed separately). DialogueLine.mode gains 'narration'. Classified once by the LLM at breakdown/expand from the brief and beats, persisted, and user-overridable, never silently re-derived. It must land before further video spend because it changes what the video model is asked for. Open constraint: Seedance's --generate-audio is one toggle for voice AND sfx, so voice_over mode cannot ask for sfx without speech; recommendation is to keep audio on, instruct no spoken dialogue, and add an UNWANTED_SPEECH defect code so the judge polices it.

audio/layers.py owns resolve() as a pure function and prompt_clause() as its only text output; video.py delegates both, so nothing re-derives the mapping. VideoAudioConfig is now speech (auto|none|video_model|tts|both) / sfx (default on, always from the video engine) / background_music / audio_mode / muted, and DialogueLine.mode gained 'narration' for copy spoken by a voice that is not on screen. audio_mode is classified once at breakdown from the whole brief, because a product-only ad with no people must be voice_over and never live_lipsync; it is returned as a PROPOSAL and accepted only when the project has neither an explicit speech source nor an existing audio_mode, so re-running breakdown never undoes a human decision.

adcrush canon describe --element --description corrects an element's description, records a canon.described ledger event, and DEMOTES the element to candidate with content_hash cleared. The demotion is the point: approved means a human accepted the SHEET, and the sheet still shows the old text; the hash is recomputed by generate, the step that knows the style and reference images it covers. Every block referencing the element therefore reads as stale, which is the honest consequence of changing what the element is. Replaces hand-editing canon.json, which bypasses the ledger and reads as an unexplained manual override.

CANON_FIDELITY_INTRO no longer opens with 'photoreal' and CANON_FIDELITY_FOOTER no longer says 'do not restyle'. Both were live-action assumptions stated as universal rules, and both contradicted the campaign treatment that the same canon grammar injects two sections later; because the intro came first it won. A motion-graphics campaign therefore got photoreal product photography for its canon, and every final conditioned on those sheets came out photoreal too. Fidelity in the canon grammar now means identity, proportion, material and colour, rendered in whatever medium the campaign's treatment states. Canon sheet ART is deliberately excluded from content_hash, so this fix does not invalidate existing sheets: a regeneration must be forced deliberately.

compile.canon_precedence_clause(style) states what the attached canon sheets are authority FOR: identity, proportion, colour and printed lettering, and NOT how they are rendered, because a sheet is drawn plainly so those facts stay readable and therefore looks photographic. Attached with nothing said, the model treats the whole sheet as the target and a stylised campaign renders photoreal while following every word of its treatment -- observed as STYLE_BREAK 0.62 on a block whose state lock already said 'no specular glints'. Returns empty for a style that already is photoreal, where the sentence would only cost prompt length. The video prompt's REFERENCE MAP header carries the same scoping.

ass.char_budget(style, canvas) computes how many characters physically fit one line, from the canvas width less the 8 percent horizontal margins and size_pct times frame height times CHAR_WIDTH_RATIO 0.62, and the smaller of that and the style's max_chars_per_line wins. The two are different numbers: max_chars_per_line is an editorial preference and was being used as the physical limit, so the motion-graphics register's 20 characters at size_pct 6.0 (about 1000px of Arial Black against 604px of usable width) shipped clipped at both frame edges. WrapStyle 2 means libass does not wrap, so anything too wide is silently CLIPPED rather than reflowed. The ratio is measured against Arial Black uppercase, the widest face any register asks for, so every other face breaks slightly early -- the safe direction. Budgets on 720x1280: motion-graphics 12, ugc-vertical 15, papercraft 16. Resolution-independent by construction since size_pct is a fraction of frame height; a 16:9 frame fits the style's full preference. The karaoke path had the same bug and never wrapped at all; it now breaks on the visible length, ignoring the \\k override tags. The guard test asserts for every style and register that budget times size_px times ratio fits the usable width, rather than freezing a golden file.

Captions are generated deterministically as ASS and burned with ffmpeg's 'ass' filter, never the 'subtitles' filter, which renders text but discards ASS animation and positioning. Verified on this machine: ffmpeg 7.1.1 built with libass, libfreetype, libfontconfig and libharfbuzz, both filters present, 2819 system fonts, so there is NO new runtime dependency. CaptionStyle becomes a struct (font_family, size_pct, fill, outline_colour, outline_px, shadow_px, position, animation none|word_pop|karaoke_wipe|bounce, max_chars_per_line, max_lines) and every major style must declare THREE substyles -- default, loud, quiet -- documented in a new docs/style-manual.md as a requirement of a style definition. An LLM computes the caption EDL (phrase grouping and per-word offsets) from the caption text plus shot timecodes; Stage 5 replaces the estimated word timings with ElevenLabs' real ones. StyleProfile.on_screen_text changes meaning from 'ask the model for text' to 'burn captions in post', generators are told there is no text at all, and TEXT_BURNED_IN inverts to fire when a generator produced text it was told not to.

Captions are planned by captions/edl.py, rendered by captions/ass.py and burned by captions/burn.py with ffmpeg's 'ass' filter as the last step of video-assemble, after the join trim. Composition onto the assembled timeline uses KEPT lengths, not clip lengths: trimming a join shortens what precedes it, so offsetting by clip length puts every caption after the first join progressively late. Captions never enter a held handle, because a caption there would be trimmed away. Word timings are labelled 'estimated' and are proportional to word length; the narration stage replaces them with measured ones. An LLM is consulted only for phrase grouping of a line too long for the style's budget, and its answer is REJECTED unless every word survives in order -- a caption is copy, and a model paraphrasing it is a defect.

Two layers. (1) The expand system prompt carries an explicit CAPTIONS ARE POST-PRODUCTION clause: copy goes in dialogue and nowhere else, because a caption is not something the camera sees, while words printed on the physical product are. (2) compile.strip_on_screen_text_directives removes whole sentences carrying an on-screen-text cue (caption, on-screen text, title card, text overlay, supertitle, subtitle) from beat, action, state_lock, entry_state/exit_state, shot_line and the video EDL relevo note. Sentence level because a generator handed half a sentence invents the rest; applied at prompt-assembly time so blocks.json keeps the author's words and no block hash moves. The cue list excludes bare 'reads' and 'lettering' because product packaging legitimately carries print. The invariant asserted in simulation is that no prompt carries a caption DIRECTIVE, never that the copy is absent: a speech video_model group is legitimately told to speak the line, and short copy like 'Made in USA.' is often the pack's own print.

video-loop takes --model/--draft-model (default seedance-2-fast) and --final-model (default seedance-2.5). The judge/retry ladder runs on the draft; every group whose review_status is 'pass' is re-rendered ONCE on the final model by media_review/tiering.py. Rejected and exhausted cuts are never re-rendered, because paying the premium for a cut the judge already rejected buys nothing. The final render is judged too, since a different model is a different model rather than a strictly better one, and on failure the draft stays promoted -- there is no ladder at this tier so failing safe means keeping what passed. The draft is preserved as <group>.draft.mp4, the only evidence of what the cheap model produced for the same prompt. Draft and final lanes are the same lane class with different model values, so transport, reference plan and rubric are shared by construction. Deliberate limitation: the reference plan is computed once from the DRAFT model's 9 slots, so the final render reuses those rather than 2.5's 30 -- same prompt, same references, different model, because changing inputs between tiers would make the comparison unattributable. Set --final-model equal to --model to disable.

elevenlabs/text-to-speech-multilingual-v2 runs on kie's normal market endpoints. Input: text (<=5000), voice (id or preset name), stability 0-1 (0.5), similarity_boost 0-1 (0.75), style 0-1 (0), speed 0.7-1.2 (1), timestamps bool (false), previous_text/next_text (<=5000), language_code (ISO 639-1). 68 documented voices with ids, names and character descriptions; default EkK5I93UQWFDigLMpZcX (James). Previews are plain files at https://static.aiquickdraw.com/elevenlabs/voice/<voice_id>.mp3, so a preview UI needs no backend. Two parameters are structurally important: timestamps=true returns WORD-LEVEL timings, which become the caption sync source so no transcription is needed anywhere; and previous_text/next_text keep prosody continuous across per-block narration segments, which is how the copy is split to match shot durations. kie-cli has NO ElevenLabs support today (routes.py knows only market, veo, suno), so Stage 5 needs an upstream PR of the same three-blocker shape as GPT Image 2.5.

kie-api-python PR #2 (squash-merged to main as 878c88b) adds elevenlabs/text-to-speech-multilingual-v2 and elevenlabs/text-to-dialogue-v3, a speech subcommand, a voices helper and MCP parity -- the same three blockers as GPT Image 2.5, including the MARKET_MODELS routing one that would raise on wait after a BILLED submit. adcrush side: kie.submit_speech defaults timestamps ON, because a segment rendered without them cannot be used for caption sync and paying twice is the only alternative; audio/narration.py owns the SpeechProvider protocol, gives every segment its neighbours via previous_text/next_text so prosody does not restart each shot, and runs a bounded fit loop -- two speed adjustments inside the provider's 0.7-1.2 range, then it REPORTS the overrun rather than truncating, because cutting audio halves a word and choosing between tightening copy and lengthening a shot is editorial. Timing parsing tolerates several plausible response shapes and returns no words rather than crashing on an unknown one.

kie's ElevenLabs voice field takes the voice ID. v3 validates it at submit and returns 422 naming the bad value; v2 accepts any string and fails minutes later with an opaque 500. CORRECTION to an earlier speculation in this stream that the field might want the voice NAME: that was read off one name-based submission getting further than an id-based one, which was noise -- both fail identically. The pipeline was already sending ids and never had this defect. Practical consequence for diagnosis: a v3 submit is a free, instant, specific check of a voice id that v2 will silently swallow.

expand --all targets only never-expanded or canon-stale blocks, so it cannot see a block that went stale because the expand SCHEMA gained a field -- blocks expanded before hook_device existed look current. expand --force re-derives every block, deliberately explicit because it changes every block hash and forces a full re-render.

run_expand_technical takes style= and prepends compile.medium_guidance(style), which quotes the treatment and asks for terms the medium actually has: no depth of field, bokeh or flare without a physical lens; no specular highlights or subsurface sheen in a flat graphic medium; cut edges and paper grain rather than skin pores in papercraft; say what MOVES and what CHANGES, which every medium can express. Positive rather than prohibitive because a banned-word list is endless and brittle -- bokeh is only wrong in a medium without a lens. It closes by naming the arithmetic: the treatment is two lines at the top of the render prompt and the expansion is four paragraphs below it, so whichever medium those words describe is the one that gets rendered. Optional, so a caller predating it keeps working.

canon generate takes --face-policy {infer,unrestricted,never} (CLI, MCP and generate_candidate). Excluded from content_hash like physical_profile, so setting it patches an approved element for free. It also DECIDES the character archetype: _is_partial_character reads face_policy first and only falls back to the description keywords for 'infer'. The keyword guess had misfired visibly -- an on-camera creator whose description mentions 'adult hands, short clean nails' was handed the hands-only character-partial archetype and rendered a sheet with no turntable. Before this flag existed, the only way to put a character on camera was to hand-edit canon.json.

EdlEntry gains hold_head and hold_tail, set by allocate_timecodes(handle_seconds=, hold_head=, hold_tail=) ONLY at clip ends that actually abut another group; a single-group ad reserves nothing. The timecodes are untouched because the clip is still generated at full length, and the hold reaches the model as a shot clause. video-assemble takes --trim-seconds (default 0.5) and trims internal joins only via the pure trim_plan(count, trim); _trim_clip re-encodes rather than stream-copies because -ss on a copy snaps to the nearest keyframe, and it takes the kept length from the group's PLANNED duration rather than probing, so a clip returning 15.07s has its overrun trimmed instead of making every join a different length. CORRECTION to an earlier claim in the plan: handles do NOT let a 30s brief deliver 30s. Each join removes 2 x trim and the generation length is capped by the model, so a two-group 30s ad delivers 29.0s. video-assemble now reports planned_duration_seconds and duration_seconds separately, and --trim-seconds 0 gives an exact-length concat.

Block.hook_device is written by expand for the OPENING block only and is hashed, so a changed hook re-renders. It is in EXPAND_SCHEMA but deliberately NOT in its required list -- demanding it everywhere would teach the model to invent one for shot 4 -- and run_expand_technical appends HOOK_GUIDANCE and enforces presence only when the block opens the ad and the format asks for a hook, failing hook_device_missing otherwise. A non-opening block has hook_device CLEARED even if the model volunteers one, because left in place it would bias a mid-ad shot toward an opening it is not. compile.calling_image_clause is keyed on hook_device rather than on order == 1, so hook_required: false costs nothing and the clause can never contradict an empty hook. HOOK_WEAK (floor major) has a full recipe ladder, and the judge rubric line is carried only by the block that has a hook, because a calm mid-ad shot judged against a hook rubric would flag the whole ad. Correction to an earlier claim: hook_required was not 'never read' -- it reached ONE sentence of the breakdown prompt; nothing downstream acted on it, which is the part that mattered.

adcrush's default image model is kie.DEFAULT_IMAGE_MODEL = 'gpt-image-2-5-sunburst' (GPT Image 2.5, Sunburst tier), replacing eight hardcoded 'gpt-image-2' literals. kie-cli resolves the alias to -text-to-image or -image-to-image from whether images are attached, so adcrush's f'{model}-{suffix}' status-model derivation is unchanged. Flare ('gpt-image-2-5-flare') stays available per call for drafts. submit_image gained an optional background passthrough (transparent|opaque|auto), omitted unless set. Upstream support is kie-api-python PR #1, squash-merged to main as 5c9fb10; adcrush keeps installing from main.

video-plan takes --keyframes {off,chained,independent}, defaulting to off. 'off' attaches only each shot's finished frame F# and ignores keyframe pngs even when they are already on disk. 'independent' is the original S10 behaviour, safe only on a single-shot clip where no neighbour can be contradicted. 'chained' reserves the name for the successor design (each shot's opening anchor is the previous shot's accepted closing anchor) and raises keyframe_mode_not_implemented rather than silently behaving like something else, so flipping the default is not a dead end.

Measured on the same engine the same day. Failing codes by attempt: live-action group-1 4/2/2, live-action group-2 8/4/5, stylised group-1 5/6/5/5. Live action roughly halves its defects at intensity 1 and then plateaus; the stylised clip never improves, with CANON_DRIFT and TEXT_GARBLED surviving every intensity while the others rotate, and intensity 3's simplification introducing HOOK_WEAK. Consequences: max-retries 1 is the right default for a stylised group, since attempt 2 bought nothing in three of four measured ladders and attempt 3 has twice made things worse (WRAPPER_SIZE on the image ladder, HOOK_WEAK on the video one); a stylised campaign's remaining defects are compositional rather than instructional and are fixed by writing different beats per the style manual's measured limits; and live action is where the ladder earns its cost, group-2 going from 8 failing codes to 4 for one 3.72 dollar attempt.

Four decisions locked. (1) Join trim approved AND handles reserved at plan time, so allocate_timecodes holds trim_seconds of tail per group and a 30s brief still delivers 30s. (2) sfx gets its own switch but keeps the video engine as its generator (see the audio-layers record). (3) BOTH ElevenLabs models are wired and switchable; multilingual-v2 is the default because it returns word-level timings while text-to-dialogue-v3 does NOT, so choosing v3 means estimated caption timing or rendering each speaker separately on v2 -- the CLI states this trade at the point of choice. (4) The truncated sixth observation is still unresolved; the user asked for the question to be clarified, and nothing in the plan depends on it.

Lane 2 must pass a simulation contract before ANY live spend, the same discipline as Lane 1's Phase B: real adcrush code, fake vendors, under adcrush-cli/simulation. New fakes: fake_speech.py (a SpeechProvider returning a tiny valid WAV plus deterministic synthetic word timings derived from character counts, recording voice id, timestamps and previous_text/next_text), and fake_kie extended with the two ElevenLabs slugs. NO ffmpeg fake and NO sfx fake -- ASS burning and audio mixing are precisely what a fake would hide, and sfx arrive inside the fake clip's own audio track as they do in production. Eleven scenarios: captions_voice_over, voice_over_silent_plate, unwanted_speech, captions_lipsync, captions_both, fully_muted, caption_substyles, unsafe_copy, v3_timing_trade, handles_and_trim, model_tiering, keyframes_off, hook_weak. New checks include check_generate_audio_matches_resolution, check_prompt_forbids_dialogue_in_tts_mode, check_ass_is_valid_and_timed, check_captions_use_real_word_timings, check_no_generator_text_requested, check_speech_gate_blocks_before_submit and check_assembled_duration_matches_brief.

The legacy boolean migration is deliberately asymmetric: voice: true maps to speech='auto', NOT to 'video_model'. It was the DEFAULT value rather than a considered decision about narration, and treating it as explicit would make every pre-existing project permanently outrank its own classifier with a value nobody chose. voice: false WAS a deliberate departure from the default and is respected as 'none'. The simulation caught the original mistake: the canonical workspace seeds a legacy config, so the classification was being refused and the voice_over prompt never forbade the model's dialogue.

assemble_final_video wraps the narration attempt: on AdcrushError it finishes the cut without narration, burns the captions on the planner's estimated timings, and records narration.failed with the vendor's code in both the ledger event and the caller's result. Re-running video-assemble once the provider recovers adds the voice and regenerates no clips. The posture generalises: the expensive, irreversible artifacts are the generated clips, so a cheap optional layer failing must never invalidate them.

video.assemble_final_video takes audio= and speech_provider=. When audio.layers.resolve(...).speech is tts or both it renders one narration segment per block via audio/providers.py, places each at an explicit adelay through audio/mix.place_segments, ducks the clip's own bed to BED_GAIN 0.35 with mix_narration (never replaces it -- the provider's audio flag stays on for sfx), and records runs/<rev>/video/narration/narration.json. The DELAY for each block is the same number that block's first caption starts on (captions.edl.block_offsets), so audio and captions cannot drift: one derivation, used twice. Ordering is plan captions -> render narration -> adopt measured timings -> burn; burning first would freeze the planner's estimate into the deliverable while the real read was already known. No provider is constructed unless the run is --live --yes, so a dry run still produces the cut and reports the skip in the ledger.

captions.edl.caption_lines is the single predicate for 'this line is on screen' (modes cartela and narration), and video.narration_segments projects from it rather than applying its own rule. In a voice-over ad the on-screen copy IS the script, and every project written before the narration mode existed keeps its copy in cartela -- selecting only narration rendered nothing on the canonical scenario. dialogo is excluded: the video model performs a character speaking in shot. A line whose printed form does not normalise and that carries no voice_over is skipped rather than guessed at; speech_safety.check is what surfaces those.

Every generator is now told there is no text in frame beyond what is physically printed on the product: the video prompt unconditionally, compile._dialogue_section (captions and narration removed, only performed speech survives because it changes the pose), _caption_mode_section (returns nothing), and keyframes.caption_for (always None, because a lettered keyframe becomes a reference teaching the video model to letter too). Copy reaches a video prompt only as a spoken cue, and only when the video model is the one speaking -- otherwise the clip would speak over the narration laid on top. On the judge side the 'required caption present and correctly spelled' question is gone, which is what produced five false TEXT_GARBLED flags on one live pass, two over the confidence gate and each costing a render, because a caption fading in over the first second looks missing in a sampled frame. TEXT_BURNED_IN now means ANY text not printed on the product; TEXT_GARBLED narrows to product lettering, which still matters because a misspelled pack is a brand defect.

video.NO_TEXT_RULE is a single string used by the video prompt and by every final image prompt (compile.no_text_rule()), widened to name headlines, stat callouts and buttons alongside captions, subtitles, titles and watermarks. The image lane had never had it: a 'final lockup' beat came back as a finished static ad with a REAL COFFEE. MORE YOU. headline, stat callouts and a SHOP NOW button, none of it requested, at TEXT_BURNED_IN critical 0.97. A model that knows what ads look like volunteers the typography unless told the frame is not where it goes.

New style papercraft.yaml, generalized from the client reference reel YouChews_Papercraft_Unbuild.mp4 (1080x1920, 24s). Describes the craft and the tabletop only, never a product or ingredient: every object sculpted from matte paper on a seamless warm-paper ground, straight-down or high three-quarter framing, soft even top light with gentle contact shadows, warm neutral palette, camera_rig tripod, its own caption_style, on_screen_text true. Any campaign can adopt it.

CanonElement.print_critical declares that an element carries printed copy which must be reproduced exactly, so its SHEET is the only source of that wording. build_reference_plan ranks print-critical sheets ahead of every other canon sheet, so reference truncation cannot reach them; canon generate --print-critical sets it. Declared rather than inferred from the description, for the same reason face_policy is: reading prose for the word 'copy' fails silently and in English only. Excluded from compute_element_hash -- a fact about how the element must be REFERENCED, not about what the art is -- so declaring it never forces a billed re-render. The underlying principle: a shape survives being described ('a low flat square slab, width clearly greater than thickness' is actionable prose and the shape-lock bullets work), but thirteen lines of pack copy reach a generator as thirteen chances to invent. Reference priority is therefore not one fixed order; it depends on whether the fact a sheet carries can travel in words at all.

At the canon gate the expand LLM's product descriptions were overridden with the approved product truth: it had proposed a 3cm rounded chew with a small wordmark where the real chew is a flat 2.5cm square under all-over tiled foil. The papercraft reference reel renders the chew as a ROUND rosette; the canon keeps the real flat square and carries the rosette as a die-cut pattern on its top face. The real 30-count pouch is DARK COFFEE-BROWN with a gold front panel, NOT black: both new projects' pouch canon was regenerated with the full front copy transcribed from the photo. This matters beyond the sheet, because the description feeds the judge's rubric -- 'black pouch' would make the judge flag a correct render as CANON_DRIFT and burn video retries. coffee-chews-ugc-v2's youchews_retail_bag_sealed still says black and should be corrected.

Generator-facing prompt text is written as description of the wanted shot, not as stacked prohibitions: FRAMING_RULE, IMPLIED_FACE_ACTION_RULE, SHAPE_LOCK_SHARED_BULLET, the caption/anti-bleed/hard-cut constraints and the clip-endpoint line. PhysicalProfile.must_not is no longer rendered into any generator prompt; it reaches the judge's rubric verbatim instead. The reason is mechanical: a diffusion model told 'no cube' draws a cube, while the judge is a language model and reads prohibitions correctly. The HARD CONSTRAINTS header is unchanged because recipes.split_shots keys on it.

render-assembly and keyframes take --no-wait, --poll-interval and --max-wait, and wait by default. Each underlying cycle is ONE bounded pass that submits, reports what is in flight as pending, and returns; the --review stages are driven to completion by media_review.loop.run_until_settled, but these two had no driver. A single call therefore left everything pending, and a runbook that stepped straight on to video-plan planned WITHOUT the G# and K# references those stages exist to produce. cli._drive_to_completion repeats the pass until nothing is pending, it halts, or max_wait expires; each pass is idempotent and never resubmits an in-flight job.

_shape_lock_bullets states print-critical elements first and MAX_SHAPE_LOCK_BULLETS is 5 (was 3). Taking the first N in reference order let three chew-and-wrapper elements fill the cap while the retail pouch -- the hero prop of the failing shot -- had no constraint line anywhere in the prompt. The cap is a length guard, not a ranking; 5 bullets cost about 200 characters against 2.3k of headroom under the 6k budget. Same principle as the reference plan one layer up. The fallback chain already reaches physical_profile.must, so an element carrying only a positive must does get a line -- the ingredient set's counts had simply been cut by the same cap, which is why it came back with five beans and an invented halved coconut.

build_reference_plan takes style= and promotes the FIRST shot's F# to just after the storyboards when compile.is_stylised_medium(style). Without it a nine-slot model filled up with G + three B sheets + five canon sheets and dropped every final, leaving the video model with sketches and plainly-lit turntables and no example of the medium -- the same failure the image lane had one stage upstream. The original 'finals last' ordering was reasoned on a photoreal campaign, where the canon sheets already are the look, and that case keeps it. is_stylised_medium is shared with canon_precedence_clause so the two cannot disagree about what stylised means.

captions.edl.adopt_measured_timings returns the track plus a per-block mode. A block whose measured word count equals its captions' word count is retimed word for word (measured). A block whose counts differ -- the NORMAL case for number-heavy copy, since 100mg is one caption word and three spoken ones -- has its captions linearly warped onto the measured duration from the block's own offset (fitted): phrase bounds become correct, the intra-phrase sweep stays an estimate. Dropping back to the estimate in that case, as the first implementation did, would have left exactly the copy stage 4 exists for unsynced. Track-level timings is measured when every block matched, fitted when some were warped, mixed when some block had no narration at all.

UGC styles (ugc, ugc-vertical) burn editor captions into finals, keyframes and video: exact text in the caption style (bold white sans, drop shadow, upper-middle safe zone); the judge requires them (missing/illegible -> TEXT_GARBLED) and flags only other text as TEXT_BURNED_IN; styles with on_screen_text=false keep the previous VO-only behavior.

Contract for the video self-improvement lane: every generated sheet carries a unified printed slug (six-zone layout catalog, guide vs canon grammar, campaign-format canvas); video prompts become referential 15s EDLs (<=3.5k chars, hard 6k) addressing sheets by slug/@Image index; total duration must be a multiple of 15s and groups exactly 15s; a media_review engine judges clips/images with Anthropic vision and retries at most 3 times with additive recipes (intensity 1 soft, 2 hard, 3 may simplify the beat); an append-only JSON ledger feeds a new adcrush dashboard; adcrush stays the CLI boundary; approved canon sheets are never regenerated; no assemble/music in this lane.

S10 keyframe expansion: per planned shot, FIRST/MID/LAST 2K keyframes at the campaign aspect derived by the LLM from F# + the EDL line; first/last carry the first/last caption line when the style burns captions in, MID never; slugs K:{order}-first|mid|last replace F# in the reference plan when complete; attached as first/last frames + references only for models flagged supports_first_last_with_references (none today), else all references; runbook video-plan -> render-assembly -> keyframes -> video-plan -> video-loop.

audio/voices.yaml holds 67 voices with the vendor's id, name and character description plus OUR tags and good_for, which is the piece the vendor docs lack. The catalog is 67 entries, not the 68 the kie docs claim: the page lists 67 rows, so one is a duplicate or a doc slip, recorded rather than padded because a fabricated entry is worse than a known gap. STYLE_AFFINITY maps each style to the tags that suit it, as data, so a new style is one row. propose() returns a ranked shortlist WITH the reason each entry scored, never one silent answer, because voice is a taste decision and the job is to narrow 67 options and explain why. A chosen voice persists as audio.voice_id -- named voice_id and not voice, because that name belonged to the legacy boolean the migration validator pops and reusing it would make one key mean two types depending on the file's age. An unknown configured voice FAILS rather than falling back: shipping an ad in a stranger's voice is worse than stopping. adcrush voice list|preview|set, with a self-contained audition page needing no API call and no backend.

DialogueLine gains voice_over, the SPOKEN form of text, and audio/speech_safety.py normalises the common cases while refusing the rest. No new dependency: a number-to-words covering ad copy plus a units table beats pulling in a locale model. Money is read as units and subunits, so $9.45 is 'nine dollars forty-five' and never 'nine point four five dollars', which is what a generic decimal rule produces and what no narrator would say. Ambiguity is LISTED rather than guessed: AMBIGUOUS_ABBREVS holds short forms with more than one reading (m metre or minute, t tonne or teaspoon, c cup or Celsius, tsp, min) and each demands an explicit voice_over, because putting them in UNITS would be choosing for the user. An explicit voice_over always wins over normalisation. The gate is _require_speakable_copy in run_video_loop -- the last free moment before spend, not plan time which is free and should never block -- and it applies whoever speaks, since the video model reads the copy too when it provides the dialogue.

A 2K GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst render costs 10 kie credits. A 15s seedance-2.5 720p clip costs roughly 1,000 -- two orders of magnitude more, and the single most important number when planning a run. kie charges a clip when it SUCCEEDS rather than when it is queued, so a credit reading taken while jobs are in flight understates committed spend; a budget guard must reserve for every queued job, not only for future submits. Harvesting an already-paid clip is free: video-loop --max-retries 0 polls the in-flight job, downloads, judges once and best-effort promotes without ever submitting.

kie bills 100 credits to the dollar (our 945-credit clip matches kie's published $9.45 for the same generation). Measured from our own receipts' creditsConsumed: gpt-image-2 2K = 10 credits ($0.10); gpt-image-2-5-sunburst 2K = 10 credits ($0.10) -- IDENTICAL, so there is no cost argument for downgrading the image model; seedance-2-fast 15s 720p = 372 credits ($3.72); seedance-2-5 15s 720p = 945 credits ($9.45), 2.5x more; suno V5_5 = 12 credits. The 30s live-action ad cost about $50.85 in total, of which $37.80 was one group's four-attempt retry ladder. Two errors caught while building. (1) The unknown-abbreviation guard ran on the OUTPUT, which is too late: after normalisation the digit has become a word, so '3 tsp' read as the innocent 'three tsp' and passed. It now runs on the input. (2) Flagging every short word after a digit rejected '$9.45 today' and '1,095 cups', both of which read perfectly; attached letters ('100mg', '3tsp') are always an abbreviation and must be known, while spaced ones only fail when the word is genuinely ambiguous. pytest 531 passed, simulation 15/15. documents.title: Goals

alternatives.statement: Captions move out of the generator into a deterministic post-step: own a captions module that writes ASS (Advanced SubStation Alpha) from the EDL plus the style's caption_style, burned with ffmpeg's 'ass' filter, NOT the 'subtitles' filter which discards animation. ASS gives per-word karaoke timing, outline, shadow, font, size, colour and absolute positioning, i.e. the CapCut/TikTok look with real control, and ffmpeg is already a hard dependency. Deliberately NOT adopting ai-video-captions, captionforge or similar: they are all transcription-first (Whisper then ASS), and we already hold the exact caption text and timecodes, so transcription would only add a dependency and inject recognition error. Second-order win: with captions in post, both image and video prompts can demand no text at all, so TEXT_GARBLED and TEXT_BURNED_IN stop being failure classes the generator can fail on -- a direct attack on the retry ladder that dominates cost. StyleProfile.on_screen_text changes meaning to 'burn captions in post' and caption_style becomes a struct.

First real campaign built with adcrush: YouChews Coffee Chews 30s/9:16 UGC-vertical Reel, 6 blocks, real brand assets from Google Drive, all rendered cleanly in rev-002. PDF export committed to research/coffee-chews-ugc-reel/. Creative iteration and M-E per-style validation remain open.

Two further changes. (1) Hooks: the first 5 seconds get their own contract. NarrativeFormat.hook_required already exists and is NEVER read -- dead config to be enforced: expand writes a hook_device on block 1, the judge scores the first shot against a hook rubric (subject readable within one second, movement in the first half-second, a visual question), and a new HOOK_WEAK code gets its own recipe ladder; block 1's image prompts bias toward higher contrast and a tighter subject. (2) Assembly trim: trim a default 0.5s at every internal join (tail of clip N, head of clip N+1), parametrizable via --trim-seconds and assembly.trim_seconds. Caution: trimming shortens the total, so a two-group 30s ad lands near 29s -- either report the real duration or design the EDL so each group's last half-second is a held handle. Silently delivering 29s for a 30s brief is exactly the drift this project exists to remove.

S10 keyframe triplets are to be OFF by default; pass the block's finished frame as the single anchor. Observed failure: the beat where the talent enters the car reads as two different cars. Cause: a triplet imposes three hard anchors per shot (nine per 3-shot clip plus the clip endpoints) and each block's triplet is planned INDEPENDENTLY from its own final frame, so block-4's last frame and block-5's first frame are unrelated renders of the same place and the model resolves the contradiction by cutting to a different car. Generalisation: any per-item reference generation must either be CHAINED from the previous item's accepted output or not used at all -- independently generated anchors are worse than fewer anchors. Keep the triplet as an opt-in for single-shot clips, where there is no neighbour to contradict.

Lane 2 is planned in docs/plans/captions-audio-and-hooks.md, seven stages ordered by leverage per dollar because measurement showed re-rendering, not model choice, dominates cost (one group's four-attempt ladder was $37.80 of a $50.85 ad). Stage 1 stops the bleeding: keyframes off by default, a parametrizable join trim, and model TIERING rather than downgrading. Stage 2 classifies audio intent. Stage 3 builds deterministic ASS captions. Stage 4 adds voice-over-safe copy. Stage 5 integrates ElevenLabs narration with a tagged voice catalog and a preview view. Stage 6 makes the hook a contract. Stage 7 is the integrator.

New general rule from the car-teleport artefact: per-item reference generation must either be CHAINED, each item derived from the previous item's accepted output, or not used at all, because independently generated anchors are worse than fewer anchors. A keyframe triplet imposes three hard anchors per shot (nine per 3-shot clip plus the clip endpoints) and each block's triplet was planned independently of its neighbours, so consecutive anchors were unrelated renders of the same place and the model cut to a different car. video-plan gains --keyframes {off,chained,independent} defaulting to off; 'chained' reserves the name for the upgrade so the default change is not a dead end; 'independent' preserves today's behaviour for single-shot clips where there is no neighbour to contradict.

Design a reusable, LLM-agnostic (OpenAI/Anthropic), 100%% CLI, no-agent system (adcrush) for authoring and publishing ad-creative storyboard image sets, generalized from the 29-razones reference implementation, with a future image-to-video lane explicitly deferred.

Baseline model policy, corrected by measurement. KEEP gpt-image-2-5-sunburst for images: it costs the same 10 credits as gpt-image-2 and is visibly better, so downgrading saves nothing. DO move video off seedance-2.5 as the default: 372 vs 945 credits for the same 15s 720p clip. The real trade-off is references, not price -- seedance-2/-2-fast accept 9 reference images against 2.5's 30 and cap at 15s, and one group's prompt already carried 16 references, so seven would be dropped with a warning, a canon-fidelity regression. Preferred shape: tier it with --draft-model and --final-model, running the judge/retry ladder cheap and promoting the accepted cut once on the expensive model, mirroring the Flare/Sunburst split already in place for images. A four-attempt group then costs $14.88 plus one $9.45 final render instead of $37.80.

Implemented the long-deferred image-to-video lane: video.py (clustering/prompt assembly/reference selection/hash-lock/async cycle), async_jobs.py (shared credit-halt/retry extraction), kie.submit_video(), new CLI+MCP surfaces. Validated against real Coffee Chews rev-002 data (clean 2x15s groups, 6 refs each, zero warnings). 168 tests passing. Real --live --yes submission smoke test still needs explicit user authorization.

Render 15s video blocks reliably and know without human frame-scrubbing whether they succeeded, proven by one budget-capped live pass on campaigns/coffee-chews-ugc-reel (<=3 retries/group) after a full offline simulation passes.

Printed form and spoken form are two different fields and conflating them is the same class of error as conflating a canon id with a description. Add DialogueLine.voice_over alongside text, plus a DETERMINISTIC pre-flight that fails before any video render when a spoken line contains a token that does not read aloud correctly: unit abbreviations (mg, g, oz, ml, kg), digit-group separators (1,095), currency, percent, ranges, initialisms (USA, TM) and URLs. Ship a normaliser for common cases and require an explicit voice_over for anything it cannot handle -- never silently guess. This lets the printed caption stay tight ('100mg caffeine. 25 calories. 2g sugar.') while the voice-over reads naturally.

alternatives.statement: adcrush-cli/ built and tested (91 passing tests): M0-M9 fully implemented, M10 11/12 style profiles authored. kie-api-python installed for real and confirmed interface-compatible. Package build verified to include bundled YAML/static assets. Viewer verified live in a real browser (guide/final toggle, scoped localStorage notes, clipboard export). Next: user-authorized real --live end-to-end run (real LLM + kie-cli spend).

Fixed and verified (with real spend) a significant bug: render.cycle() never attached approved canon reference sheets as image references, only guide PNGs, causing visible brand drift across independently-rendered blocks. Fix (canon registry param, attach all canon_refs' sheets for guide+final, correct image-to-image poll model) confirmed by clearing stale outputs and re-rendering for real -- all 3 finals now consistently show the same mug/logo. 105 tests passing. Republished corrected revision.

Completed and fully confirmed the design phase for adcrush (reusable ad-creative storyboard CLI); journal reusable-storyboard-cli marked status: stable. Next recommended step: scaffold the uv-managed adcrush CLI per the reference interface (19 commands / MCP tools), author the remaining ~11 style-profile templates, wire up kie-cli as a uv-installed subprocess dependency, and build the generalized local viewer/server. No open design ambiguity blocks starting implementation.

Milestone plan fully reconciled after 6 simulation rounds; no open issues block starting implementation. Next step: build M0 (uv scaffold) and proceed autonomously through the milestone chain, pausing only for real credentials or an actual live-spend confirmation.

Completed a real, user-authorized end-to-end adcrush run with actual spend, finding and fixing 4 real bugs (resolution casing, async poll/download missing in canon.py and render.py, download User-Agent 403, unpersisted style choice). Produced publication-quality real output end-to-end (check/canon/breakdown/expand/compile/render/audit/publish/serve all verified live). 100 tests passing. Remaining: the mature/adult style profile still needs explicit user direction; minor cross-block canon-fidelity drift (logo typography) observed as a content-quality note, not a code bug.

Added reference_images support to canon.generate_candidate for real (non-AI) assets, confirmed live with a logo swap. Found 2 new architectural gaps: (1) canon changes don't re-trigger expand_technical, so block text can go stale and contradict new canon images -- no general fix decided yet; (2) render.cycle doesn't copy forward unchanged blocks' renders across revisions. Both worked around manually for this run; corrected output published. 107 tests passing.

SHEET_PROMPT_TEMPLATE's layout is now kind-specific (character/location/object/style-reference) instead of forcing expressions+action-pose onto every canon element; object layout also got a strengthened default proportion-lock (measure from reference aspect ratio, explicit anti-elongation, 'proportion fidelity outranks visual drama'). Found and fixed while building a real YouChews Coffee Chews UGC-vertical campaign using real Drive brand assets. 139 tests passing.

Built canon_video (motion-guide/text-overlay/assembly-guide) + seedance-2.5 support; found and fixed 3 more real bugs via live re-rendering (sketch-mandate for motion-guide, canon-sheet attachment for video, motion-plausibility judged relative to canon facts); delivered a corrected final video after 3 live re-render rounds. Also built a campaign white-paper template (fpdf2, outside this repo) and the Coffee Chews white paper itself. 261 tests passing.

Built and rendered the first real adcrush campaign end-to-end (YouChews Coffee Chews UGC-vertical Reel, 6/6 blocks, rev-002), surfacing two real engine fixes (canon fidelity, expand-batch canon dedup) recorded separately in adcrush-implementation. PDF export committed to research/coffee-chews-ugc-reel/.

run_expand_technical now takes pending_canon_needed (accumulated canon_needed from earlier blocks in the same batch, not yet approved) and instructs the model to reuse an existing pending id for the same recurring subject rather than inventing a duplicate. cmd_expand and adcrush_expand both accumulate+thread this across their loops. Found via a real 6-block UGC campaign where 3 blocks independently invented 3 different 'hands' character ids. 141 tests passing.

youchews-chew-motion-graphics is the one incomplete deliverable. Its canon is already regenerated in the motion-graphics treatment and approved (v2/v3, correctly flat and illustrated), but rev-001's ART is still the photoreal pass and it has no clip. The re-render was stopped by the credit floor after archiving only the guide directory; that archive was moved back so rev-001 is consistent. To finish: top up kie, archive rev-001's art, then render-guide and render-final with --review, render-assembly, keyframes, video-plan, video-loop. About 16 image renders (~160 credits) plus one or more clips (~1,000 each). scratchpad/mg_images.sh does the image half and deliberately stops before video.

kie credit confirmed at 424 via GET /api/v1/chat/credit, so renders are unblocked. Next: coffee-chews-ugc-v2 selfie-rig switch (rewrite pov_operator canon to selfie/talent-on-camera, face_policy unrestricted, regenerate+approve, expand --all, compile rev-004, re-render guides/finals/keyframes/assembly on Sunburst, video-plan, video-loop). Then two new isolated projects sharing the YouChews context, each with its own dashboard URL: (1) product-only motion-graphics sequence, (2) a generalized papercraft style then the same video in it.

Replaced GUIDE_TEMPLATE with a fixed, style-independent annotation harness (sketch mandate, annotation gutter, 7 continuity dimensions, chronology lock, entry/exit continuity, lettering placeholder, checklist) mirroring 29-razones' real guide prompts; style only touches one note. Added assemble_guide_prompt()'s deterministic 3-attempt compaction ladder to stay under kie's 19000-char limit. 135 tests passing. M-E in progress (4 styles + 1 partial done under the OLD template, needs redo); motion-graphics/professional-storyboard/ugc-vertical/ugc/videogame-capture not started.

Execution discipline set by the user: write the plan to disk, break it into SOLID handoffs, perfect it against the simulation harness, and only then execute live. The plan is at docs/plans/captions-audio-and-hooks.md with the handoff breakdown in Part VI and the simulation contract in Part VII. Build order is Stage 1 (keyframes off, held handles plus join trim, draft/final model tiering), Stage 2 (audio layers and intent), Stage 3 (ASS captions plus three substyles per style and a new docs/style-manual.md), Stage 4 (voice-over-safe copy), Stage 5 (ElevenLabs, needs an upstream kie-cli PR), Stage 6 (hooks), Stage 7 (integrator).

Four questions gate Lane 2. (1) Stage 1b: accept a 29s cut for a 30s brief, or reserve held half-second handles at plan time (recommended)? (2) Stage 2: in voice_over mode keep Seedance audio on for sfx and police invented speech with a new code (recommended), or turn audio off and lose sfx? (3) Stage 5: is text-to-speech-multilingual-v2 sufficient, or also wire elevenlabs/text-to-dialogue-v3 (Eleven v3, audio tags, multi-speaker) for the mixed case? (4) Is the truncated sixth observation ('a video with s') superseded by the seven items, or still outstanding?

Block.expanded_canon_hashes + compile.is_block_stale() implemented; cmd_expand/adcrush_expand auto-retarget stale blocks; cmd_compile/adcrush_compile exclude stale blocks and report stale_needs_reexpand. 6 new tests (4 unit + 2 MCP integration). 122 tests passing total. M-D (cross-revision copy-forward) and M-E/M-F not started.

render.cycle() now copies forward an unchanged block's previous-revision render (guide or final) instead of re-rendering, via new compile.previous_revision_id(); a real MCP stdio subprocess smoke test (tests/test_mcp_stdio.py) proves the FastMCP server actually works over real JSON-RPC/stdio transport, not just direct Python calls. 130 tests passing. Only M-E remains, gated on user-authorized real spend for the ~10 unvalidated style profiles.

youchews-chew-motion-graphics rev-001 is off-brief: its canon and finals are photoreal because of the hardcoded-medium bug, so it reads as a product film rather than motion graphics. Plan: reset its canon elements to candidate, re-run the canon script (now medium-neutral and with the corrected brown-and-gold pouch copy), approve, move rev-001's art aside for comparison, then re-render guides, finals, assembly and keyframes and re-run the video loop. Dashboards: 4174 old project, 4175 coffee-chews-ugc-v2, 4176 motion-graphics, 4177 papercraft.
The user's sixth observation arrived truncated as 'a video with s' and was never completed. It must be asked rather than guessed before the design agenda is considered closed.

Two new isolated projects share the YouChews context but nothing else, each its own .mcp-adcrush workspace: youchews-chew-motion-graphics and youchews-chew-papercraft, both from one shared brief -- 15s, 3 x 5s, exactly one group, product only with no people, focused on the chew wrapped and unwrapped plus its taste and its four ingredients. Both were seeded with the same real product photos and are running expand -> compile -> guides -> finals -> video-plan -> assembly -> keyframes -> re-plan -> video-loop. The user asked for each project's dashboard URL when ready.

Live Seedance smoke test verified for both groups; built and live-verified voice/sfx/background_music config, ffmpeg video-assemble (concat + Suno-mixed background music with fades/looping), fixing 3 real API bugs (Suno null model, missing callBackUrl, no-audio-stream mix fallback) only found by running it live. 192 tests passing (up from 168). Delivered a real, verified 30s assembled video with mixed instrumental to the user. Committed as a milestone; user explicitly flagged more polishing is needed (video-side hash-staleness/copy-forward gaps, music-track staleness on duration change, generate_background_music's flat retry loop).

video.py + async_jobs.py + kie.submit_video() + video-plan/video-render CLI + adcrush_video_plan/adcrush_video_render MCP tools, built on branch video-gen after two research passes confirmed real Seedance constraints from kie-cli's own source (15s/clip max for seedance-2-fast, not the assumed 30s; two different reference-image CLI-flag shapes; job-status must poll with the resolved provider model string). 168 tests passing (up from 141).

Caption switch, opened-prop rule and S10 keyframes implemented and simulated (10/10, 439 tests). Next: init the new campaign (same Coffee Chews brief, ugc-vertical, 30s, 9:16), intake -> breakdown -> expand -> canon from zero (generate + approve) -> compile -> render-guide/final --review -> video-plan -> render-assembly -> keyframes -> video-plan -> video-loop (seedance-2.5); dashboard served over http for the new project.

Phase A done: plan in docs/plans/video-self-improvement.md, journal stream 4a1e9708 opened, branch video-self-improvement created. Next: Phase B -- build adcrush-cli/simulation/ (fakes, scenarios, runner, checks) and implement S1..S8 against it, recording each simulation run in the journal.

Phase B done and frozen (tag sim-pass-20260910). Next: Phase D live, gated on the user's go -- S3 spot-check (one B + one G sheet vs 29-razones), S6 calibration (video-review on rev-003 group-2 must flag REFERENCE_BLEED + EXTRA_PERSON_OR_LIMB), then S9 canonical run: expand -> compile (rev-004) -> render-guide/final --review -> video-plan -> render-assembly -> video-plan -> video-loop --max-retries 3 --stop-after render, budget <= 8 Seedance renders + 8 judge calls, human spot-check, dashboard --watch. Follow-ups: split video.py (~1,600 lines), recipes.py, loop.py; second adapter seam in media_review/cli.py.

Phase D paused on kie credit. To resume: top up kie, clear halted in runs/rev-006/video/state.json, then video-loop --revision rev-006 --model seedance-2.5 --max-retries 3 --max-judge-calls 8 --stop-after loop --live --yes; then human spot-check promoted clips, audit, journal, commit. Follow-ups: template version in block hash (template fixes needed manual sheet retirement), reference-map lines dominate prompt length on 30-slot models, video.py/recipes.py/loop.py splits.

Paused on Anthropic API credit (400 credit balance too low). Resume: top up Anthropic, then from campaigns/coffee-chews-ugc-v2: adcrush keyframes --revision rev-002 --live --yes; adcrush video-plan --revision rev-002 --model seedance-2.5; adcrush video-loop --revision rev-002 --model seedance-2.5 --max-retries 3 --max-judge-calls 8 --stop-after loop --live --yes; then human spot-check, audit, journal, commit. Dashboards: 4174 (old project), 4175 (new).

events.summary: Explored 29-razones (journals, narrative model, technical pipeline, prompt-template structure, continuity rules) to reverse-engineer a reusable adcrush design: 5 vectors (narrative_format, canon, style, duration, platform), a gate cycle with an explicit LLM/deterministic boundary, per-block hash-lock invalidation, a generalized read-only viewer, MCP-as-thin-wrapper, and a concrete config schema -- all confirmed item-by-item via a 30-point questionnaire.

Ran 6 rounds of pre-mortem simulation against the M0-M10 milestone chain: Round 1 found major gaps (credentials contradiction, missing schemas); Round 2 found consequences of those fixes (slugification, attachment versioning, check cost, MCP env freshness, a third narrative invalidation scope); Rounds 3-6 (resolved autonomously) found init-vs-ancestor behavior, a cross-cutting JSON error envelope that had been missed entirely, LLM-call retry discipline, and a revision-mixing correctness rule for publish. Plan converged with no blocking open issues.

Built the adcrush CLI at adcrush-cli/ following the reconciled M0-M10 plan: workspace/schemas/corpus (M0-M1), provider-agnostic multimodal LLM adapter with retry (M2), kie-cli subprocess integration (M3, later installed and verified for real), canon gate with sheet templates and hash-based invalidation (M4), breakdown/expand/compile with per-block hash-lock (M5), the render queue with credit-halt and resumability (M6), a generalized viewer forked from 29-razones's real player and verified live in a browser (M7), audit/publish with a revision-mixing correctness rule (M8), an MCP server exposing all 17 commands via the official SDK (M9), and 11 of ~12 style profiles (M10, one deferred pending user direction). Stopped short of any real LLM/image-gen spend pending explicit authorization.

Executed a live end-to-end run against a minimal Cafe Lunar product-shot brief with real credentials, surfacing 4 real implementation bugs invisible to mocked tests: wrong resolution casing (2k vs 2K), canon.generate_candidate and render.cycle both assuming synchronous image generation when kie's API is async (fixed with proper job-status polling and centralized download), a 403 from the kie CDN rejecting Python's default User-Agent (fixed with a shared kie.download() helper), and compile's --style flag not being persisted (fixed to auto-save). The full corrected pipeline then ran successfully end-to-end, including a real canon-discovery loop-back (expand_technical found 2 new needed elements mid-run) and a real viewer verification in a browser. Test suite grew from 91 to 100 passing tests.

The user spotted a real continuity defect by eye (cup color/logo shape/typography differed across the 3 live-rendered finals despite sharing one canon reference). Root-caused to render.cycle() never resolving block.canon_refs to their approved sheet_path and attaching them as --image references -- it only ever attached the guide PNG, so the model only ever read a text description of the approved cup/table/window and improvised a plausible-but-different one each time. Fixed by adding a canon registry parameter to render.cycle(), attaching every approved canon_ref's sheet for both guide and final phases, and fixing job-status polling to use the correct image-to-image model variant. Added 5 regression tests. Confirmed with a real, user-authorized re-render: cleared the 3 stale outputs, re-rendered guide then final for all 3 blocks, and all three now show the same navy mug and logo. Re-published the corrected revision.

User supplied a real external logo asset (SVG) and asked to swap it into the demo's canon, replacing the AI-imagined brand mark. Added reference_images support to canon.generate_candidate (image-to-image conditioning, hash includes reference images, correct poll model). Confirmed with a real regeneration: the exact logo transferred faithfully. Recompiling correctly invalidated the blocks referencing the changed canon element, but the resulting render was wrong -- root-caused to blocks' own cached expand_technical text still describing the OLD branding, contradicting the new canon reference image the render correctly attached. Worked around by manually editing the stale text and recompiling; flagged as an unresolved architectural gap (canon changes invalidate compile/render but never re-trigger expand_technical). Also found unchanged blocks aren't copied forward across revisions, requiring a manual copy. Corrected revision rendered and published successfully.

Completed M-A (review command), M-B (adcrush_serve MCP tool), and M-C (automatic re-expand on canon change via is_block_stale + expanded_canon_hashes) from the post-run SOLID-handoff remediation plan; 122 tests passing (up from 116). M-D, M-E, M-F remain.

Completed M-D (cross-revision copy-forward for unchanged blocks) and M-F (real MCP stdio client/transport smoke test) from the post-run SOLID-handoff remediation plan; 130 tests passing (up from 122). Only M-E (real per-style spend validation) remains, explicitly gated on future user authorization.

Redesigned adcrush's guide-prompt template to match 29-razones' proven universal annotation harness (style-independent structure, style touches only one note), plus a deterministic 3-attempt 19000-char retry ladder. 135 tests passing (up from 130). M-E (per-style visual validation) is in progress -- 4 styles done, 1 partial -- but all under the pre-redesign template and needs re-running.

Fixed a real canon-sheet fidelity bug found while building a real YouChews Coffee Chews UGC-vertical ad campaign: the sheet-generation template forced character-style expressions/action-pose instructions onto logos and products, causing distortion. Split into kind-aware layouts (character/location/object/style-reference) as the new engine default, plus a strengthened proportion-lock for object canon. 139 tests passing (up from 135).

Fixed a real engine gap found mid-build: run_expand_technical processed each block statelessly, letting 3 separate blocks in the same batch each invent a different id for what should have been one recurring 'talent hands' canon character. Added pending_canon_needed batch cross-talk so the model reuses an existing pending id instead of duplicating it. 141 tests passing (up from 139).

First real (non-demo) adcrush campaign built end-to-end: a 30s/9:16 UGC-vertical Reel for youchews.com Coffee Chews, using real Drive brand assets and Facebook Ad Library competitive research. All 6 blocks compiled and rendered cleanly in rev-002; a compact PDF export is committed to research/coffee-chews-ugc-reel/.

Built the image-to-video lane (M-video): new video.py clusters compiled blocks into Seedance-sized groups, assembles prompts, selects priority-ordered reference images, and submits/polls via kie-cli's video subcommand. New CLI (video-plan/video-render) and MCP tools (19->21). Validated against real Coffee Chews production data. 168 tests passing (up from 141).

2026-09-08/09: real live Seedance smoke test confirmed the job-status polling fix works end-to-end; then built voice/sfx/background_music config, ffmpeg video-assemble, and real Suno integration -- fixing 3 live-only bugs (null model, missing callBackUrl, no-audio-stream mix filter) -- and delivered a real 30s assembled video with mixed instrumental. 192 tests passing (up from 168). Milestone committed with known rough edges (no video-side hash-staleness detection or copy-forward, no music-track staleness check) explicitly called out for follow-up.

2026-09-09: added seedance-2.5 support (sibling kie-api-python repo) and canon_video -- a second, video-stage canon registry (motion-guide/text-overlay/assembly-guide) discovered via a new run_video_canon_discovery LLM pass, with blocked_on_video_canon cross-checking. Three real bugs found via live re-rendering and fixed in sequence: a photoreal motion-guide causing hand/jewelry discontinuity (fixed by reusing the guide-image sketch-mandate discipline), a missing canon-sheet-attachment gap causing wrong product texture (the same bug class as the earlier image-side 'Fifth bug', just never fixed on video), and a physically implausible one-handed unwrap motion (fixed via a motion-plausibility check judged relative to the canon's own established facts, per the user's explicit correction). Separately built a non-technical, platform-agnostic creative-process white paper for the Coffee Chews campaign plus a reusable PDF template/README at campaigns/white-papers/. 261 tests passing (up from 168).

2026-09-09: opened the adcrush-self-improvement lane -- referential imprinted sheets, 15s EDL prompts, vision judge + additive retry recipes, JSON ledger + live dashboard -- as an approved, simulation-first plan (Phases A-D) on branch video-self-improvement.
2026-09-10: Phase B of the adcrush self-improvement lane closed -- full offline simulation passes (10/10 scenarios), 420 tests green, tagged sim-pass-20260910; live Phase D pending user go.
2026-09-10: first live self-improvement run -- judge calibrated, sheets and finals judged/promoted, one video group promoted, second group's retry paused on kie credit.
2026-09-10: user review of the first live run -> captions burned in for UGC, opened-prop rule, and S10 keyframe expansion added; simulation green; new isolated campaign starts.
2026-09-10: new isolated campaign reaches finals + edit sheets with the double-wrap and caption problems resolved; keyframes/video loop wait on Anthropic credit.
2026-09-10: adcrush renders on GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; kie-cli main carries the four new slugs; prompt language simplified; 447 tests and simulation 10/10; kie credit restored to 424.
2026-09-10: rev-004 selfie pass promoted 12/12 sheets on GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; two new YouChews projects seeded from the same brief in motion-graphics and papercraft.

2026-09-10: coffee-chews-ugc-v2 group-1 passed the judge first try with the selfie rig and burned-in captions; the canon grammar's hardcoded 'photoreal' was found restyling a motion-graphics campaign.
2026-09-10: session ends with kie credit exhausted at 64. Two projects complete with promoted clips, the motion-graphics spot awaits a re-render on its restyled canon.
2026-09-10: review of the three delivered spots turns into a design agenda; measured costs show the retry ladder, not the model, is the dominant cost.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 planned -- deterministic ASS captions, ElevenLabs narration with audio-intent classification, hooks as a contract, keyframes off, join trim and model tiering.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 plan locked with decisions, SOLID handoffs and an eleven-scenario simulation contract to pass before any live spend.

documents.description: Record of the first real, non-demo adcrush campaign: a 30s/9:16 UGC-vertical ad for youchews.com Coffee Chews, built with real Drive brand assets and Facebook Ad Library competitive research. Documents where the deliverable lives.
documents.raw:

# Goal

Build the first real (non-demo, non-`29-razones`, non-Cafe-Lunar-test)
adcrush campaign: a 30-second, 9:16 UGC-vertical Reel ad for
`youchews.com`'s Coffee Chews, and record where the resulting deliverable
lives so it stays discoverable outside the raw project working directory.

# Task Contract

- Intended outcome: a compiled, fully rendered 6-block ad (guide + final
  for every block), using real YouChews brand assets (not AI-imagined),
  compliant with the brand's own Voice & Compliance Guide, and a durable
  research record of the exercise.
- Observable success criteria: all 6 blocks compiled and rendered without
  a real (non-recoverable) error; the deliverable is viewable via the
  adcrush viewer; a representative export exists somewhere version-controlled.
- Constraints and non-goals: no real spend without explicit `--live --yes`
  confirmation at each step (project-wide standing rule); no unverified
  compliance claims in copy; this journal documents the campaign, not the
  adcrush engine itself (see `adcrush-implementation` for the engine-level
  fixes this build surfaced).
- Open questions and assumptions: M-E (broader per-style validation) and
  further creative iteration on this specific campaign are both open,
  future work, not part of this record.

# Execution Boundaries

- Authorized scope: build one real campaign end-to-end using the existing
  adcrush CLI/library surface; fix genuine engine defects found along the
  way (recorded in `adcrush-implementation`, not duplicated here);
  research competitive ad creative via a newly vetted third-party MCP.
- Affected interfaces: none beyond what's already recorded in
  `adcrush-implementation`'s corresponding entries (canon sheet fidelity,
  expand-batch canon deduplication).
- Out of scope: further copy iteration, additional style variants for this
  same campaign, actual ad-platform publishing.

# Handoff Topology

Single handoff — one cohesive campaign build, one owner (this session),
no cross-team composition needed.

# Existing Approaches

- Followed the same real-spend discipline established for the Cafe Lunar
  demo and the M-E style-validation batch: dry-run by default, explicit
  `--live --yes` (or the MCP `live=true` equivalent) for every cost-bearing
  step, streamed images back to the user as each one completed.
- Brand assets sourced for real, not invented: Hector Carmona's shared
  Google Drive folder ("YouChews Intelligence"), found via a Gmail search
  and read through the newly connected Google Drive MCP connector — the
  official gold-tile logo, isolated wrapped/unwrapped chew renders, and the
  retail bag front, used as `reference_images` for canon generation.
- Competitive research: installed and code-reviewed
  `facebook-ads-library-mcp` (github.com/RamsesAguirre777/facebook-ads-library-mcp,
  MIT, 234 stars, single 288-line file, no unsafe patterns) before use, per
  the user's explicit "check if it's safe first" instruction. Its headless
  scraper turned out to be blocked by a Facebook bot-detection interstitial
  it can't click through, so the actual research was done with the
  session's own interactive browser instead — still valuable, since it
  surfaced the closest real analog (SuperBeets Heart Chews' emoji-bullet,
  urgency/authority-driven ad pattern) and confirmed the brand's own
  Coffee Chews ads were already running and gave real creative DNA to
  match, rather than inventing an untested "viral meme" tone.
- Brand Voice & Compliance Guide and Customer Voice & Objections docs (also
  from the Drive folder) directly shaped the script: no onset-time
  promises, no "gummy," no unverified ingredient percentages, no
  competitor names by name, and — critically — no invented cross-section
  ingredient visual, after the Customer Voice doc flagged exactly that kind
  of ad-vs-product mismatch as the brand's #1 real complaint pattern.

# Planned Proof

- Deterministic checks: adcrush's own `compile`/`verify_structure` gate
  (unchanged, pre-existing).
- Integration checks: full real render of all 6 blocks, visually reviewed
  block by block as each image completed.
- Remaining judgment: creative quality of the result is a subjective human
  call, not something this record certifies as "good enough to ship" —
  only that the pipeline produced a complete, on-brand, compliant set.

# Status

- [ ] Planned
- [ ] In progress
- [x] Complete (this build; further iteration is separate future work)

# Work Log

1. Pulled real brand assets from `youchews.com` directly (logo SVGs,
   product gallery images) before Drive access existed.
2. User connected Google Drive; found Hector's "YouChews Intelligence"
   folder via Gmail search, pulled the official logo, wrapped/unwrapped

3. Vetted and installed `facebook-ads-library-mcp`; its own scraper was

4. Drafted and iterated the script through several rounds: an initial
   claymation "viral" concept, then a UGC-vertical pivot once real Ad
   Library data showed trust/authority/specificity outperforming comedy
   in this exact category, then a copy rewrite mirroring SuperBeets' and

5. Built the adcrush project at
