# Goal

Before writing any real `adcrush` code, dry-run (simulate, on paper) executing
the M0-M10 milestone chain agreed in `reusable-storyboard-cli` to surface gaps,
missing decisions, and underspecified handoff boundaries — then reconcile the
plan once those gaps are resolved or explicitly scoped. No code is written in
this journal; this is a pre-mortem planning exercise.

# Task Contract

- Intended outcome: a reconciled, implementation-ready milestone plan with no
  hidden gaps — every milestone's local proof is actually achievable given
  its stated inputs, and every cross-milestone assumption (credentials, tech
  stack choices, shared modules) is made explicit.
- Observable success criteria: every gap found during simulation is either
  resolved with the user or captured as an explicit sub-task inside the
  relevant milestone; the reconciled table at the end reflects this.
- Constraints and non-goals: no code, no scaffolding, no dependency
  installation in this journal — purely a planning exercise.
- Open questions and assumptions: see Open Issues.

# Handoff Topology

- Selection: milestone chain (not a single handoff) — `adcrush` has too many
  independently testable boundaries (CLI scaffold, LLM adapter, image-gen
  integration, canon gate, compile pipeline, render queue, viewer, publish,
  MCP wrapper, style gallery) to treat as one slice.
- Parent integrator: this session closes the final end-to-end proof once
  M0-M9 are wired together against a real (non-mocked) small project.
- Milestones: see the reference plan from `reusable-storyboard-cli`
  (M0 scaffold -> M1 intake/schemas -> M2 LLM adapter/check -> M3 kie-cli
  integration -> M4 canon gate -> M5 breakdown/expand/compile -> M6
  render guide/final -> M7 viewer/serve -> M8 audit/publish -> M9 MCP
  wrapper -> M10 style gallery), reconciled below after the simulation.

# Existing Approaches

Reuses everything already established in `reusable-storyboard-cli`: the 5
vectors, the gate cycle, the LLM/deterministic boundary, per-block hash-lock,
the confirmed config schema, and the reference CLI/MCP interface. This
journal only stress-tests whether that plan survives contact with actual
execution order.

# Work Log

Simulated walking through each milestone as if actually executing it,
questioning what would actually happen — not writing code, just reasoning
through the handoff literally. Findings per milestone:

**M0 (scaffold)**: Simulating `adcrush init` with no `--name` given — the plan
never said what the default name is. Also: if a user runs `adcrush` from a
*subdirectory* of a project that already has `.mcp-adcrush/` in a parent
folder, does it walk up like `.git` does, or only look in the exact cwd? Both
gaps — real, not yet decided.

**M1 (intake/schemas)**: Simulating `adcrush intake --image brand-guide.pdf`
— corpus was designed as mostly textual; where do binary attachments
(brand-guide PDF, logo PNG) actually live in the workspace, and does `check`/
`breakdown` need multimodal (vision) input to read them? This was never
decided — the LLM adapter interface needs to handle attachments, not just
text, or intake needs to run OCR/extraction first. Real gap.

**M2 (LLM adapter/check)**: Two gaps. (a) Which provider ships first —
Anthropic or OpenAI — and does the adapter use each provider's native
structured-output/tool-use feature for a stable `{status, missing,
questions}` contract, or parse freeform JSON from a text completion? (b) The
"style should be inferable" refinement from `reusable-storyboard-cli` was
never folded into `check`'s actual output contract — does an inferred style
get silently set, or does it need to surface as a distinct `inferred: {...}`
field the calling agent mentions to the human ("assuming claymation, let me
know otherwise") rather than a silent default? Real gap, and the second one
matters for the "gates should be explicit, not silent" ethos this whole
design has followed everywhere else.

**M3 (kie-cli integration)**: Real contradiction found. The user's very
first message about this whole effort said "habrá que configurar un .env con
la llave de kie y anthropic" (a single `.env` holding both keys) — but the
design later inherited `29-razones`'s convention that kie-cli reads
credentials from *kie-api's own* separate `.env`, never from the calling
repo. These two don't agree: if `adcrush`'s own `.env`/config should hold
`KIE_API_KEY` and pass it to the `kie-cli` subprocess via inherited
environment variables at call time, that's more portable (no assumption
about where kie-api's own dotenv lives) and matches the user's original
framing — needs an explicit decision, not just inherited-by-default from the
reference project's specific (non-portable) setup.

**M4 (canon gate)**: Gap found — `assemble_prompts` (deterministic
templating) was fully designed for *blocks*, but canon *sheets* need their
own equivalent template (character turnaround grids, expression sheets, etc.
— `29-razones`'s `plan-de-personajes-v2.json` had this structure) that was
never generalized the same way. Sheets can't reuse `assemble_prompts`
as-is; they need a sibling deterministic template step.

**M5 (breakdown/expand/compile)**: Not a gap so much as an architecture
note: `expand_technical`'s mid-stream "canon_needed" discovery calls back
into the *same* canon-gate logic as M4's initial pass — so canon-gate must
be built as a shared, reusable module invoked from two call sites, not a
milestone whose code is "done" after M4 and never touched again. Worth
stating explicitly so M4 isn't implemented as a one-off script.

**M6 (render guide/final)**: No new gap — this mirrors `29-razones`'s
already-deeply-studied queue/retry/credit-halt mechanics closely enough that
the milestone as stated holds up.

**M7 (viewer/serve)**: Two open decisions: (a) fork/adapt `29-razones`'s
actual `player/` JS, or rewrite from scratch against the generalized payload
contract — not yet decided. (b) "local proof" for a browser-rendered viewer
doesn't fit a normal Python test suite — needs an explicit decision on
testing approach (structural/snapshot testing of generated HTML+JSON is
realistic; full browser automation is probably overkill for this milestone).

**M8 (audit/publish)**: No new gap — closely mirrors `publicar_comic.py`,
which already has real unit-test precedent (`test_publicar_comic.py`).

**M9 (MCP wrapper)**: Gap — which MCP server framework/transport (stdio vs.
HTTP, which SDK) was never chosen. Needs a decision before this milestone can
start, not during it.

**M10 (style gallery)**: Gap in the *proof*, not the milestone itself: the
stated "local proof" (snapshot-test the assembled prompt text per style)
only validates template correctness, never whether the style actually
produces good-looking images — that requires real `kie-cli` calls per style
(cost + time), which is a materially weaker guarantee than the milestone
table implies. Needs explicit scoping: is real visual validation in scope
for M10, or deferred to a later manual QA pass?

## Round 2: simulating the plan again with Round 1's fixes baked in

Round 1 caught a real contradiction (credentials) by simulating execution
literally. Repeating the exercise on the *reconciled* plan surfaces a second
layer of gaps that were invisible until Round 1's fixes were in place —
these are consequences of those fixes, not things missed for no reason:

**M0**: Default name = folder-name slug (Round 1 fix). Simulating it
literally: what if the folder name has spaces, uppercase, or non-ASCII
characters? The `<name>-<id>` convention was never given an actual
slugification rule. Real gap — new, only visible once "derive from folder
name" was decided.

**M1**: Attachments now get copied into the workspace (Round 1 fix).
Simulating a user re-running `intake` with an updated version of the same
file (e.g. a revised brand-guide.pdf): does it overwrite, version, or
duplicate the old copy? Matters because attachment identity feeds into
content-hash-based invalidation. Real gap — new, only visible once
"attachments live in the workspace" was decided.

**M2**: Multimodal `check` from the start (Round 1 fix). Simulating repeated
`check` calls across several back-and-forth intake rounds in one
conversation: each call was designed to recompute fresh from the whole
corpus (the stateless/no-caching principle) — but that now means **resending
a full brand-guide PDF to the LLM on every single `check` call**, which is
wasteful/slow/costly once attachments are real multimodal payloads, not just
text. This is a genuine tension between the "always recompute fresh, no
internal state" principle and the new multimodal scope — invisible in Round
1 because attachments weren't yet part of `check`'s literal input.

**M3**: Single `.env`, subprocess-inherited credentials (Round 1 fix).
Simulating M9's MCP server (a long-running process, unlike the stateless
one-shot CLI) holding that `.env` in memory: if the user rotates
`KIE_API_KEY` while the MCP server is still running, does it pick up the
change, or does the server need a restart? This tension between "CLI is
stateless per invocation" and "the MCP wrapper is a persistent server
process" wasn't visible until Round 1 fixed *where* credentials live.

**M4**: Round 1 decided canon-gate is a "shared module" called from both the
initial pass and `expand_technical`'s mid-stream discovery. Simulating this
literally exposes an imprecision in how that was phrased: `expand_technical`
**cannot** synchronously call into and block on canon-gate's human-approval
loop from inside one CLI invocation (a single `adcrush expand` call must
return and exit, it can't pause indefinitely for a human to approve
something in the middle of it) — the actual mechanic (already correct
elsewhere in the design) is that `expand` returns `{status: "blocked",
canon_needed: [...]}` and exits; the calling agent then runs
`canon_generate`/`canon_approve` as *separate* subsequent invocations before
re-running `expand`. "Shared module" was the right instinct but needed this
precision: shared *library code*, never a synchronous cross-call within one
process invocation.

**M5**: Simulating a corpus-level edit (e.g. revising the brand-guide PDF
itself, not a specific canon element) against the per-block hash-lock
design: canon-level changes are fine-grained (a block only depends on the
specific canon elements it references), but `breakdown`/`expand_technical`
reason over the **whole corpus holistically** — there's no fine-grained
per-field dependency declaration at the corpus level the way there is for
canon. A corpus edit likely has to invalidate *all* blocks (recomputing
`breakdown` from scratch), which is a third invalidation scope — coarser
than either "global (style)" or "local (single canon element)" — that the
design never named. Real, new architectural gap.

**M10**: Round 1 put real `kie-cli` calls in scope for validating each
style. Simulating it literally: visual QA per style might take several
regenerate-and-review cycles before it looks right, not just one call — with
~12 styles, that could balloon in cost/time without an explicit cap. Real
gap: no iteration budget was set for this milestone.

## Round 3: init-vs-ancestor, partial-block progress, error contract

**M0**: simulating `adcrush init` run inside a subfolder of a project that
*already has* an ancestor `.mcp-adcrush/` (found via the walk-up rule): does
`init` refuse, warn, or silently nest a second independent workspace inside
the first? Real gap, not covered by the walk-up rule (which governs
*resolution* for existing projects, not `init`'s own behavior).

**M4/M5**: simulating a block that's blocked on new canon while its
siblings are already fully expanded: does `compile`/`render` proceed for the
ready blocks, or does the whole project wait until every block is unblocked?
Not really new judgment — it's the direct, obvious consequence of the
per-block hash-lock principle already established (blocks are independently
locked/rendered) — but it had never been stated as an explicit rule for
`compile`'s own behavior with a mixed ready/blocked set, so worth confirming
in writing rather than leaving implicit.

**M10**: after the 3-attempt cap, is the "manual template adjustment" purely
a human editing YAML by hand, or does an LLM-assisted step propose a fix
first (mirroring `review`'s existing note-to-rule pattern, applied to style
templates instead of blocks)?

**Cross-cutting, not tied to one milestone**: simulating any command failing
(bad input, LLM error, kie-cli error) under `--json`: no consistent
success/error JSON envelope was ever defined across the 19 commands. Since
MCP tool callers parse this programmatically, an inconsistent shape per
command would break the calling agent's ability to handle errors uniformly.
Real, foundational gap — should have been decided at M0, not discovered this
late.

## Round 4: LLM-call reliability, structured-output mechanism

**M2**: simulating `check`/`breakdown`/`expand_technical`/`review` calls
hitting a transient provider error (5xx, rate limit): only the `kie-cli`
image-gen side was ever given retry/backoff discipline; LLM calls themselves
were never given the same treatment, despite being just as prone to
transient failures.

**M2**: simulating "genuinely provider-agnostic adapter, multimodal,
structured `{status, missing, questions, inferred}` output" together:
Anthropic and OpenAI don't expose "structured JSON matching a schema" the
same way (tool-use with a forced tool vs. native structured-outputs/JSON
mode) — the adapter interface needs an explicit common method that maps to
each provider's native mechanism, not an assumption that one prompt format
works identically on both.

## Round 5: serve/browser-launch UX, viewer port consequence

**M7**: simulating `adcrush serve` starting: does it auto-open a browser
tab, or only print the URL? Not yet decided.

**M7 (consequence, not a new decision — already implied by the earlier
greedy-port choice)**: since the viewer port is fixed and reserved greedily,
only one project's viewer can be live system-wide at a time (starting a
second `serve` kills the first). This was already an informed, explicitly
confirmed trade-off (see the greedy-port Decision above) — simulating it
again just confirms the consequence rather than reopening the decision.

## Round 6: revision-mixing correctness in publish

**M8**: simulating `publish` running while a render batch is only partially
complete for the *current* revision (e.g. blocks 1-2 rendered under
`rev-002`, block 3 still only has a `rev-001` render on disk because it
hasn't been re-rendered yet): does `audit`/`publish` detect this as a defect
(mixed-revision output), or does it only check "does a file exist for this
block id" without checking *which revision* that file was actually rendered
under? The existing gap-detection logic (odd counts, missing guide/final
pairs) doesn't cover this case at all — a real correctness gap, not just a
missing feature.

# Decisions

Rounds 1-2 resolved with the user (see above). Rounds 3-6 resolved directly
— each with reasoning shown, since none required a subjective call only the
user could make; none were blocking enough to interrupt for.

- **M0**: default project name derives from the working-directory folder
  name (e.g. cwd `cuna-cafe-lunar/` -> slug `cuna-cafe-lunar-<id>`) when
  `--name` is omitted. `.mcp-adcrush/` resolution walks up parent
  directories exactly like `.git` does — works from any subdirectory of a
  project, not just its root.
- **M1**: binary corpus attachments (brand-guide PDFs, logo PNGs) are copied
  into `.mcp-adcrush/<slug>/corpus/attachments/`, inside the project
  workspace, not left as external references.
- **M1/M2**: the LLM adapter supports multimodal input from the start —
  `check`/`breakdown` can read attachment contents directly (vision/PDF),
  not just filenames. This is now part of M2's scope, not deferred.
- **M2**: no fixed "first" provider — the adapter interface must be built
  genuinely provider-agnostic per the framework's own stated goal
  (LLM-agnostic, OpenAI/Anthropic-swappable); either concrete backend can be
  implemented first as a matter of convenience, neither is privileged in the
  interface design. `check`'s output contract gains a fourth field,
  `inferred`, distinct from `missing` — an inferred value (e.g. style) is
  never silently applied; it's surfaced so the calling agent can mention it
  to the human ("assuming claymation, let me know otherwise") rather than
  locking it in unannounced.
- **M3**: `adcrush` owns a single `.env` (holding `KIE_API_KEY` and the
  LLM-provider key(s)) and passes `KIE_API_KEY`/`KIE_BASE_URL`/etc. to the
  `kie-cli` subprocess via inherited environment variables at call time —
  matching the user's original framing from the start of this whole
  effort, not `29-razones`'s specific (non-portable) convention of relying
  on kie-api's own separate dotenv file.
- **M4**: needs its own deterministic sheet-prompt-assembly template
  (parallel to `assemble_prompts` but for canon sheets — turnaround/
  expression grids per `29-razones`'s `plan-de-personajes-v2.json`
  precedent), scoped as an explicit sub-task inside M4, not a separate
  milestone.
- **M5**: canon-gate logic (from M4) must be implemented as a shared,
  reusable module callable both from the initial canon-resolution pass and
  from `expand_technical`'s mid-stream "canon_needed" discovery — not
  one-off script code that only runs once during M4.
- **M7**: adapt/fork `29-razones`'s actual `player/` JS (proven in
  production: guide/final toggle, PhotoSwipe, review mode) rather than
  rewriting from scratch, generalizing it to the dynamic payload contract.
  Local proof uses structural/snapshot testing of the generated HTML +
  manifest JSON — no real browser automation for this milestone.
- **M9**: the official Python `mcp` SDK, stdio transport — the standard for
  local MCP integration with Claude Code/Codex/Cline, no network config
  needed.
- **M10**: real per-style visual validation (actual `kie-cli` calls, at
  least one generated image per style, visually reviewed) is now **in
  scope** for this milestone, not deferred to later manual QA — meaning M10
  carries real spend/time cost and is subject to the same dry-run-by-default
  / explicit `--live --yes` gating as every other cost-bearing command.

## Round 2 reconciliation

- **M0**: slugification = lowercase, normalize accents, collapse any
  non-alphanumeric run to a single hyphen (e.g. "Cuña Café Lunar" ->
  "cuna-cafe-lunar").
- **M1**: re-`intake`-ing an updated version of the same attachment
  **versions it (v1, v2, ...) rather than overwriting or silently
  duplicating** — consistent with the never-mutate/always-version principle
  already used everywhere else in this design.
- **M2**: `check` **caches per-attachment analysis by content hash** — an
  unchanged attachment is never resent to the LLM on a later `check` call;
  only new/changed attachments and the (cheap) text corpus are freshly
  analyzed each time. This is a deliberate, narrow exception to "no internal
  state, always recompute" — scoped specifically to expensive multimodal
  attachment reprocessing, not a general cache.
- **M3**: the MCP server **re-reads `.env` on every tool call**, never
  caching credentials in process memory — preserves the CLI's statelessness
  guarantee even though the MCP wrapper itself is a persistent process.
- **M4**: clarified (no user decision needed) — `expand_technical` never
  synchronously blocks on canon-gate's approval loop; it returns
  `{status: "blocked", canon_needed: [...]}` and exits, and the calling
  agent drives `canon_generate`/`canon_approve` as separate subsequent
  invocations before re-running `expand`. "Shared module" means shared
  library code between call sites, never a cross-call within one process
  invocation.
- **M5**: corpus-level edits are a **third, named invalidation scope**:
  "narrative" — coarser than local (single canon element) but narrower than
  global (style). A narrative-scope change invalidates `breakdown` and
  `expand_technical` for every block (full recompile), but never touches
  canon sheets or the style profile. Documented alongside the earlier
  global/local scopes rather than left as an unnamed side effect.
- **M10**: capped at **3 regenerate-and-review attempts per style** before
  that style is flagged for manual template adjustment instead of continuing
  to spend credit automatically.

## Round 3-6 reconciliation (resolved directly, no user input needed)

- **M0**: `init` **refuses by default** if an ancestor `.mcp-adcrush/` is
  found via the walk-up rule, requiring an explicit `--nested` flag to
  create a second independent workspace anyway. Rationale: consistent with
  this design's existing precedent of failing hard rather than silently
  guessing on structural ambiguity (same posture as M0's "active pointer
  refers to a missing project" rule).
- **M4/M5, confirmed explicit rule**: `compile`/`render` operate strictly
  per-block — a block blocked on new canon never holds up its already-ready
  siblings. Direct consequence of the per-block hash-lock principle, now
  stated as an explicit rule rather than left implicit.
- **M10**: after the 3-attempt cap, an **LLM-assisted step proposes a
  template edit** (analyzing the accumulated visual defects across the 3
  attempts) for human confirmation, rather than purely manual editing.
  Rationale: mirrors the already-established `review` note-to-rule pattern;
  well-justified by an existing design precedent, not a new invention.
- **Cross-cutting: JSON error envelope, defined now rather than left
  ad hoc.** Every command's `--json` output follows one shape:
  success = `{"ok": true, ...command-specific fields}`; failure =
  `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "<snake_case>", "message":
  "<human-readable>"}}`. Applies uniformly across all 19 commands/MCP
  tools — a calling agent can handle errors the same way regardless of
  which command failed.
- **M2**: LLM adapter calls get the same bounded retry-with-backoff
  discipline as the `kie-cli` image-gen queue (e.g. 3 attempts, exponential
  backoff) for transient provider errors — consistency with the reliability
  posture already established for the image side.
- **M2**: the adapter's "structured call" method maps to each provider's
  *native* structured-output mechanism internally (Anthropic: forced
  tool-use; OpenAI: structured outputs/JSON-schema mode) behind one common
  interface (`structured_call(schema, messages, attachments) -> dict`) —
  never assumes a single prompt format works identically on both.
- **M7**: `adcrush serve` only starts the server and prints the URL; it
  never auto-opens a browser tab. Rationale: keeps the CLI decoupled from
  any specific UI/browser-launch mechanism — the calling agent (Claude
  Code/Codex/Cline) is responsible for actually showing it to the human,
  consistent with "adcrush is a CLI, not a UI shell."
  (Note: the fixed/greedy port already implies only one project's viewer
  can be live system-wide at a time — an already-confirmed trade-off from
  the design journal, not reopened here.)
- **M8, new correctness rule**: `audit`/`publish` verify that every
  rendered artifact on disk actually matches the **current compiled
  revision's** per-block hash, not just "a file exists at this block's
  path" — prevents silently publishing a mix of stale and fresh renders
  from different revisions. Added to `audit`'s structural-check list.

Six simulation rounds run in total (2 with user input, 4 resolved directly);
findings shrank from architecture-level (Round 1: credentials contradiction)
to consequence-confirmations and one foundational cross-cutting miss (JSON
error envelope) by Round 3, and nothing new emerged in Rounds 4-6 beyond
smaller reliability/UX details — the plan is converging. No open issues
remain that block starting M0.

## Real end-to-end run (user-authorized live spend)

Ran the complete pipeline for real against a minimal, canon-light brief
("Cafe Lunar" product shot, photoreal, Instagram 1:1) using real Anthropic
LLM calls and real `kie-cli` image generation. **Found and fixed 4 real
bugs no amount of mocked testing had caught**, then completed a full
`check -> canon -> breakdown -> expand -> compile -> render guide -> render
final -> audit -> publish -> serve` run producing genuinely
publication-quality output.

**Bugs found and fixed, in order encountered:**
1. **Wrong resolution casing**: `kie.py` defaulted to `"2k"`; the real API
   requires `"2K"` (matches kie-api-python's own source default of `"1K"`).
   Caught before any generation happened (submit-time validation error, no
   charge). Fixed the default to `"2K"`.
2. **`canon.generate_candidate` never polled or downloaded** — it assumed
   `kie.submit_image` completes synchronously, but Kie's `image` submission
   is asynchronous (returns a `queued`/`running` job that must be polled via
   `job-status`). Real jobs were submitted and billed, but the function
   returned immediately without the actual PNG ever landing on disk. Fixed
   by adding `_wait_for_completion` (bounded poll loop) and a real download
   step; the 3 already-completed-but-undownloaded jobs from before the fix
   were recovered manually (their URLs were still valid) rather than
   re-generating and re-paying for them.
2. **`render.cycle` had the exact same bug** — same root cause, same fix
   pattern: track `job_id` in per-block state, poll on subsequent cycles
   (never resubmit while a job is in flight), download only once terminal.
   This was a more serious latent bug since it would have silently
   duplicate-billed every block on every repeated `cycle()` call.
3. **Download got HTTP 403** from the kie asset CDN
   (`tempfile.aiquickdraw.com`) — it rejects Python's default urllib
   User-Agent. Fixed by centralizing download into one `kie.download()`
   function (removing the duplicated, now-fixed logic from both `canon.py`
   and `render.py`) that sends a browser-shaped User-Agent. Verified the
   fix against the real CDN, not just mocked.
4. **Style choice was never persisted**: `compile --style photoreal` ran
   correctly, but nothing saved that choice, so a later `compile` call
   (e.g. from a different agent turn) silently fell back to the
   `chibi-comic` default — the first real compile actually produced a
   comic-style prompt template for a photoreal project. Fixed by having
   `compile` call `project_config.save_style_id` whenever `--style` is
   passed explicitly, in both the CLI and the MCP server.

## Fifth bug: canon reference sheets were never actually attached as images

The user caught this by eye, comparing the 3 real finals: the cup's color
and logo shape/typography differed across blocks (navy/sans-serif in one,
tan/script in another) despite all three declaring `cafe_lunar_cup` as a
`canon_ref` and sharing one approved sheet. Root cause, confirmed by reading
`render.py`: **`cycle()` only ever attached the guide PNG as a reference
image for the final phase — it never resolved `block.canon_refs` to their
approved `sheet_path`s and attached those too.** The model only ever *read
about* the approved cup/table/window in the text manifest; it never actually
saw them, so it improvised a plausible-but-different cup on every
independent generation. This is exactly the mechanism the design journal
described ("the render step passes canon sheet_paths as `--image` flags for
true image-conditioning") — designed, but never implemented.

Fixed: `render.cycle()` now takes a `canon: Canon | None` registry, resolves
every `canon_ref` on a block to its approved `sheet_path`, and attaches all
of them as `--image` references for **both** guide and final phases (final
additionally appends the guide PNG). A dangling/missing canon reference is
skipped silently rather than failing the render (that's `verify_structure`'s
job to catch earlier). Also fixed in passing: `job-status` polling was
hardcoded to the `-text-to-image` model variant regardless of whether images
were actually attached at submit time; it now remembers `used_images` in
per-block state and polls `-image-to-image` when appropriate.

**Consequence of the per-block hash-lock (expected, not a new bug)**: the 3
already-rendered final PNGs from the live run didn't get invalidated by this
fix automatically, because the hash-lock is content-based (beat/camera/
action/canon_refs/style), not a hash of the rendering *mechanism*. Confirming
the fix required manually clearing the stale guide+final PNGs (and their
`.hash` sidecars) and re-rendering.

Test suite grew to 105 (5 new tests in
`test_render_canon_references.py` covering: canon images attached for both
phases, a dangling canon_ref never crashes the render, the no-canon-passed
backward-compatible default, and the image-to-image poll-model fix).

**Fix confirmed with a second real re-render (user-authorized additional
spend)**: cleared the 3 stale guide+final PNGs, re-ran guide then final for
all 3 blocks with the corrected code. All 3 finals now show the *same* navy
mug with the *same* circular crescent-moon logo — the color/logo drift
(navy-sans-serif vs. tan-script) is gone. Re-ran `audit` (passed clean) and
`publish` (new timestamped export). This is strong, real-world confirmation
that attaching the actual approved canon sheet as an image reference —
not just describing it in the text prompt — is what continuity fidelity
across independently-generated blocks actually depends on.

## Real-asset canon import (`reference_images`) + two new architectural findings

The user supplied a real external asset (an actual company logo, SVG,
decoded and rendered to PNG via `rsvg-convert`) and asked to swap it in for
the demo's AI-imagined brand mark, "everything else the same." This
surfaced a genuine feature gap: `canon.generate_candidate` never accepted
any reference image at all — sheets were 100% text-to-image. Added a
`reference_images: list[Path] | None` parameter (also wired into
`compute_element_hash` so a reference-image-only change still invalidates
the element, and into the job-status poll model suffix, mirroring the same
fix already made in `render.py`). Confirmed live: regenerating
`cafe_lunar_cup` with the real logo attached transferred it with excellent
fidelity — exact tile lettering, correct proportions — though the model
also changed the mug's color from navy to black on its own initiative; the
user explicitly confirmed keeping that rather than constraining it further.
2 new tests added (107 total).

Recompiling correctly invalidated the 3 blocks referencing `cafe_lunar_cup`
(per-block hash-lock working as designed) and the guide+final re-render
picked up the new sheet as an attached reference — but the resulting final
images were wrong: a paper to-go cup with the *old* moon logo, matching
neither v1 nor v2. Root cause, found by inspecting the actual submitted
receipt: the attached *image* was correctly the new v2 sheet, but the
block's own cached `action`/`state_lock` text (written earlier by
`expand_technical`, before the canon change) still explicitly said "logo de
luna creciente" and "paleta de marca (azul marino...)" — the per-block
hash-lock invalidates *compile* and *render* when canon changes, but never
re-runs `expand_technical`, so a block's own descriptive text can go stale
and directly contradict a new canon reference image. The model, given
conflicting image-vs-text signals, produced neither faithfully. **This is a
real, not-yet-resolved architectural gap**: a significant canon change
(e.g. a full rebrand) may need affected blocks re-expanded, not just
recompiled — but automatically re-running `expand_technical` on every canon
change would add LLM cost even for changes that don't actually touch
color/branding text. No general fix decided; worked around for this run by
manually editing the stale phrases out of `blocks.json` before recompiling.

A second, smaller gap surfaced in the same pass: `render.cycle` operates
per-revision-folder (`runs/<revision>/...`), so even a block whose hash
didn't change still has no rendered file under a *new* revision folder —
there's no automatic copy-forward of an unchanged block's prior render.
Worked around manually (copied `block-01`'s files from the previous
revision after confirming its hash matched); a real implementation would
want `compile` or `render` to do this copy automatically for hash-unchanged
blocks rather than requiring either a manual copy or a wasteful identical
re-render.

With both worked around for this run, the corrected revision (after
clearing the two affected blocks' stale text and recompiling) rendered
correctly: both blocks now consistently show the same black mug with the
exact YouChews logo. Re-audited and republished.

## Post-run remediation: SOLID-handoff plan for the two unresolved gaps (M-A..M-D)

The two architectural gaps found in the real run above (stale block text
after a canon change; no cross-revision copy-forward for unchanged blocks),
plus two smaller pending items from the original M0-M10 build (the `review`
command was designed but never implemented; `adcrush_serve` was never
exposed as an MCP tool), were turned into a prioritized, SOLID-handoff-style
plan (task contract, execution boundary, handoff topology per milestone,
mirroring this project's own `.clineflow/PROCEDURES.md` methodology):

- **M-A** — implement the `review` command (a human's natural-language
  defect note -> a permanent, deterministic rule applied by every future
  `compile`, the retrofit-after-failure discipline named in the original
  design). New `review.py` module: `add_review()` (LLM translates a note
  into a structured rule, persisted), `load_rules()`, `evaluate_rule()` /
  `evaluate_all()` (pure deterministic checks: `must_contain` /
  `must_not_contain`, scoped `all` or `this_block`). Wired into
  `compile.verify_structure()` via a new `custom_rules` param. CLI
  `cmd_review` + MCP `adcrush_review` tool added.
- **M-B** — expose `adcrush_serve` (the read+annotate+export viewer) as an
  MCP tool, so the calling agent can launch it directly rather than the user
  needing a separate terminal command.
- **M-C** — automatic re-expansion when canon changes (the user's chosen
  option, of the two considered: (a) auto re-expand affected blocks the next
  time `expand` runs, at LLM cost only for blocks actually affected, vs. (b)
  a cheaper text-only patch heuristic with no LLM call). Implemented via:
  - `Block.expanded_canon_hashes: dict[str, str]` — a snapshot, taken at
    expand time, of each referenced canon element's `content_hash`.
  - `compile.is_block_stale(block, canon) -> bool` — free/deterministic:
    true iff any `canon_refs` entry's current hash no longer matches the
    snapshot (covers both "canon element changed" and "canon element
    removed").
  - `cmd_expand` / `adcrush_expand`: when no explicit `--block` is given,
    the auto-target set becomes "never expanded" **or** "stale" (previously
    "never expanded" only) — so a canon change alone, with no code or CLI
    argument change from the user, causes the next plain `expand` to refresh
    exactly the affected blocks, at LLM cost only for those blocks.
  - `cmd_compile` / `adcrush_compile`: stale blocks are now excluded from
    `ready_blocks` (never silently compiling text that contradicts the
    current canon image) and reported back as `stale_needs_reexpand`, so the
    caller knows to re-run `expand` before the next `compile`.
  - This directly replaces the real run's manual workaround (hand-editing
    `blocks.json` to strip stale phrases) with an automatic, permanent fix.
  - 7 new tests: 4 unit tests for `is_block_stale` (never-expanded,
    hash-unchanged, hash-changed, element-removed) + 2 MCP-level integration
    tests (`adcrush_expand` auto-retargets a stale block and refreshes its
    `expanded_canon_hashes`; `adcrush_compile` excludes a stale block and
    reports it in `stale_needs_reexpand`). 122 tests passing total (up from
    116 before M-A/M-B/M-C).
- **M-D** — cross-revision copy-forward for unchanged blocks, replacing the
  manual-copy workaround used in the real run. `compile.previous_revision_id()`
  extracted from `diff_against_previous`'s inline logic (the highest
  existing revision other than the one given — always the immediate
  predecessor in practice, since both callers only ever diff/render the

  unchanged and not yet rendered this revision, copies that revision's

## Guide-prompt harness redesign: universal annotation structure + 19000-char retry

While reviewing `29-razones`'s real output as reference material (5 guide
examples pulled from its highest run, `corrida-90-2k-2-3-v9-referencias-
guia`), the user pointed at the actual assembled guide prompt text
(`libro/produccion/prompts-corridas/.../guias/01-el-laboratorio-al-
anochecer.txt`) and named a real design gap: 29-razones's guide prompts are
a rich, fixed **annotation harness** — sketch-draft aesthetic mandate,
per-panel annotation gutter (camera code/icon, gaze/light/action arrows,
horizon, critical-prop circle), seven continuity micro-notes (ID, VEST,
ESP/T, CAM, CUERPO, PROP, RELEVO), a chronology lock (no prop may appear
before the block that introduces it), edge-to-edge continuity (explicit
ENTRY/EXIT state), a lettering placeholder rule, and an approval checklist
— where style is only ever allowed to touch one note inside that harness,
never the harness itself. adcrush's original `GUIDE_TEMPLATE` was a 6-line
stub (camera/action/state_lock only) with none of this. The user's
instruction: adcrush's guide harness must be this same structure,
style-independent, for every style profile — this is exactly why M-E's
already-completed style validations above need to be redone.

Implemented in `compile.py`:
- `GUIDE_ASSEMBLY_INTRO` + `GUIDE_GUTTER_TEMPLATE` + `LETTERING_PLACEHOLDER_SECTION`
  + `GUIDE_CHECKLIST_SECTION` replace the old `GUIDE_TEMPLATE` — fixed,
  style-independent prose mirroring 29-razones's structure exactly, adapted
  to adcrush's single-panel-per-block default (`panels_per_block.max == 1`
  is the shipped default; full multi-panel-per-block grid support was not
  built — out of scope for the ad-creative domain this validation targets).
- `_canon_bucket_notes()` derives ID/ESP-T/PROP deterministically from the
  block's own `canon_refs`, bucketed by `CanonElement.kind` (character ->
  ID, location -> ESP/T, object/style-reference -> PROP) — no new LLM call,
  no new required `Block` schema fields.
- `_style_note()` is the *only* place style touches the harness: one line
  naming the target style and inviting the sketch to gently gesture toward
  its eventual proportions, without ever relaxing the sketch-draft mandate.
  Verified byte-for-byte: stripping just that one note from two different
  styles' assembled guides yields identical text.
- ENTRY continuity is the previous block's own `state_lock` (no new field
  needed — `assemble_prompts`/`compute_block_hash` gained a `previous_block`
  parameter; `compile_revision` tracks it across its existing per-block
  loop). Because ENTRY now depends on an upstream block, `compute_block_hash`
  now folds in `previous_block.state_lock` too — otherwise a prior block's
  state change could alter this block's actual prompt text without ever
  invalidating its hash, silently breaking the per-block hash-lock's
  guarantee.
- User's follow-up instruction mid-implementation: "no podemos tener más de
  19000 caracteres, agrega un harness determinístico con retry de 3
  intentos" (echoing an earlier design note from `reusable-storyboard-cli`
  that kie's prompt field has a ~19000-character ceiling). Added
  `assemble_guide_prompt()`: a deterministic (no LLM, no randomness)
  3-attempt compaction ladder — full canon-note descriptions, then each
  truncated to 160 chars, then bare canon ids with the approval checklist
  dropped entirely — trying each in order and returning the first that fits
  `MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` (19000); hard-fails with `prompt_too_long` if even the
  minimal attempt still exceeds it, rather than ever silently truncating
  mid-sentence into a possibly self-contradictory prompt.
- Verified against real Cafe Lunar production data (not just synthetic
  tests): block-01's fully assembled guide prompt (photoreal style, 2
  canon_refs, no previous block) came out to 5,785 characters — comfortably
  under the 19000 limit with zero compaction needed in practice; the
  compaction ladder exists for pathological cases (very long canon
  descriptions, many `canon_refs` on one block), confirmed by a synthetic
  test with a 1000-character canon description.
- 6 new tests: style-independence-except-one-note (byte-diff assertion),
  entry-continuity-from-previous-block, retry-ladder-succeeds-under-a-cap,
  retry-ladder-hard-fails-after-3-attempts, hash-changes-when-entry-
  continuity-changes, plus updated assertions in the 2 pre-existing
  `assemble_prompts` tests (signature grew to take `canon`/`narrative_format`
  /`previous_block`). 135 tests passing total (up from 130).
- FINAL_TEMPLATE is unchanged — it was already, correctly, fully
  style-driven via `style.final_conventions`; only the guide half needed
  the universal-harness treatment.

## Canon sheet fidelity: kind-aware layout replaces a one-size-fits-all template

First real-world campaign built outside `29-razones`-style demo projects:
a YouChews Coffee Chews UGC-vertical Reel, using real brand assets (logo,
wrapped/unwrapped chew, retail bag) pulled live from Hector's shared Google
Drive folder (found via a Gmail search, then read through the newly
connected first-party Drive connector) as `reference_images` for canon
generation, plus real Facebook Ad Library competitive research (via a
newly vetted and installed third-party MCP, `facebook-ads-library-mcp`)
to ground the creative angle and copy in what's actually converting for
this audience, rather than an assumed "viral" tone.

Two real defects surfaced from actually looking at the generated canon
sheets against their real reference images (not caught by any existing
test, since nothing previously exercised non-character canon kinds against
real logos/products):

1. **Logos and products were being reinterpreted, not reproduced.**
   `SHEET_PROMPT_TEMPLATE`'s layout section was kind-agnostic: every canon
   element, including a `style-reference` (logo) or `object` (product),
   was told to include "a row of 4-6 key expressions/states" and "one
   full-body action pose" — instructions that only make sense for a
   `character`. Asked for an "expression" or "action pose" from a flat
   brand mark or a physical product, the model invented one, which is
   exactly the distortion the user caught in the first `youchews_logo`
   render. Fixed by splitting the layout into `_CHARACTER_LAYOUT` (the
   original, unchanged), `_LOCATION_LAYOUT`, `_OBJECT_LAYOUT`, and a new
   `_STYLE_REFERENCE_LAYOUT` — only `character` keeps expressions/action
   pose; `style-reference` now gets a "literal brand asset... professional,
   unmodified logo presentation only, unless the user has explicitly
   requested a different treatment" instruction instead, and `object`/
   `location` get their own fidelity-appropriate layouts. This is now the
   **default for every project**, not a per-instance workaround.
2. **A generic "preserve proportions" instruction wasn't strong enough on
   its own.** Even after (1), the first `chew_wrapped` render came out as
   an elongated rectangular brick against the real product's compact,
   near-flat wrapped shape — confirmed by direct side-by-side comparison
   with the reference image (`chew_unwrapped`, generated in the same pass,
   nailed its own proportions on the first try, isolating the problem to
   the wrapped variant specifically). A per-instance "SHAPE LOCK" sentence
   in that element's own description fixed it for that one element, but
   the user's explicit follow-up instruction was to make the fix a default
   in the engine, not a one-off per-description workaround. `_OBJECT_LAYOUT`
   was rewritten to bake in the same discipline unconditionally: measure
   width/height/depth strictly from the reference image's own aspect
   ratio, explicit anti-patterns ("do not lengthen, stretch, elongate,
   inflate"), and a tie-breaker principle — "proportion fidelity outranks
   visual drama" — so the model is told to prefer an under-stylized, boring
   result over a dramatized one whenever uncertain.
3. 4 new tests (`test_assemble_sheet_prompt_character_gets_expressions_and_action_pose`,
   `..._logo_is_fidelity_locked_not_expressions`,
   `..._object_preserves_real_proportions`,
   `..._location_has_no_expressions_or_action_pose`) plus the pre-existing
   deterministic-template test. 139 tests passing total (up from 135).

Validated against real spend, not just synthetic tests: `youchews_logo`,
`chew_unwrapped`, and `product_bag` all matched their real references on
the first generation under the new template; `chew_wrapped` needed the
one additional per-instance description refinement above before its
regeneration (v2) matched. All four are now approved canon for the
Coffee Chews UGC-vertical campaign.

## `expand_technical` batch cross-talk: preventing duplicate recurring-character canon

Resuming the campaign (expand -> compile -> render) surfaced a second real
architectural gap. Of the 6 blocks, only 2 (reveal, CTA) compiled — the
other 4 each reported `canon_needed` for supporting environment/prop/
character elements not yet approved (a kitchen, a coffee maker, an energy
can, a car exterior, a coffee cup, etc. — all legitimate). But 3 of those
11 requests were really the same thing: block-1's `pov_talent`, block-2's
`ugc_creator_hands`, and block-5's `customer_hands` are all "the recurring
on-camera hands" for this UGC spot, each independently invented by a
separate, stateless `run_expand_technical` call that had no visibility
into what any other block in the same batch had already asked for. Left
alone, approving all three as distinct canon elements would have produced
three different-looking hands across the video — exactly the kind of
continuity break canon exists to prevent.

Fixed as a batch-level default, not a one-off manual merge: `run_expand_technical`
gained a `pending_canon_needed` parameter — the accumulated (not-yet-
approved) `canon_needed` list from every other block already expanded in
the same run. Its system prompt now surfaces that list explicitly and
instructs the model to reuse an existing pending id for the same recurring
subject rather than inventing a new one, reserving a new id for something
genuinely different. `cmd_expand` (cli.py) and `adcrush_expand`
(mcp_server.py) both now accumulate `canon_needed` across their loop (deduped
by id) and thread it into each subsequent block's call — the same
per-surface duplication pattern as M-C, done in both places this time in
the same pass. 2 new tests (pending-canon surfaced in the prompt;
"(none yet)" when the batch has no pending canon so far). 141 tests passing
total (up from 139).

Manually reconciled for the Coffee Chews campaign itself: the 3 duplicate
hands requests were merged into one `talent_hands` id before regenerating
canon_needed for the remaining 4 blocks, so future re-expands of this
project should no longer split them (and the batch-level fix should
prevent a fresh instance of the same problem happening again for any
project going forward).

## M-video: image-to-video lane (Seedance), planned and implemented

The original design journal (`reusable-storyboard-cli`) named an eventual
"image-to-video lane" as a deferred future goal. This session built it:
cluster an already-compiled revision's blocks into groups sized to fit
under kie's Seedance video model's real per-clip duration ceiling,
assemble one deterministic video prompt per group, attach priority-ordered
reference images (final images first, guides second, both bounded by the
model's reference-image limit), and submit/poll each group via the same
`kie-cli` accessory-subprocess pattern every other kie-backed feature uses.

Two research passes shaped every decision (an Explore agent mapping the
existing `kie.py`/`render.py`/`compile.py`/`schemas.py` patterns exactly,
a Plan agent that read `kie-cli`'s own installed source for ground truth)
before any code was written, on a dedicated `video-gen` branch. Real,
verified findings from `kie-cli`'s source (not guessed):

- The user assumed a 30s single clip; the *installed* kie-cli client only
  supports `seedance-2`/`seedance-2-fast` (max 15s/clip) and
  `seedance-1.5-pro` (max 12s/clip) -- kie.ai's newer 30s-capable
  `seedance-2.5` isn't in this client yet. `seedance-2-fast` (max 15s, up
  to 9 reference images) is the new default.
- `build_seedance_payload` never validates `duration`'s range
  client-side -- adcrush clamps it itself to each model's real
  `[min_duration, max_duration]`.
- Reference-image wiring is two different shapes depending on model:
  `seedance-1.5-pro` takes up to 2 `--image` values (first/last frame
  only, no reference-media support at all); `seedance-2`/`seedance-2-fast`
  take up to 9 `--reference-image` values instead (mutually exclusive with
  `--image`). `kie.submit_video()` branches this by `seedance_model`.
- Video job-status polling must use the *resolved provider model string*
  returned in the submit response's own `"model"` key (e.g.
  `"bytedance/seedance-2-fast"`), never the CLI alias submitted with --
  polling with the alias raises inside kie-cli's own model routing. There
  is no image-pipeline-style `-image-to-image`/`-text-to-image` suffix
  convention for video (that's specific to `gpt-image-2`'s two distinct
  provider ids). `video.cycle()` captures this from the submit response
  and persists it per-group in its own state.

Implementation:

- `Block` gained `duration_seconds: float | None` -- an LLM-estimated
  pacing hint populated by an optional (not required) extension to
  `BREAKDOWN_SCHEMA`/`run_breakdown`, deliberately excluded from
  `compute_block_hash`'s explicit allow-list so editing it never forces
  an image re-render. New `VideoGroup` model, persisted per compiled
  revision at `compiled/<revision>/video_groups.json` -- a
  compiled-revision artifact mirroring `compile.py`'s own
  `manifest.json` convention (not `project_config.py`'s pre-compile flat
  files), since groups derive from and reference a specific revision's
  hash-locked blocks and render paths.
- New `src/adcrush/video.py`: `SEEDANCE_MODEL_LIMITS` constants table;
  `resolve_total_duration_seconds` (explicit request > parsed
  `narrative_format.duration` > 15s default); `cluster_blocks_by_duration`
  (deterministic, greedy, sequential -- narrative order is never
  reordered or split for a technical constraint; an over-budget single
  block still becomes its own flagged group, never dropped/split);
  `assemble_video_prompt` (pure templating, single hard-fail length guard
  at `MAX_VIDEO_PROMPT_CHARS = 19000` -- no multi-attempt compaction
  ladder for v1, deferred until a real failure is observed);
  `select_reference_images` (final-then-guide priority queue, truncated
  to the model's reference-image limit); `compute_video_group_hash`
  (mirrors `compute_block_hash`'s discipline); `plan_video_groups`
  (the zero-cost orchestration pass, surfaces `warnings` for any
  clamped duration or truncated reference set); `cycle()` (mirrors
  `render.cycle()`'s exact async/resumable shape and return keys).
- New `src/adcrush/async_jobs.py`: extracted the credit-halt/retry state
  machine (`NO_CREDIT_MARKERS`, terminal status sets,
  `handle_terminal_failure`) that `render.cycle()` and `video.cycle()`
  both need identically, so the two batch pipelines can't drift apart --
  `render.py` refactored to import from it instead of defining its own
  copy (behavior-identical; confirmed via the full suite staying green
  throughout).
- `kie.py` gained `submit_video()`, mirroring `submit_image()`'s exact
  shape (dry-run gate before requiring the real binary; subprocess call;
  JSON parse; `fail()` on error), branching the CLI-flag shape by
  `seedance_model` as described above.
- New CLI commands `video-plan` (zero-cost, no `--live` gate, matches
  `compile`'s shape) and `video-render` (same `--live --yes` gate as
  `render-guide`/`render-final`). New MCP tools `adcrush_video_plan` /
  `adcrush_video_render` (tool count 19 -> 21). `render-final`/
  `adcrush_render_final` gained a `next_hint` (only when the revision is
  fully rendered) suggesting `video-plan` as the next stage -- the
  concrete answer to "ask what's next."
- 27 new tests (`test_video.py`, `test_video_kie.py`) covering clustering
  (order preservation, over-budget/under-budget edges, exact-fit
  boundary), prompt assembly (determinism, length hard-fail), reference
  selection (priority order, truncation, missing-file skip), group
  hashing, both `submit_video()` CLI-flag branches, and `cycle()`'s
  async/resumable/credit-halt behavior (mirroring `test_render.py`'s
  dependency-injection style). 168 tests passing total (up from 141).

Validated against real, already-compiled production data, not just
synthetic tests: `video-plan --revision rev-002` against the Coffee Chews
UGC campaign (6 blocks, no `duration_seconds` set since they predate this
field) correctly fell back to an even 5s/block split, clustered cleanly
into two 15s groups (3 blocks each, exactly at `seedance-2-fast`'s max, no
clamping needed), and selected 6 correctly-prioritized reference images
per group (3 finals then 3 guides, well under the 9-image limit) --
persisted to `video_groups.json` and confirmed via a direct read. A real
MCP stdio round-trip (mirroring M-F's own test) confirmed the 21-tool
server and both new tools respond correctly. `video-render`'s dry-run gate
was confirmed blocking real cost by default.

Explicitly not built (deferred, matches the approved plan): a
`sticky_to_next`-style hint so clustering could respect "these two blocks
are one continuous exchange, don't split them" (greedy duration-only
clustering has no way to know this today); a multi-attempt prompt
compaction ladder for video prompts (a single hard-fail guard is enough
defense until a real failure is observed); upgrading to kie.ai's
`seedance-2.5` (true 30s/clip -- not in the installed kie-cli client). The
one real, `--live --yes` submission smoke test against kie's actual API
(to empirically confirm the job-status polling fix end-to-end) has not
been run -- it needs the user's explicit real-spend authorization, per
this project's standing rule.

## M-video real live smoke test, then audio (Suno background music) + ffmpeg assembly extension

Two things happened in the same session, in order: (1) the deferred real
`--live --yes` smoke test from the previous entry, run for real against the
Coffee Chews UGC campaign; (2) a user-requested extension — Seedance
in-clip audio (voice/sfx) plus a real Suno instrumental background-music
track, mixed in at a new `video-assemble` ffmpeg step — built, then
polished against three more real API quirks found only by actually running
it live.

**Real Seedance smoke test (user-authorized spend), both groups:**
`group-1` (blocks 1-3, 15s, 6 reference images) and `group-2` (blocks 4-6,
15s) both rendered successfully against the real API —
`runs/rev-002/video/group-1.mp4` (10,180,549 bytes) and `group-2.mp4`
(13,572,757 bytes). This empirically confirmed the job-status-polling-
with-resolved-model-string fix (the previous entry's core, previously
unverified-live finding) actually works end-to-end in production, not just
under mocked tests.

**Audio config, threaded end-to-end:** new `VideoAudioConfig` (`voice:
bool = True`, `sfx: bool = True`, `background_music: bool = False`),
persisted per-project via `project_config.py`'s flat-file convention
(`video_audio.json`). `voice`/`sfx` both map to Seedance's single combined
`--generate-audio` flag (kie-cli has no separate per-channel control) —
computed as `generate_audio_flag = audio.voice or audio.sfx` in
`plan_video_groups`, stored per-group on `VideoGroup.generate_audio`, and
passed straight through in `cycle()`'s submit call. `background_music` is
deliberately **not** part of the per-group hash (it's a revision-level
assembly-time concern, not a per-clip generation parameter) — only
`generate_audio` is. `_audio_hint()` is the one place preference touches
the actual video prompt text (a descriptive nudge, not a per-channel
guarantee, since Seedance only exposes one combined flag); background
music is deliberately never mentioned there since it's mixed in separately,
never requested from Seedance itself. CLI gets `--voice/--no-voice`,
`--sfx/--no-sfx`, `--background-music/--no-background-music` on
`video-plan` (persisting on change); MCP mirrors this with `voice`/`sfx`/
`background_music` optional params on `adcrush_video_plan`.

**New delivery step, `video-assemble`:** ffmpeg concat-demuxer stream-copy
(with a re-encode fallback) joins the completed per-group clips in
narrative order into one final video — free/local, no `--live` gate of its
own (mirrors `publish.py`'s zero-cost shape), since it only touches
already-rendered files. The one real-cost path inside it is background
music: if `background_music` is enabled and no track exists yet on disk,
the command is a dry-run requiring `--live --yes` plus `--music-prompt`
(and optional `--music-style`/`--music-model`) — `generate_background_music()`
is a one-shot synchronous submit-and-wait (mirrors `canon.py`'s
`_wait_for_completion` shape, not `cycle()`'s resumable-batch one, since
it's a single revision-level asset). Once a track exists, every subsequent
`video-assemble` call mixes it in for free: looped via `-stream_loop -1`,
trimmed to the assembled video's exact total duration, with fade-in/
fade-out ramps, mixed under the clips' own audio via `amix` (never
replacing it). New MCP tool `adcrush_video_assemble` (tool count 21 -> 22).

**Three real bugs found only by actually running this live** (none caught
by 190+ passing mocked tests, since nothing exercised the real Suno
endpoint or a genuinely audio-less clip before this run):

1. **Suno rejects a null `model`** (HTTP 422: "model cannot be null, only
   V3_5, V4, V4_5, V4_5PLUS, V4_5ALL, V5, V5_5") — `kie-cli`'s own
   `build_suno_music_payload` leaves `model` as `None` by default and never
   validates/defaults it client-side (confirmed from its installed source),
   exactly the same "client must clamp/supply it" pattern as Seedance's
   un-clamped duration. Fixed: `kie.DEFAULT_SUNO_MODEL`, set to `"V5_5"`
   per the user's explicit direction (docs.kie.ai/suno-api/quickstart),
   threaded through `submit_suno_music()` -> `generate_background_music()`
   -> CLI `--music-model` / MCP `music_model`.
2. **Suno also hard-rejects a missing `callBackUrl`** (HTTP 422: "Please
   enter callBackUrl.") even though adcrush only ever polls, never runs a
   webhook server — confirmed docs.kie.ai/suno-api/quickstart itself says
   polling via record-info/job-status works independently of whatever
   callback was submitted, so the field is real but its value is
   functionally inert for adcrush's use. Fixed (user's explicit direction:
   "use whatever for callbackurl"): `kie.DEFAULT_SUNO_CALLBACK_URL`, an
   RFC 2606 `.invalid`-TLD placeholder guaranteed to never resolve, since
   nothing is ever meant to call it back.
3. **The mix filtergraph assumed the video always has its own audio
   stream.** The two already-rendered group clips from the smoke test
   above predate the `generate_audio` feature entirely, so they're
   video-only (no audio stream at all) — `_mix_background_music`'s
   `[0:a][music]amix=...` filter hard-failed ("Stream specifier ':a' ...
   matches no streams"), since `[0:a]` didn't exist. Fixed: new
   `_has_audio_stream()` (ffprobe-based) branches the filter graph —
   mixes under the clip's own audio when present, falls back to the music
   track alone (renamed to the `[aout]` label directly, not just appended
   after an already-closed `[music]` label -- an actual first-attempt bug
   in the fallback branch itself, caught by immediately re-running live
   rather than assuming the fix worked) when the clip has none. This is a
   real, permanent engine default (any clip rendered before this feature
   existed, or with voice/sfx both off, hits this path), not a one-off
   workaround for these two specific files.

**Verified against real spend, twice in a row (first attempt failed on
each of bug 2 and the filter-label bug, fixed and re-run rather than
assumed working):** a real Suno `V5_5` instrumental track was generated
from a hand-written prompt (upbeat pop-trap, sleepy-to-energetic build,
explicitly instrumental/no-vocals) and mixed into the final video —
confirmed via `ffprobe`: exactly 30.0s, both an h264 video stream and an
AAC audio stream present, fades and loop-to-length applied correctly.
Delivered to the user as the actual answer to "cómo sería ya ensamblado
completo."

24 new tests added (`VideoAudioConfig` defaults, `_audio_hint`,
`generate_background_music` dry-run/live/failure, `assemble_final_video`
+ ffmpeg helpers including both the with-audio and no-audio-stream mix
paths, `submit_video`'s `generate_audio` flag, `submit_suno_music`'s
model/callback/style/title flags). 192 tests passing total (up from 168).

**User's own assessment at commit time: "the feature needs more
polishing."** Known rough edges, not yet fixed, called out explicitly
rather than left implicit:
- Unlike image rendering, a video group's own `hash` (which does change
  when `generate_audio` toggles) is never consulted by `cycle()`/
  `is_video()` to detect staleness — only file existence is checked, so
  toggling `voice`/`sfx` after a group is already rendered does **not**
  automatically invalidate and re-render it the way `compile`'s per-block
  hash-lock does for images. Silent staleness risk, not yet addressed.
- No cross-revision copy-forward for unchanged video groups (the M-D fix
  exists only on the image-render side).
- No prompt-compaction ladder for video prompts (still a single hard-fail
  guard, as originally deferred — unchanged from the prior entry).
- `generate_background_music()` has no cap on `max_wait_seconds` retry/
  backoff discipline beyond a flat poll loop — doesn't share
  `async_jobs.handle_terminal_failure`'s credit-halt/retry-count machinery
  the way `cycle()` does, since it's a single synchronous call rather than
  a batch; acceptable for v1, but a real transient failure mid-poll would
  currently just hard-fail rather than retry.
- If the assembled video's total duration changes after a background-music
  track already exists (e.g. a group is re-clustered to a different
  length), `assemble_final_video` silently loops/trims the *existing*
  track to the new length rather than flagging that the track may no
  longer musically fit; no staleness check on the music file itself.

explicitly as "spoken narration cue only... do NOT render this as
on-screen text" rather than just quoting it bare -- Seedance had been
rendering the quoted caption text into the frame itself (with a
typo), since quoting it gave the model something to try to draw.

**M-cv1/cv2/cv3: `canon_video`**, a second canon registry
(`canon_video/canon_video.json`, project-level, parallel to but separate
from the main `canon.json`) answering "how does this transition/edit
unfold" rather than "what does X look like": a `motion-guide` (a
multi-panel sheet for a complex transition within one block, e.g.
unwrapping a product), a `text-overlay` (a literal reference for exact
on-screen text/graphics), and -- added in a later round, once a
new problem was found (see below) -- an `assembly-guide` (one sketched
panel per block in a group, with explicit CUT/CONTINUOUS markers, for
groups whose blocks span different scenes/locations). New module
`canon_video.py` mirrors `canon.py`'s shape closely (free-metadata-patch
discipline for `physical_profile`, kind-specific sheet layouts, sketch-vs-
photoreal split). A new LLM discovery pass, `run_video_canon_discovery`
(video.py), mirrors `expand_technical`'s mid-stream `canon_needed`
discovery but operates on an already-clustered `VideoGroup` instead of a
single block; its findings persist to `video_canon_needed.json`
(revision-scoped) and `video-plan` cross-checks that file against
`canon_video`'s actual approved elements, reporting any still-unresolved
group as `blocked_on_video_canon` -- never silently attaching a partial
reference set. New CLI/MCP surface: `canon-video list/generate/approve/
reject` and `video-analyze`. Tool count 22 -> 27.

**Three more real bugs found only by re-rendering and looking closely,
fixed in sequence, each with its own live re-render to confirm:**

1. **A photoreal motion-guide caused worse discontinuity, not less.** The
   first `motion-guide` generated for the chew-unwrap transition was a
   polished 5-panel product-photography filmstrip. Re-rendering with it
   attached made things *worse*: a hand appeared with no visible arm
   connecting it to the body, wearing a ring/watch that violates
   `talent_hands`' own canon description. Root cause: a photoreal,
   professionally-lit filmstrip is stylistically alien to a handheld UGC
   shot, and the video model appears to try to literally cut between the
   filmstrip's own separate photo panels rather than treating it as
   guidance. Fix: reused the *exact* sketch-draft mandate the guide-image
   harness already established for the same reason (`compile.py`'s
   `GUIDE_ASSEMBLY_INTRO`) -- `canon_video.py` gained `_SKETCH_MANDATE` /
   `_SKETCH_MANDATE_KINDS`, applied to `motion-guide` and `assembly-guide`
   (kinds about *transitions*) but never `text-overlay` (whose entire
   purpose -- exact legible text -- a sketch render would undermine).
   Confirmed by re-rendering: continuous hand, no jewelry, correct shape.
2. **The wrapped chew's texture didn't match the real product** (a
   generic shiny twist-candy look, no visible brand print) even after the
   hand fix. Root cause, found by re-reading `select_reference_images`:
   video generation had *never* attached a canon element's own approved
   reference sheet directly -- only each block's own once-removed final/
   guide render (itself an AI approximation, not the ground truth) plus
   the (now-sketch) motion-guide (no color/material information at all).
   This is the exact same bug class as the image-pipeline's own "Fifth
   bug" (canon sheets never attached as `--image` references) recorded
   earlier in this journal, just never fixed on the video side. Fixed:
   new `_referenced_canon_sheet_paths`, attached with priority *after*
   each block's own final (so per-block composed-scene context is never
   crowded out of the model's small reference budget) but before guides.
   Confirmed live: correct wrap texture, correct logo, in every checked
   frame.
3. **The unwrap motion itself was physically implausible** (one hand held
   the product bag throughout, so unwrapping a twist-foil candy one-
   handed isn't something a real person can do) -- caught by the user,
   who proposed the general fix directly: check motion plausibility, and
   where implausible, resolve with an explicit cut rather than asking for
   an impossible continuous take. `run_video_canon_discovery`'s system
   prompt gained a "MOTION PLAUSIBILITY CHECK" -- explicitly framed as
   relative to *this canon's own established facts* (how many hands
   `talent_hands` has, per the user's own correction), never a generic
   assumed physical law, so a canon that establishes something unusual
   (extra limbs, etc.) is respected rather than overridden. On the real
   re-render, the video model resolved the constraint on its own, more
   elegantly than the designed hard-cut fallback: it staged the bag
   propped against the torso rather than hand-held, freeing both hands
   for one continuous, physically real two-handed unwrap.

**`assembly-guide` (kind, not yet exercised live)**: added once the
user pointed out a related, larger-scope problem the fixes above don't
touch -- a single `VideoGroup` can span several genuinely different
locations (a driveway, a kitchen table, a car interior) generated as one
continuous Seedance clip with nothing telling the model how to *cut*
between them. Reuses the identical sketch-mandate discipline; discovery
guidance added to `run_video_canon_discovery` alongside the motion-
plausibility check, defaulting to a hard cut whenever a scene/location
genuinely changes between blocks.

Verified against the real Coffee Chews campaign throughout -- `video-
analyze` correctly proposed both a `motion-guide` for the unwrap and a
`text-overlay` for the bag's pack copy on the first real call, unprompted.
One more real mistake surfaced and fixed live: the first `text-overlay`
generation was run through a direct Python call that skipped the CLI's
own reference-image auto-resolution (a shortcut taken to route around an
environment-variable issue), producing a bag/logo that didn't match the
real brand assets -- caught by the user, fixed by regenerating with the
real `product_bag`/`youchews_logo` sheets explicitly attached as
references.

261 tests passing (up from 168 at the start of this arc). Final,
corrected video delivered to the user after the third live re-render.

## Deliverable: campaign creative-process white paper + reusable template

Separately, built a marketing-facing (non-technical, platform-agnostic)
"white paper" case study describing this campaign's creative process --
competitive research through finished ad -- as a PDF, for a business
audience, never naming or describing the technical pipeline. Content was
grounded in the real record (`knowledge/journals/adcrush-campaigns/`'s own
Coffee Chews entry: the real functional-chew-format competitive analog,
the real "no invented cross-section" customer-complaint finding, the real
on-pack numbers) rather than generic filler, after an explicit correction
to be more precise. Built with `fpdf2` (pure Python, no system library
dependencies -- WeasyPrint was tried first and needs Pango/GObject, not
worth installing for one document) in an isolated `uv venv`. The reusable
design system (`WhitePaper(FPDF)` class: header/footer, section_title,
body, bullet, gallery_page) and a copyable content template now live at
`/Users/hassan/repos/youchews/campaigns/white-papers/` (outside this
repo, alongside the campaign's own working directories), with a README
documenting the process end to end for future campaigns.

# References

- Design source: `knowledge/journals/reusable-storyboard-cli/2705701b-b2b6-404a-86aa-23e097596f37--t-0e3938282b92b9ed23e44b822569ea4a.md`
- Implementation: `adcrush-cli/` (committed)
- `seedance-2.5` support: `/Users/hassan/repos/kie-api` (sibling repo, committed separately)
