# Goal

Formalize the category AdCrush is betting on and map the competitive space, as investor-room
research documents. Success: a founder can answer "what category are you in, who else is in it,
and why won't they win" from written, source-linked material rather than improvisation.

# Task Contract

- **Intended outcome:** five new documents in `investors_room/Research/` (03–07) plus an index,
  and a published visual landscape.
- **Observable success criteria:** every competitive claim carries a public source; every price
  and funding figure is marked third-party reported; the category recommendation is explicit;
  open items are named rather than papered over.
- **Constraints and non-goals:** desk research only — no primary interviews, no paid data. No
  changes to `adcrush-cli/` code. Does not modify the existing deck JSON; §5 of doc 03 records
  proposed deck edits for the founder to apply.
- **Open questions and assumptions:** assumes the shipped-code inventory in doc 06 §4 is accurate
  as of the `video-self-improvement` branch.

# Execution Boundaries

- **Authorized scope:** new research documents under `investors_room/Research/`; one published
  artifact. Explicitly excluded: editing `AdCrush_AI_Agentic_Deck.json`, the PDFs, or any code.
- **Affected interfaces and owners:** investor-facing narrative, owned by the founder. All
  category and pricing recommendations are marked as decisions, not findings.
- **Escalated during the task:** the category name itself changed twice under founder direction —
  from "rename away from GTM" to "GTMTech Agentic" to "define PMFTech above GTM". Each was a
  founder call on requirements, correctly escalated rather than assumed.

# Handoff Topology

- **Selection:** single handoff. One cohesive, independently verifiable slice — a set of research
  documents that stand or fall together and are verified by reading, not by execution.
- **Integrator:** author. No delegation; no subagents used.

# Existing Approaches

- Followed the method established by `01-system-blueprint.md`: a stated method note, claims traced
  to a citable source, and explicit separation of finding from recommendation.
- Retained that document's discipline of naming its own limits, which is why every doc here has an
  open-gaps section and every figure is marked directional.

# Planned Proof

- Deterministic: markup validation of the published artifact (SVG well-formedness, no `var()` in
  SVG presentation attributes, no label overflow past the viewBox).
- Integration: cross-reference integrity between docs 03–07 and the index.
- **Remaining judgment:** the strategic recommendations are arguments, not verifiable outputs. The
  correlation claim underpinning the whole thesis is unproven and is recorded as open item 1.

# Status

- [x] Planned
- [x] In progress
- [ ] Complete — deck edits in doc 03 §5 not yet applied; open items 1–7 outstanding

# Work Log

- Read the existing investor materials to extract the current claim: deck declares
  `category: "GTM Product Engineering"`, `mcp_strategy: "MCP-first, not MCP-only"`, entry offer
  $499, Lab $399–999/mo, plus six diligence flags.
- Ran eight web-research passes: GTM Engineering as a category; synthetic-audience concept
  testing; AI UGC creative generation; real-spend smoke testing; research incumbents; creative
  testing platforms; MCP adoption and ad-platform MCP launches; PMF as a category term.
- Wrote `03-category-definition.md` — category position; rewritten twice under founder direction
  (see Decisions).
- Wrote `04-competitive-landscape.md` — eight bands of adjacency, ranked threat register, full
  source list.
- Wrote `05-market-thesis-operator-class.md` — the demand-side thesis, plus §2.1 on what operators
  already pay for PMF.
- Wrote `06-canonical-example.md` — the white chocolate YouChews walkthrough, with a per-stage
  owned / connector / service marker.
- Wrote `07-agentic-interface-shift.md` — MCP as a platform moment, including a correction to a
  proposed claim that failed checking.
- Wrote `investors_room/Research/index.md` and cross-linked all documents.
- Published the landscape artifact.

# Decisions

- **Category: define PMFTech, sit above GTMTech.** Converged over three founder-directed
  revisions. "GTM Engineering" is occupied by Clay (reportedly 84% adoption among GTM engineers,
  plus a job title, certification ecosystem, and annual state-of-category report), so an
  unqualified GTM claim imports the wrong comparables. The deeper problem is sequence: GTM
  presumes you know what you are selling. PMFTech has no vendor category, no analyst coverage and
  no incumbent, while the concept needs zero education.
- **Recorded a self-correction rather than hiding it** (doc 03 §1.5). An earlier draft argued for
  a vector *inside* GTMTech and listed four objections to claiming PMFTech. Three do not survive:
  the budget exists but is unlabeled; category creation is cheap when the concept needs no
  teaching; and — the actual error — sitting *above* GTM strengthens the orchestrator claim rather
  than forfeiting it, because the whole GTM stack becomes downstream. Only the upmarket-vocabulary
  objection stands.
- **Demoted "MCP-first" from moat to table stakes.** Meta shipped an official Ads MCP on
  2026-04-29 (29 tools), X on 2026-08-24 (23 tools), StackAdapt on 2026-04-21. Reframed: platform
  MCPs commoditize *access*, which is a cost removed; the moat is state and judgment — canon,
  bounded cost, norms, the verdict. Pure routing is worth zero.
- **Named the norms database as the durable moat.** Every component of the loop is individually
  purchasable in 2026; the assembled loop is an integration moat, and integration moats decay as
  components acquire clean interfaces. The accruing asset — Distribution Viability Score norms —
  is the only piece a competitor cannot buy, and is precisely what Zappi rents at $3K–25K/study.
  Reframes the $499 test as a norms-acquisition channel rather than the revenue engine.
- **Adopted the white chocolate YouChews question as the standing canonical example.** Chosen
  because it is small, decidable, has a real control (the existing chocolate SKU), is repeatable
  by construction, and — the load-bearing reason — the white chocolate product does not exist, so
  the creative must invent a photoreal product and hold it consistent across every shot. That is
  the commercial justification for the canon engine: continuity is the *enabling condition* for
  pre-launch testing of physical products, not a quality nicety.
- **Rejected a proposed market-thesis claim on evidence.** See Verification Results.

# Verification Results

- **Fact-check, requested by the founder: "people spend more time with their agents than in any
  other non-AI app" — FALSE, and excluded from the materials.** ChatGPT is reported at ~23
  min/day per user (~6 min/session, Apr 2026); TikTok ~95 min/day per DAU, YouTube+Shorts ~75,
  Instagram ~55, Facebook ~33; global social media average ~2 h 21 min. Recorded in doc 07 §3
  together with a defensible replacement that needs no time-spent figure: agent use is
  intent-driven not attention-driven (~72% desktop traffic), so the claim to make is share of
  high-intent commercial work, narrowed to our own ICP.
- **Fact-check: is PMFTech a defined category — no.** No vendor category, analyst coverage, market
  map, or incumbent found. The concept is well established (Andreessen; Sequoia's Arc PMF
  Framework; VC glossaries and vendor measurement guides).
- **Shipped-code inventory confirmed against source**, not assumed: `adcrush-cli` exposes 24 CLI
  subcommands covering intake, canon, canon_video, breakdown/expand, compile, render-guide,
  render-final, video-render, audit, publish, review. No landing-page, campaign-launch,
  instrumentation, DVS, or verdict module exists. Doc 06 §4 therefore marks stages 3, 7, 9, 11 and
  12 as service- or connector-delivered. This is a diligence-material gap and is stated as such.
- **Artifact markup validated:** 39 `<text>` elements balanced, 5 `<g>` balanced, no unclosed
  shape tags, zero `var()` remaining in SVG presentation attributes (converted to CSS classes,
  since presentation attributes do not reliably resolve custom properties). Three labels were
  found to overflow the 1000-unit viewBox and were re-anchored before republishing.
- **Not verified:** all pricing and funding figures are third-party reported and remain
  directional. Several (Zappi per-study, Suzy contract range) are buyer-reported rather than
  published. Flagged in every document.

# Open Issues

1. **No quantified correlation** between a pre-launch test and downstream commercial outcome. The
   largest open item; already the deck's own first diligence flag.
2. **Norms database not yet accumulated** — N is the binding constraint on the stated moat, and on
   whether the norms slide can be shown at all.
3. **Distribution half of the loop is not shipped code** (doc 06 §4).
4. **Ad-platform policy exposure unmeasured** — no rejection-rate or incident data for pre-launch
   / fake-door creative.
5. **$499 price point** sits in an unoccupied $200–$3,000 band; pressure direction unknown.
6. **Operator-population size and concepts-fielded-per-year unmeasured** — the multiplier in the
   bottom-up model, and the difference between a transaction and a subscription business.
7. **Will this ICP pay for negative information?** Velocity framing ("find the winner in ten days
   instead of ten weeks") is untested and is itself a landing-page test AdCrush could run on
   itself.
8. **Deck edits not applied.** Doc 03 §5 lists seven proposed changes to
   `AdCrush_AI_Agentic_Deck.json`; left for the founder.
9. **Audos not fully mapped** — closest thesis analog; method overlap unknowable from public
   sources.

# References

# Goal

Make `adcrush` render a 15-second video block *reliably* — same product shape in
every frame, no phantom limbs or people, no reference sheet leaking into
footage, the talent's face never shown — and make the pipeline able to tell,
without a human scrubbing frames, whether it succeeded. Today the pipeline can
produce a good clip but cannot distinguish a good clip from a bad one, and
when it fails it retries with the byte-identical prompt. This lane closes that
loop: instructions become visual and referential instead of verbose, every
result is judged by a vision model, retries apply escalating additive fixes
that never mutate the compiled source, and every step is recorded in a ledger
surfaced by a live dashboard.

The durable, versioned plan is `docs/plans/video-self-improvement.md` (Parts
I-VIII: narrative preamble, locked decisions, research, architecture "why",
grounded code citations, SOLID principles, handoff stages S0-S9, execution
guide). This journal is the main index for the lane and records what actually
happens against that plan. Work happens on branch `video-self-improvement`
(from `video-gen`).

# Task Contract

- Intended outcome: (1) referential, lean EDL video prompts (target <= 3,500
  chars, hard cap 6,000, down from 14-18k) that address imprinted sheets by
  slug and `@Image{n}` index; (2) one imprint/slug system and one six-zone
  layout catalog for every generated sheet (canon, canon_video, block
  storyboard, group assembly), guide grammar = sketch, canon grammar =
  faithful; (3) total duration a multiple of 15s, every group exactly 15s,
  EDL timecodes normalized to the boundary; (4) a formal `media_review`
  engine (frames -> vision judge -> additive recipes at intensity 1/2/3 ->
  max 3 retries) reusable for video groups and guide/final images; (5) an
  append-only JSON ledger and a new `adcrush dashboard` tool (Explore /
  Timeline / Outputs / constraints); (6) one budget-capped self-improvement
  run on `campaigns/coffee-chews-ugc-reel` stopping at `video-render`.
- Observable success criteria: `video-plan` on the canonical project yields
  two 15s groups with EDL sums of 15.0 and prompts <= 3.5k chars; a live
  `video-review` on the existing rev-003 group-2 clip flags
  `REFERENCE_BLEED` and `EXTRA_PERSON_OR_LIMB` (its known defects); one live
  pass (<= 3 retries/group) on rev-004 yields promoted clips with per-shot
  verdicts, a full ledger, and a dashboard timeline of the run within budget
  (worst case 8 Seedance renders + 8 judge calls + <= 2 synth calls + ~14
  image renders/reviews); `uv run pytest` green at every stage (baseline
  261); the simulation harness (`adcrush-cli/simulation/run_simulation.py`)
  passes end-to-end offline before any live spend.
- Constraints and non-goals: dry-run by default (`--live --yes` on every
  cost-bearing call, every time); `adcrush` itself is the CLI boundary (the
  LLM SDK stays inside `LLMAdapter`; no standalone `llm-cli`); the 13
  existing approved canon sheets are NOT regenerated (referenced by attach
  order via the prompt's REFERENCE MAP); no `video-assemble`/music in this
  lane; no brand-level canon library (only a small `canon promote` guard);
  no second live pass without the user's explicit go; dashboard is vanilla
  JS, English, CDN libraries only if downloaded and frozen under
  `static/vendor/` with name/version/source/sha256 recorded in this
  journal's Decisions.
- Open questions and assumptions: `@Image{n}` ordinal addressing is
  documented for the ByteDance partner API (fal.ai README) and inferred for
  kie.ai (attach order == array index is verified in kie-cli source) — the
  S4 dry-run and the S9 live run verify it; Seedance may still reproduce
  sheet chrome even with imprint + anti-bleed clause — mitigations are the
  `drop_reference_kinds` recipe at intensity 2 and, as a fallback, attaching
  only G + C + F for video; the judge's false-positive rate is unknown — the
  first live run gets a human spot-check of every promoted clip.

# Execution Boundaries

- Authorized scope and exclusions: branch `video-self-improvement` in
  `/Users/hassan/repos/youchews/ad-crush` (code under `adcrush-cli/`,
  knowledge under `knowledge/`, plan under `docs/plans/`); new modules
  `ledger.py`, `sheet_layouts.py`, `sheet_harness.py`, `jobs.py`,
  `media_review/`, `dashboard/`, `simulation/`; modifications to
  `schemas.py`, `compile.py`, `canon.py`, `canon_video.py`, `video.py`,
  `render.py`, `publish.py`, `corpus.py`, `project_config.py`, `review.py`,
  `cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `viewer/server.py`. Excluded: `main`/`video-gen`
  branches, the sibling `kie-api` repo, regenerating approved canon sheets,
  any assemble/music step, any spend outside Phase D of the execution guide.
- Affected interfaces, owners, and relevant side effects: CLI gains

  `Block` gains `shot_line`, `lens`, `transition_out` (hash-relevant fields
  change every block hash -> the canonical run is a full re-render, accepted);
  `VideoGroup` gains `slug`, `edl`, `reference_map`, `assembly_sheet_path`;

  - **S1 Ledger** (`ledger.py`, `note`, `ledger backfill`) — entry: S0; in:

  - **S2 Sheet layout catalog + harness** (`sheet_layouts.py`,
    `sheet_harness.py`, pure text) — entry: S0; in: 29-razones compiled guide
    prompt + direction-sheet anatomy; out: `LayoutSpec`, `closest_layout`,
    `render_sheet_harness`, slug grammar, six zones, ten archetypes; proof:

## 2026-09-10 20:30 - The first assembled cut shipped a clipped caption

`video-assemble` produced the 15s stylised cut: 15.14s delivered, nine caption

The cause: `max_chars_per_line` is a style's EDITORIAL preference and was
being used as the PHYSICAL limit. The motion-graphics register asks for 20
characters at `size_pct` 6.0; on a 720-wide frame that is 77px Arial Black,
about 1,000px of type against 604px of usable width. "COFFEE YOU CAN CHEW."
is exactly 20 characters, so `_wrap` correctly kept it on one line -- and
`WrapStyle: 2` means libass does not wrap, so it was simply clipped. Both
halves behaved as written; the two numbers were never the same number.

`ass.char_budget(style, canvas)` now computes the physical limit from the
canvas and `size_pct` via `CHAR_WIDTH_RATIO = 0.62` (measured against Arial
Black uppercase, the widest face any register asks for, so every other face
breaks slightly early -- the safe direction when the alternative is silent
clipping), and the smaller of the two wins. Budgets on a 720x1280 frame:
motion-graphics 12 (from 20), ugc-vertical 15 (from 26), papercraft 16 (from
30). The budget is resolution-independent by construction, since `size_pct` is
a fraction of frame height -- a caption occupies the same share of the picture
on any screen -- and a 16:9 frame does fit the style's full preference.

A second instance of the same bug, found while fixing the first: the karaoke
path (`word_pop`, `karaoke_wipe`) built one space-joined line and never
wrapped at all, so an ANIMATED register clipped exactly like a plain one. It
now breaks on the visible length, ignoring the `\k` override tags.

Re-burned and re-inspected: two lines, both comfortably inside the margins.

The test that now guards it asserts, for every style and every register, that
`budget x size_px x ratio` fits the usable width -- not a golden file. This is
the third bug in this subsystem that only reading pixels would find, after the
missing `Style: ` prefix and the `ass_time` carry.

## 2026-09-11 The judge could not see a melted hand, and never looked at a guide

The first live M# batch came back with a third hand in panel 2 of M5 --
holding the crushed foil, floating, traceable to no arm -- and nothing in the
pipeline objected. Pulling that thread found four separate holes, each of
which alone was enough to let it through.

**The motion sheets were rendered with no references at all.** `motion_records`
built `{"block": {"id": ...}}`, and `render.cycle` reads
`record["block"]["canon_refs"]` to choose reference images. Every M# was drawn
from text alone, which is why the talent wore a pink tank top in the guide and
an olive tee in all six finals. An M# is itself a video reference, so this is
worse here than on any other sheet: a motion guide that disagrees with the
canon teaches the generator the disagreement. The record now carries the whole
block -- the review lane re-validates the same dict as a `Block`, so a
hand-picked subset of fields fails there instead.

**The taxonomy counted limbs and never checked their shape.**
`EXTRA_PERSON_OR_LIMB` fires on the wrong NUMBER of hands. A hand with five
fingers and melted geometry passed it clean. `ANATOMY_DEFORMED` now covers the
right-count-wrong-geometry case, with the hands called out specifically because
they are where it fails most and are rarely the subject of the shot.
`EXTRA_PERSON_OR_LIMB` additionally says to trace each hand along its arm to a
shoulder, which is what makes an unattached one detectable at all.

**`render-motion` had no `--review`, and review was opt-in everywhere else.**
Motion sheets were never judged, by anything. Worse, opt-in is the shape of
thing that gets forgotten: a guide rendered without `--review` is looked at by
nothing, and a guide is not cosmetic -- the final is drawn from it and the clip
from the motion sheet. Every image phase is now judged by DEFAULT, with
`--no-review` kept for a deliberate cheap pass.

**A motion sheet would have been judged as footage.** `sheet_mode` was
`phase == "guide"`, so the new phase would have gone to the footage rubric,
which reports panel borders as REFERENCE_BLEED -- a CRITICAL code -- on every
sheet, every time. The retry ladder would then have worked to strip the chrome
that makes a sheet a sheet. Membership is now a property of the phase set.

### Rule sets per image type, as data

Three media types reach the judge and they are not interchangeable: a sheet's
panel borders are its chrome, and the identical borders in a finished frame are
a critical defect. That adaptation already existed, in two hand-written
paragraphs of prose, and the prose had drifted -- neither mode asked whether
the drawn body held together. `media_review/modes.py` holds it as DATA instead:
per mode, what the image IS, which codes are inapplicable, and the MINIMUM
failure list, each code paired with what it means in THAT mode. The preamble is
generated from the list, so adding a check is adding one row, and a test
asserts no mode both checks and excuses the same code, and that every mode
checks anatomy, limb count and canon.

### Physics per canonical thing

`PhysicalProfile.rigidity` had been a label since it was added: five allowed
strings that read as a fact and translate into no check anybody runs. A judge
told "the chew is rigid" still has to invent what that forbids.
`integrity.py` expands it deterministically into the two sentences that matter
-- what the thing is ALLOWED to do and what would mean it broke -- and the
judge rubric now carries one line per element. A character is neither rigid nor
soft, so characters get ARTICULATED: rotation at real joints, within range,
segments of constant length, every hand traceable to a shoulder. An element
declaring no rigidity gets no rule at all; an invented physics is worse than
none, because the judge would then reject frames against a rule nobody wrote.

**One thing this broke and restored.** Flipping review to the default silently
removed the render stage from the ledger -- the review lane emits only
`media_review.*` -- so the dashboard timeline would have stopped showing
renders. A promoted image now emits `render.completed` whichever path produced
it. The first version of that emit named an actor the ledger rejects and
vanished, because `safe_emit` swallows its own errors; the test asserts the
event lands rather than that the call was made.

## 2026-09-11 References without a map are a style instruction

Giving the motion sheets their canon references fixed the identity drift and
broke the sheet completely: the next live batch came back as flawless
PHOTOGRAPHS. Correct talent, correct wardrobe, correct product, both hands
attached -- and no panels, no imprint card, no cut bars, no timecodes. Not a
motion guide at all.

The cause is one empty argument. `assemble_motion_prompt` passed
`references=[]`, so the harness emitted no REFERENCE MAP clause, and the clause
is what says "use these for identity, proportion, material and place only;
never copy their composition, poses or panels". Without it the attached canon
sheets -- photoreal by design -- are simply the best evidence in the prompt
about what the output should look like, and the model followed them. The B#
storyboards never had this problem because `_storyboard_references` has always
built the map. The motion sheet now builds the same map from the same
`canon_refs` in the same order, so `@Image{n}` means the same n in both.

**The judge missed it, and that is the more interesting failure.** In sheet
mode the rubric already said a photoreal image with no panels is STYLE_BREAK.
It reported CANON_DRIFT at 0.35 and passed the sheet. Every code in the list
asks about the SUBJECT, the subject was flawless, so each passed in turn and
nothing asked whether the artifact was the right KIND of thing. The sheet mode
now answers that first, explicitly, before any subject check.

After both fixes all six sheets carry the grammar and the identity together,
and the ladder did its job on its own: block_5 failed CONTINUITY_BREAK at 0.72,
a recipe was composed on top of the base prompt, and attempt 1 passed. Five
blocks promoted at attempt 0; one at attempt 1; none exhausted.

## 2026-09-11 The storyboard grid was a print constraint we copied without its reason

The user looked at a B# sheet beside its final and said the guide should be an
annotated version of how to produce that final pose. Checking the 29-razones
reference confirmed it, and located the original error.

**What the reference actually does.** Its guide prompt declares
`Retícula: dos viñetas superiores iguales; una viñeta inferior de ancho
completo. Número de celdas: 3`, and its FINAL prompt declares the identical
reticle -- `Use exactly 3 distinct comic panels... Exact page reticle: dos
viñetas superiores iguales; una viñeta inferior de ancho completo` -- and
attaches the guide labelled "Previsualización de ESTA MISMA PÁGINA; conserva su
continuidad, no copies sus anotaciones técnicas". One page, drawn twice: once
annotated, once finished. Guide cells equal final cells, one to one. Every
annotation on the sheet -- VP lines, action line, gaze and light arrows, prop
circle, gesture skeleton -- exists to direct the pose that will actually be
rendered.

**Why it has three cells.** Because 29 razones is a PRINTED COMIC. A page holds
several panels; the guide has several cells because the final does. That is a
constraint of that deliverable and not a property of storyboarding. adcrush
copied the grid and left the reason behind -- and this is, I think, the stem of
every confusion in this area.

**What it cost us.** Our deliverable is one video frame per block, but
`storyboard_panel_count` returned 3, or 4 past six seconds, with the panels
being MOMENTS IN TIME. `render-final` was then told to "realize its LAST panel".
So three of four annotated poses directed nothing at all, the pose that shipped
got a quarter of the sheet's direction, and the guide had quietly stopped being
a blueprint of the final -- it was a different artifact that happened to
contain the final in its last cell. Meanwhile M# was independently re-deriving
the same block into segment panels, so the exit state was drawn twice, from two
prompts, paid for twice and judged twice.

**The fix.** `NarrativeFormat.cells_per_clip`, default 1, is the single
declaration of the grid, and `sheet_harness.grid_declaration()` renders the one
sentence that goes into BOTH prompts -- the reference's invariant, made
mechanical. `STORYBOARD_FINAL_CLAUSE` stops saying "realize its LAST panel" and
says the storyboard is an annotated preview of this same shot whose
composition, camera, pose, eyeline, light and prop state are to be kept exactly
and whose annotations must never appear. On a one-cell sheet the cell IS the
exit state, and ENTRY and ACTION become annotations ON the frame ("arrives
from", "through") rather than cells of their own -- which is what a director's
sketch does anyway.

Two follow-on corrections the change forced. The cell grammar used to say
"panels run chronologically" and "between adjacent panels draw the transition
glyph"; on a one-cell sheet those are an invitation to invent cells, so
`panel_grammar(count)` now splits, and the single-cell wording says explicitly
that there is no reading order, nothing to sequence, and no second cell for a
before or after state. Both wordings keep the construction a renderer needs:
gestural skeleton, horizon and vanishing points, depth layers, coded gutter. And
because `group-assembly` lists ONE cell spec meaning "one panel per block", cell
count cannot be read off the spec list -- `LayoutSpec.multi_cell` declares it.

`panels_per_block` stays in the schema, unread, so older `narrative_format.json`
still loads; a test asserts a project carrying the old 3/4 range gets 1.

Multi-cell remains available by raising `cells_per_clip` for a deliverable that
really is multi-cell -- a print page, a carousel. A shot's temporal breakdown is
NOT such a reason: panels across time belong to M#, whose panels are segment
ends and which the video model actually reads.

Consequence: every block hash moves, so guides and finals re-render. M# and
canon are untouched. 717 unit tests green, simulation 24/24.

# Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Storyboards | Per-block storyboard AND per-group assembly sheet, one harness | Per-block carries the action, per-group the edit; one visual language |
| Prompt | Referential + lean EDL (slugs, `@Image{n}`, timecodes, shoot preamble, transitions) | Long prose diluted adherence and bred new defects; detail belongs in images |
| Imprint | Unified printed label on every generated sheet; guide vs canon grammar; no regeneration of approved sheets | One naming system; approve-cycle cost > API cost; REFERENCE MAP covers legacy sheets |
| Layout + canvas | Six-zone anatomy, ten archetypes, closest-layout fallback; canvas = campaign format | Grounded in two reference sheets; composition transfers; bleed guarded by chrome + clause + recipe |
| Intensity 3 | May simplify the story beat | Fail-proof must be allowed to change choreography; the message survives |
| Judge | Anthropic vision, frames + labeled references | Adapter already supports attachments; refs make "matches approved product" checkable |
| CLI boundary | `adcrush` is the CLI; SDK inside `LLMAdapter` | Zero new infra, provider-agnostic, extractable later |
| Image lane | Same engine wired into render-guide/final now | Proves the abstraction; catches defects before video |
| 15s rule | Fail hard; groups exactly 15s | "Never silently generate with a gap" |
| Budget | 1 pass, <= 3 retries/group, then report | Validate the engine before paying for convergence |
| Journal | New topic `adcrush-self-improvement` | Clean stream; links back to `adcrush-implementation` |
| Dashboard | New tool, English, vanilla JS, frozen vendored libs only | Offline, reproducible, in the viewer's spirit |
| Execution | Simulation-first (Phases A-D), tag `sim-pass-<date>` before live | Prove offline, then spend once |
| Vendored dependencies | none (dashboard ships plain HTML/CSS/ES-module JS, no CDN) | Record name/version/source/sha256 here if any is ever frozen |

## Measured unit costs (our own receipts, `creditsConsumed`)

kie bills 100 credits to the dollar, confirmed by cross-checking our 945-credit
clip against kie's own published "$9.45" for the same generation.

| What | Credits | USD |
|---|---:|---:|
| `gpt-image-2` (either mode), 2K | 10 | $0.10 |
| `gpt-image-2-5-sunburst` (either mode), 2K | 10 | $0.10 |
| `seedance-2-fast`, 15s, 720p | 372 | $3.72 |
| `seedance-2-5`, 15s, 720p | 945 | $9.45 |
| `suno` V5_5 music | 12 | $0.12 |

Actual cost of the 30s live-action ad this session: about 36 image renders
(~$3.60) plus 5 clips (~$47.25) = **~$50.85**, of which **$37.80 was
group-2's four-attempt retry ladder**. The retry ladder, not the base render,
is the dominant cost. That reframes everything below: the highest-leverage
cost lever is raising the FIRST-ATTEMPT pass rate, not choosing a cheaper
model.

## 1. Keyframe triplets (S10) hurt continuity -- disable by default

Observed: in the live-action ad, the beat where the talent enters the car has
an unnatural transition that reads as two different cars or two irreconcilable
car angles.

Diagnosis: the triplet imposes THREE hard visual anchors per shot, so a
3-shot 15s clip must satisfy nine anchors plus the clip's own endpoints. Worse,
each block's triplet is planned INDEPENDENTLY from that block's own final
frame, so consecutive anchors are never derived from one another -- block-4's
"last" frame and block-5's "first" frame are two unrelated renders of the same
place. The model resolves the contradiction by cutting to a different car.

Generalisation: **any per-item reference generation must either be chained
(each derived from the previous item's accepted output) or not used at all.**
Independently generated anchors are actively worse than fewer anchors.

Decision: default S10 off; pass the block's final frame as the single anchor.
Keep the triplet as an opt-in for a single-shot clip, where there is no
neighbour to contradict and the endpoints are the clip's own.

## 2. Move captions out of the generator and into a deterministic post-step

Observed: captions are hard for video generators.

Research: every off-the-shelf package (`ai-video-captions`, `captionforge`,
the various ffmpeg caption skills) is **transcription-first** -- Whisper for
word timings, then ASS, then ffmpeg. We do not need any of that: we already
KNOW the exact caption text and its timecodes, from the EDL. Adopting a
transcription pipeline would add a dependency and inject recognition error
into text we already hold exactly.

Recommendation: own a small `captions.py` that writes **ASS (Advanced
SubStation Alpha)** from the EDL plus the style's `caption_style`, burned with
ffmpeg's `ass` filter (NOT the `subtitles` filter, which discards animation).
ASS natively gives per-word karaoke timing (`\k`), outline, shadow, font,
size, colour and absolute positioning -- i.e. the CapCut/TikTok look with real
control. ffmpeg is already a hard dependency; no new runtime package.

Second-order win, and the reason this matters beyond looks: once captions are
a post-step, **both the image and the video prompt can say "no text at all"**.
`TEXT_GARBLED` and `TEXT_BURNED_IN` stop being failure classes the generator
can fail on, which directly attacks the retry ladder that dominates cost.
`StyleProfile.on_screen_text` changes meaning from "ask the model for text" to
"burn captions in post", and `caption_style` grows into a real struct (font,
size, fill, outline, shadow, position, animation preset).

## 3. Hooks: the first 5 seconds must earn attention

Observed: we need strong hooks by default; the first 5s must be eye-catching,
with better visual rhythm.

Generalisation: the opening shot is a different genre from the rest of the ad
and deserves its own contract, not the same treatment as beat 4.
`NarrativeFormat.hook_required` already exists and is **never read** -- dead
config. Proposal: enforce it. `expand` writes a `hook_device` on block 1;
the judge scores the first shot against a hook rubric (is the subject
readable inside one second, is there movement in the first half-second, is
there a visual question); a new `HOOK_WEAK` defect code with its own recipe
ladder. Also worth a general "calling image" bias: the storyboard/final
prompts for block 1 should ask for higher contrast and a tighter subject than
the body shots.

## 4. Trim at every internal join when assembling

Observed: a little drift at the start and end of each 15s group when one is
assembled onto the next.

Decision: trim a default **0.5s** at each internal boundary -- tail of clip N
and head of clip N+1 -- parametrizable so the user can tune it.

Generalisation and caution: trimming shortens the total, so a two-group 30s ad
lands near 29s. Either accept and REPORT the real duration, or plan for it:
design the EDL so the last half-second of each group is a held "handle"
rather than a moment we need. I prefer planning for it, because silently
delivering 29s when the brief said 30s is the kind of drift this project
exists to eliminate. Expose as `--trim-seconds` on `video-assemble` plus
`assembly.trim_seconds` in config.

## 5. Cheaper baseline models -- half right, with data

The user asks for `gpt-image-2` + `seedance-2.0` as the baseline defaults.

**The image half saves nothing.** `gpt-image-2` and `gpt-image-2-5-sunburst`
both cost exactly 10 credits per 2K render, measured on our own receipts. The
2.5 sheets are visibly better (one identity held across a ten-cell turntable,
legible real pack copy). Recommendation: KEEP GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; there is
no cost argument for downgrading.

**The video half is right and large.** 372 vs 945 credits for the same 15s
720p clip -- 2.5x. Agreed.

The real trade-off is not price but references: `seedance-2`/`-2-fast` accept
**9** reference images against 2.5's **30**, and cap at 15s. Group-2's prompt
carried 16 references, so on a 9-slot model seven would be dropped with a
warning, which is a canon-fidelity regression, not a saving.

Better shape, and what the user's own Higgsfield note argues for: **tier it.**
Run the judge/retry ladder on the cheap model and promote the accepted cut
once on the expensive one -- `--draft-model` / `--final-model`, mirroring the
Flare/Sunburst split we already have on images. With the ladder at $3.72 an
attempt instead of $9.45, a four-attempt group costs $14.88 instead of $37.80,
and the single final render adds $9.45.

## 7. Voice-over-safe copy must be a deterministic pre-flight check

Observed: copy written to be READ aloud needs a spoken form -- "100mg" has to
become "one hundred milligrams" -- so there should be a voice-over text
mapping, checked deterministically before generating video.

Generalisation: printed form and spoken form are two different fields, and
conflating them is the same class of error as conflating a canon id with a
description. Proposal: `DialogueLine.voice_over` alongside `text`, plus a
deterministic pre-flight that FAILS when a spoken line contains a token that
does not read aloud correctly: unit abbreviations (mg, g, oz, ml, kg),
digit-group separators (1,095), currency, %, ranges, initialisms (USA, TM),
and URLs. Ship a normaliser for the common cases and require an explicit
`voice_over` for anything it cannot handle -- never silently guess, and never
let a video render start with an unresolved spoken line. This also frees the
printed caption to stay tight ("100mg caffeine. 25 calories. 2g sugar.")
while the VO reads naturally.

# Open Issues
- **`canon.json` has no write lock, so concurrent `canon generate` calls lose
  elements silently.** Generating 13 canon sheets for `coffee-chews-ugc-v3`
  left 13 sheets on disk and 12 entries in the registry:
  `youchews_pouch_30ct_sealed` was billed, rendered and written to
  `canon/sheets/`, then vanished because a neighbouring generation's
  read-modify-write of `canon.json` clobbered it. `save_canon` reads the whole
  registry, mutates and rewrites, with no locking -- unlike `ledger.emit`,
  which already takes `fcntl.flock`. The failure is SILENT and costs real
  money: the sheet exists, so nothing looks missing until an approve fails or a
  block's `canon_refs` cannot resolve. Fix: the same `flock` the ledger uses,
  or a read-verify-retry on write. Until then, canon generation must be
  strictly sequential.
- **`canon generate` has no retry, unlike every other billed step.** Five of
  the same 13 generations failed with `FileNotFoundError` from kie-cli -- all
  five carrying reference images -- and succeeded when re-run individually, so
  it is a transient upload failure under rapid sequential submission.
  `render.cycle` has the full backoff-and-halt ladder; `canon generate` has
  nothing, which makes a batch of canon generations the most fragile billed
  step in the pipeline. They failed at submit so nothing was charged, but the
  operator has to notice and re-drive them by hand.
- **Nothing distinguishes a style that was CHOSEN from one that was DEFAULTED.**
  Setting up `coffee-chews-ugc-v3` I forgot to set the style, so `breakdown` and
  `expand` ran under the `chibi-comic` default and produced canon describing a
  "semi-chibi superhero-proportioned woman" in "flat saturated comic colors,
  cel-shaded" -- for a live-action UGC brief. Every gate passed: `expand`
  blocked on canon exactly as designed, and approving those 13 sheets would
  have rendered the whole 30s spot as a comic with nothing objecting. The style
  reaches canon descriptions, sheet grammar, the medium guidance, the caption
  registers and the music bed, so a defaulted style silently decides the entire
  campaign. Candidate fix: `style.json` records whether the id was set
  explicitly, and `breakdown`/`expand` warn (or refuse without `--yes`) on a
  never-chosen style. Cost of the miss here was only time, because it was

# Goal

Extract a reusable, LLM-agnostic (OpenAI/Anthropic-swappable), 100% CLI, no-agent
procedural system for authoring and publishing storyboard image sets,
generalized from the concrete implementation found in the sibling reference
folder `29-razones/` (comic "Ferry PowerPuff Star", now a frozen git-less
snapshot inside this repo). The real target domain (this repo is `ad-crush`)
is direct-response ad creative for platforms like Facebook — `29-razones` is
only the reference implementation used to reverse-engineer the procedural
pattern, not the end product. A future, explicitly deferred lane (not
designed here) will take the generated final images and produce video from
them. Work proceeds in layers: (1) understand the storytelling/content model
as implemented, (2) question and refine it in the abstract, (3) only then
draw the boundary between LLM-driven steps and deterministic steps, expressed
as modular CLIs with defined failure cases and verification.

# Task Contract

- Intended outcome: a validated, shared understanding of the current system's
  content model and technical pipeline (this entry), as the basis for a later
  design of a reusable framework. This phase is planning/journaling only — no
  code changes.
- Observable success criteria: the three research summaries below are
  confirmed or corrected by the user; open ambiguities are resolved or
  explicitly deferred before any implementation starts.
- Constraints and non-goals: do not modify `29-razones/` content; do not start
  building the generalized CLI yet; do not touch the external `kie-api`
  sibling repo.
- Open questions and assumptions: see "Open Issues".

# Existing Approaches

## Reference implementation surveyed: `29-razones/` ("Ferry PowerPuff Star")

### Narrative / content model
- Hierarchy: Book -> Acts (5, by page range) -> Page (90 pages, 6x9, 2:3) ->
  Panel/"celda" (2-6) -> fields (camera, action, state, text).
- Source-of-truth chain: corpus narrative (`libro/manuscrito/06-corpus-narrativo-90-paginas.md`)
  -> ingredient map (`07-mapa-de-ingredientes-90.md`) -> technical script
  (`08-guion-tecnico-90-paginas.md`) -> JSON image plan (`plan-de-imagenes-90.json`,
  one object per page: panels, layout, references[], beats[], cells[{cell,
  placement, camera, action, state_lock, creature_lock, lettering_type,
  lettering_placement, printed_text, permitted_diegetic_text}], state_lock,
  previous_page_reference, prompt path, production_guide path).
- "Element" = reusable character/place/object with a versioned "sheet" image
  (`*-character-sheet-v{N}.png`, `*-environment-sheet-v{N}.png`) that is the
  visual authority over any text description ("gana el rasgo visible de la
  hoja v2" per `biblia-visual.md`). A shared style-reference image is attached
  to every generation. A distinct "ingredient" element type (29 symbolic
  props) is explicitly denied face/personality.
- Continuity index (`indice-de-continuidad.json`): assets array
  `{id, kind(style|character|creature|location), status(approved|candidate),
  path, description, pages}`; `pages` is either explicit ranges/values or
  `{from_plan_references:true}` delegating to each page's `references[]`.
  `candidate` assets are withheld unless explicitly included post human review.
- Guide vs. final prompt: same cell data, different render target. Guide
  (`.md`) asks for an annotated previz/storyboard (pencil lines, mannequin
  figures, a 7-dimension continuity annotation checklist, only short codes for
  text, ends in a human approval checklist) and explicitly forbids literal
  dialogue text. Final (`.txt`) asks for finished flat-color art with exact
  quoted dialogue/SFX and negative-prompt anatomy guards.
- Dialogue is a separate concern (`dialogos-y-texto-visible-90.md`): only the
  text after "Texto impreso exacto:" renders, always in quotes; voice/mode
  (cartela/dialogo/pensamiento/SFX/SILENCIO) is typed per character.
- Continuity audits are layered: per-cell state_lock/creature_lock (positive +
  negative), a species/creature whitelist per page (`auditoria-de-especies-90.md`),
  and a full backward chain audit page 90->01 (`auditoria-retroactiva-90.md`).
- Flagged contradiction: `clineflow_specification.yml` id `comic-mute-format`
  is `unresolved: true` in 29-razones' own ledger (early spec = silent/mute
  horizontal album; later spec = dialogue-driven 6x9 vertical). Not our call to
  resolve — just noting the source project never closed it.

### Technical pipeline
- Prompt compilation is 100% deterministic Python templating
  (`compilar_prompts_desde_corpus.py`): corpus + continuity index ->
  90 final prompts + 90 guide prompts. No API calls, no LLM calls anywhere in
  the pipeline — prompt/story authoring is done externally by a human (with an
  LLM chat tool), the codebase only consumes finished text.
- Image generation is a subprocess call to a *sibling* CLI, not a library
  import: `kie-cli` from `/Users/hassan/repos/kie-api` (package `kie_cli`,
  console scripts `kie-cli`/`kie-mcp`), invoked via hardcoded absolute path in
  5+ scripts (`generar_paginas.py` is the only one with a `KIE_CLI` env
  fallback). Credentials (`KIE_API_KEY`, `KIE_BASE_URL`, `KIE_UPLOAD_BASE_URL`)
  live in kie-api's own `.env`, never in this repo.
- Guide->final is enforced purely by filesystem state (no workflow engine):
  `mantener_cola_paralela_guia.py::submit` only allows phase="final" once
  `guide_output_dir/{page_id}.png` exists; that PNG is attached as an extra
  reference image to the final call. V9
  (`mantener_cola_paralela_v9_referencias.py`) reuses this exact mechanism via
  monkeypatching, only changing where per-page reference images are sourced
  (parsed from a `REFERENCIAS DECLARADAS PARA ESTA PAGINA` block in the
  prompt text, vs. a fixed style/character-sheet set).
- Queue/concurrency: single-process cooperative scheduler, bounded
  `max_active`, `fcntl.flock` advisory lock against concurrent cycles,
  exponential-backoff retry up to `max_retries`, `--watch` loop with
  `--interval-seconds`. Resumability is entirely filesystem-derived (existence
  of `<id>.png` or `<id>.json` receipt), no separate state DB. Credit
  exhaustion is detected by substring-matching provider error text and halts
  the run pending manual resume.
- "Corrida" (run) is a versioned JSON config (`schema_version:1`) with a
  `prompt_lock.sha256` over all page prompts — any prompt edit invalidates the
  run and must be re-locked. Run state/receipts live under
  `libro/arte/salidas/<id>/estado.json` and `libro/produccion/jobs/<id>/`.
- Publish (`publicar_comic.py`): validates consecutive numbering (or
  `--allow-gaps`), even page count, every final has a matching guide; writes
  optimized WebP into a staging dir, then atomically swaps into `docs/`
  (GitHub Pages source) with rollback on failure.
- Review viewer (`player/`): vanilla ES-module JS + vendored PhotoSwipe, no
  framework, no backend. Reads a generated `manifest.json`. Guide/final toggle
  is client-side. `?review=true` mode stores free-text notes in
  `localStorage` only (per-browser, not shared/synced).
- Verification today is static/structural only: `verificar_continuidad.py`
  asserts plan/prompt/guide text against hardcoded rules (no pixel checks);
  only `publicar_comic.py` has unit tests
  (`tests/test_publicar_comic.py`); nothing tests the queue/operator scripts.

### Process/methodology mined from 29-razones' 34 journals (chronological, not just final state)

Read for inspiration on the LLM-vs-deterministic "gate" pattern (see Decisions
below). The 90-page project actually went through: brief -> 32pg draft ->
expanded to 90pg with technical scripts -> character sheets v2 -> pilot
5-page live test (deliberately withheld from approved-art dir pending human
review) -> a retrofit cluster fixing continuity/anatomy/eye-color/dialogue
issues found in that pilot, each fix immediately encoded as a permanent
compiler rule + verifier check -> formal milestone-chain infra for a 4K run
(paused/cancelled twice) -> sequential previous-page chaining tried as the
continuity mechanism, then downgraded to optional/off-by-default because it
didn't scale, replaced by declarative per-cell state/creature locks as the
sole mechanism -> full visual audit pass (diagnostic-only, no fixes applied,
pending authorization) -> credit-exhaustion hard-stop (402) -> two-phase
guide-gated pipeline (V6) -> hash-locked immutable per-revision configs
(V7-V9, never mutate a running one) -> species-identity retrofit (Zeus
rendered as wrong breed) -> continuity-asset candidate/approved status wall
-> static publisher with atomic-replace-or-reject -> V9 hit an undocumented
external hard limit (Kie's 20,000-char prompt cap), retrofitted as a
19,000-char mandatory cap in the verifier (safety margin) -> partial publish
via an explicit `--allow-gaps` flag, gaps left visible not silently patched.

Concrete gate patterns observed as already battle-tested (source: journals
`fac1bc0b`, `a5188ac8`, `bb7af813`, `b0e0a34a`, `f35327cb`, `08550f91`,
`64abe638`, `f1bbc83b`, `a79f3c53`/`eb84e3fd`, `d58f3640`, `3b2c03f5`,
`908c2512`, `d6ea836a`/`1bd2a70d`, `1df5f62e`):
- Dry-run-by-default; any spend/private-data-transfer step requires an
  explicit separate ask each time, never assumed from an earlier approval.
- Pilot-before-batch: generate a small representative sample first, review
  before committing the full run.
- Resource/quota exhaustion is a hard stop requiring human intervention, not
  a silent retry.
- **Retrofit-after-failure discipline**: every defect found in review
  (continuity, anatomy, species, dialogue voice, prompt-length overflow)
  was immediately encoded as a permanent compiler rule + automated verifier
  check, never left as a one-off manual fix. This is the concrete mechanism
  by which the LLM/human-review boundary and the deterministic-check boundary
  co-evolve over time.
- Diagnostic-only passes are a distinct mode from fix passes: audits produce
  a findings list and explicitly wait for human authorization before any
  correction is applied.
- Hash-locked immutable snapshot per revision instead of mutating a running
  config — directly confirms our root-folder/statelessness decision above.
  candidate/approved status + explicit override flag is the generalizable
  pattern for any AI-generated asset needing human promotion, not just
  continuity references.
- Atomic publish that rejects on structural defect and preserves the last
  good state; explicit gap-tolerance flag rather than silent patch/renumber.
- **Lesson from an abandoned approach**: strict runtime sequential
  dependency (page N+1 blocked until page N's approved art exists) was tried
  first as the continuity mechanism and abandoned/downgraded because it
  didn't scale to 90 pages — replaced by independent, declarative per-cell
  locks checked without a runtime chain. For the generalized system this
  argues for continuity/canon enforcement as stateless declarative
  constraints (checkable independently per block — the generalized system's
  term for the atomic narrative unit, replacing "page/scene" which are
  format-specific) rather than a sequential runtime dependency between
  blocks.
- Two journal streams show real process friction, kept as honest data: one
  opened and never filled in (`d087f4e6`), and the very last one
  (`1bd2a70d`) left "In progress" with empty Work Log/Decisions/Verification
  — even the source project's own journaling discipline had gaps.

### Deep-dive: literal prompt-template structure and continuity-verifier mechanics

Studied in depth on the user's request, since this directly informs how
`assemble_prompts` (templating) and `verify_structure` (rule checks) should
be designed for the generalized system. Source:
`compilar_prompts_desde_corpus.py`, `verificar_continuidad.py`,
`continuidad-de-estados.md`, `preparar_prompts_ejecucion_v9.py`, plus two full
prompt pairs (pages 25 and 76).

**Final-prompt template, ordered (`prompt_for()`, lines 814-848)**: fixed
page-format instruction -> variable reticle/layout line -> fixed
lettering-rendering contract (only "Texto impreso exacto:" text may render)
-> fixed `TREATMENT_BASE` (style/anatomy) -> variable continuity-reference
manifest (headed `"REFERENCIAS DECLARADAS PARA ESTA PÁGINA — ARCHIVOS DE
EJECUCIÓN:"`, one line per applicable canon asset) -> fixed character
framing -> fixed `CHARACTER_SHEET_AUTHORITY` block -> variable
creature-identity bible (only creatures active on that page) -> fixed
voice-direction block -> fixed pose/anatomy rules -> fixed negative-anatomy
prompt -> variable negative-creature prompt -> fixed palette line ->
conditional previous-page-continuity instruction (off by default) ->
variable page-level state-lock (7 phase bands) -> per-cell blocks (camera,
action, creature lock, lettering type/position, exact printed text,
permitted diegetic text).

**Guide-prompt template, ordered (`guide_for()`, lines 657-707)**: variable
title -> fixed sketch/previz framing paragraph -> fixed explanation of the
**7-code continuity annotation system: ID, VEST, ESP/T, CAM, CUERPO, PROP,
RELEVO** -> variable creature legend for the page -> fixed
non-final-art negative instruction -> `## Formato de página` (grid, cell
count, edge-safety) -> `## Estado de escena` (time/light, place, characters,
wardrobe, chronology lock) -> `## Continuidad de borde a borde` (ENTRADA from
previous page's last beat, SALIDA to next page's first beat) -> `##
Desglose por celda` (per-cell: reading function, environment, characters,
camera, mandatory graphic annotations, creature lock, the 7-dimension
continuity notes spelled out, exact action/props, pose, gaze, a
voice/SFX script explicitly marked "NO renderizarlo en esta guía", lettering
marker, state to respect) -> fixed `## Chequeo de aprobación` checklist.

**Diff**: final adds the literal-lettering-render contract, treatment/anatomy
boilerplate, character-sheet authority, voice direction, negative prompts,
and the reference manifest as inline prose; guide adds all markdown section
scaffolding, the 7-code annotation system, sketch/non-final framing, prose
narrative fields (reading function, gaze, pose-support), and the approval
checklist, while explicitly forbidding literal dialogue (only short codes).
Shared: per-cell creature/species lock, camera description, state/chronology
lock wording.

**Verifier (`verificar_continuidad.py`) rule taxonomy**, ~50 `require()`
call-sites (several loop over all 90 pages, so effectively hundreds of
atomic checks), in 13 categories: continuity-index integrity; per-page
required-asset attachment; plan-level policy-string assertions; a
default-off previous-page-reference check; phase/state-lock phrase checks at
7 page boundaries; audit-report ordering (retrograde 90->01, forward
creature audit 01->90); exact opening/closing date-card text equality;
cell-level state-lock substrings for pages 01-02; global cross-90-prompt
substring assertions (11 required headings must appear in *every* prompt);
negative-regression guards (banned legacy phrases must appear in *none*);
voice statistics (e.g. >=90% of substantial thoughts have >=6 words); guide
structural checks; and cross-file creature-token parity (a species token's
presence in a cell's `creature_lock` must exactly match its presence in both
the final prompt and the guide for that page). Concrete rule shapes range
from exact-string-equality, to substring-must-appear, to
substring-must-never-appear, to statistical thresholds, to cross-file
consistency checks — a genuinely varied toolkit, not just one rule shape.

**Continuity state-table** (`continuidad-de-estados.md`): a finite-state-like
table per recurring prop, columns `Elemento | Origen permitido |
Transiciones obligatorias | Prohibición clave` (e.g. "Monitor | 01/2 encendido
con gráficos azules | 02/1 aún encendido -> 02/2 Hassan pulsa y se vuelve
negro -> 02/3 permanece apagado | Jamás aparece apagado antes de 02/2."), plus
a second, finer-grained table for the critical 01-02 transition using
`Página/celda | Estado que debe verse | Ausencias obligatorias`.

**`indice-de-continuidad.json` schema, byte-exact**: top level
`{schema:1, project, attachment_policy, assets:[]}`; each asset
`{id, kind: "style"|"character"|"creature"|"location",
status: "approved"|"candidate", path, description, pages}`, where `pages` is
either `{from_plan_references:true}` (applicability derived per-page from a
compiler function) or `{ranges:[[start,end],...], values:[n,...]}` (either
or both keys may be present; a page matches if it falls in any range OR is
listed in `values`).

**Design implication for the generalized system** (not yet decided, just
observed): the final-prompt shape here is genuinely "fixed boilerplate
blocks interleaved with variable per-page/per-canon content in a strict
order" — a real template, not free-form LLM prose — which supports the
earlier decision that `assemble_prompts` can stay pure deterministic
templating once `expand_technical`'s structured output exists. The
verifier's variety of rule shapes (exact-match, substring-presence,
substring-absence, statistical threshold, cross-file parity) is a reasonable
starting taxonomy for the generalized `verify_structure`'s rule types, rather
than inventing a narrower one from scratch.
