# Decisions

- **Tool statelessness / root-folder contract**: every CLI in the generalized
  system must be DRY and hold no state of its own. The only required input is
  a project-root folder path (e.g. `--root <path>`). From that root, the tool
  assumes a conventional workspace layout (elements/sheets, prompts, runs,
  jobs, output) and creates any missing pieces of it as needed — it never
  hardcodes absolute paths (this directly replaces the source project's
  hardcoded `/Users/hassan/repos/kie-api/...` `kie-cli` path pattern) and
  never keeps state in the process itself. All state (run receipts, job
  status, locks, prompt-hash locks) is filesystem-derived under that root and
  recomputed fresh on every invocation, generalizing the resumability pattern
  already present in `mantener_cola_paralela*.py`. This is a design decision
  for the deterministic tooling layer, not yet implemented.

- **Concrete workspace container: hidden `.mcp-adcrush/` folder, multiple
  named projects, one active pointer.** Refines the root-folder contract
  above. In the working directory, a hidden `.mcp-adcrush/` subfolder is
  created (analogous to `.git`/`.clineflow`). Inside it, each project lives
  in its own subfolder named `<readable-name>-<unique-id>` (id suffix to
  avoid name collisions between projects sharing a human-chosen name). A
  top-level config file directly under `.mcp-adcrush/` records which project
  is currently "active." With a single project folder present, it's active
  by default (no config needed); once more than one exists or the user
  explicitly switches, the active pointer is written to that config file.
  This lets CLI/MCP calls omit an explicit project target most of the time
  (operate on whatever is active) while still supporting multiple concurrent
  projects (e.g. several ad campaigns) addressed unambiguously by
  name+id — the "root" from the earlier decision is really
  `.mcp-adcrush/<name>-<id>/`, not the bare working directory itself.

- **Everything about the story is a variable, nothing is canon in the tool
  itself**: page count, narrative format/structure (acts, panels-per-page,
  page dimensions, dialogue-vs-mute mode, lettering rules), and "el canon" —
  the concrete set of characters/places/objects/style and their reference
  sheets — must all be fully swappable per project, never hardcoded in the
  generic tool. `29-razones` (90 pages, dialogue mode, Ferry/Hassan/Zeus/etc.,
  chibi-superhero style) becomes just one instance/config of the framework,
  not something the framework assumes. Practically this implies the
  root-folder workspace holds a project-level config/manifest (page count,
  narrative-format rules, canon = element list + sheet paths/versions) that
  every deterministic tool reads instead of assuming any of it. This also
  retroactively resolves the earlier-flagged "silent/mute" ambiguity: it stops
  being a design choice the framework has to make and becomes just a
  narrative-format parameter a project can set either way.

- **Visual style is a third pluggable config dimension, independent of
  narrative format and canon**: the guide/final rendering conventions (line
  art vs. flat color, mannequin previz vs. professional storyboard markup,
  render fidelity, camera/annotation conventions) must adapt to whatever style
  is requested, while the underlying mechanic (guide first, final only after
  a guide artifact exists, guide attached as a reference to the final call)
  stays the same across styles. The framework should ship an initial preset
  catalog (~12 starting points, final list): claymation, comic, chibi,
  photoreal, live-action, UGC, UGC vertical (clarified — earlier transcribed
  as "UGC terminal," a typo), motion graphics, 3D animation, videogame
  capture, plus others including mature/adult style genres (named
  purely as an art-style category, no content implication) — the exact set
  and its schema are not yet defined, but style must not be hardcoded to the
  "chibi-superhero" look used in `29-razones`.
  **Refinement (confirmed by user)**: the catalog is not just a suggested
  open-ended list — `adcrush` should **ship with a real gallery of style
  templates and their concrete artifacts** (the template-snippet bank
  identified in the generic `assemble_prompts` breakdown: treatment
  paragraph, positive rules, negative prompt, palette line, on-screen-text
  yes/no), ready to use out of the box, not just names to be filled in
  later. Additionally, **style should be inferable rather than always asked
  for**: if the user doesn't specify one, `check` should first attempt to
  infer a reasonable style from the initial brief/brand context before
  surfacing it as a `missing` question — asking explicitly is the fallback
  when inference isn't confident, not the default path.
  Clarification: style is cross-cutting — it affects all vectors
  proportionally (narrative format, canon/element sheets, and the
  guide-vs-final rendering conventions alike), not just prompt-template text
  for the final image. The guide-before-final structural mechanic itself
  stays a fixed invariant regardless of style; what changes proportionally
  per style is how each vector expresses itself under it (e.g. what a
  "guide" artifact even looks like, or how strict continuity/canon
  enforcement needs to be) — not yet reduced to a concrete schema.

- **Guide = visualization of the technical/structural map; final = the
  style-specific deliverable, and what carries over between them is itself
  style-dependent.** Conceptually the guide is always a rendering of the
  underlying technical plan (camera, state_lock, continuity annotations,
  dialogue placement) used for internal reasoning/QA — that concept is
  constant across styles. What differs per style/format profile is which
  layers of that technical map are allowed to survive into the final
  deliverable:
  - comic/storyboard final: carries rendered on-screen dialogue text, but not
    raw technical annotation marks.
  - live-action or UGC final: carries no on-screen text/dialogue at all.
  - a "cinematic previz" mode: the final itself still carries technical
    annotations (unlike the other formats above) — i.e. for that mode,
    "final" and "annotated" are not mutually exclusive.
  So the framework needs a per-style/format rule (not yet schematized) for
  "which technical-map layers pass through to the final artifact," separate
  from the always-constant "guide renders the technical map" concept.

- **Real target domain: direct-response (DR) ad creative, not generic
  comics/storyboards.** `29-razones` was a convenient reference implementation
  to reverse-engineer the procedural pattern from, but the actual application
  (this repo is literally `ad-crush`) is generating ad creative for platforms
  like Facebook — images now, with an explicitly deferred future lane that
  takes the generated final images and produces video from them (not to be
  designed or discussed yet, just named as the end goal so current design
  choices don't foreclose it). Assuming the domain is "ad" (rather than
  "book") adds its own narrative-format convention: an ad's story generally
  requires an initial hook. It also introduces two more variable vectors
  alongside narrative format / canon / style:
  - **duration** (e.g. "30s") — relevant now as a narrative-pacing constraint
    even though rendering is still images, and directly relevant once the
    future video lane exists.
  - **platform/optimization target** (e.g. "Facebook ads") — implies its own
    conventions (aspect ratio, safe zones, etc.), analogous to how style
    implies rendering conventions.
  Worked example from the user: "historia en claymation de 30s optimizada
  para Facebook ads" = style(claymation) + duration(30s) +
  platform(facebook-ads) + narrative-format(ad-with-hook), composed together;
  could equally be live-action or a comic-style ad instead of claymation.

- **Draft gate cycle (v1)**, pending final confirmation: init (deterministic
  scaffold) -> intake (deterministic corpus append) -> check (1 bounded LLM
  call: corpus + 5-vector schema -> `{status, missing[], questions[]}`, loops
  with intake until ready) -> canon resolution (per element: sheet exists? if
  not, generate one via its own guide->final, starts `status: candidate`
  until human-approved) -> compile, which is **not purely deterministic as
  first assumed** (see the correction below): corpus+format -> breakdown
  into blocks (LLM), block -> technical detail per block (LLM, scales in
  call-count with content size), technical detail + style profile -> final
  prompt text (deterministic templating, exactly like
  `compilar_prompts_desde_corpus.py`), then structural verification
  (deterministic) -> hash-locked immutable revision -> pilot guide (dry-run
  default, small representative sample only, never the full batch first) ->
  human review (defects become permanent verifier rules + a new hash-locked
  revision, never one-off patches — the retrofit-after-failure discipline
  above) -> full guide batch (bounded concurrent queue, retries, credit
  hard-stop, filesystem-resumable) -> full final batch (per-block gated on its
  guide already existing on disk, same queue mechanics) -> audit
  (deterministic structural checks always run; an optional diagnostic-only
  pass reports findings, never auto-fixes) -> publish (atomic, rejects
  structural defects unless an explicit `--allow-gaps`-style flag, purely
  local — writes the static output to a local folder only, no git
  dependency, no deploy step or assumption of any kind; unlike
  `29-razones`'s actual `publicar_comic.py`, which wrote to `docs/` for
  GitHub Pages and relied on a human `git push` to deploy, `adcrush publish`
  stops at the local filesystem — any actual deployment is entirely the
  user's own external concern, out of scope). A future image->video lane is
  named as the end
  goal but explicitly out of scope/undesigned here. Illustrated end-to-end
  with a simulated CLI transcript (simple 15s live-action coffee-brand ad)
  during this planning conversation; not yet committed to real code.

- **MCP is a thin wrapper over the same CLI, not a new logic layer.** Each
  gate/subcommand (`init`, `intake`, `check`, `compile`, `render guide`,
  `render final`, `review`, `audit`, `publish`) is exposed as one MCP tool
  taking the same arguments (`root` + content) as its CLI form — no
  duplicated implementation, no separate reasoning path. The conversational
  agent that holds the dialogue with the human (relaying `check`'s
  `questions[]`, collecting the human's free-form answers, calling `intake`
  again) is the *external* chat client already driving the MCP session —
  Claude Code, Codex, Cline, etc. — never something `adcrush` itself runs.
  This preserves "100% CLI, no agent required" as the core guarantee: the MCP
  server is optional sugar for interactive use inside agent-native tools, and
  the same bounded internal LLM adapter (OpenAI/Anthropic-swappable) still
  does the gap-analysis/report-to-rule translation regardless of whether the
  caller is a bare terminal, a CI pipeline, or an MCP-driven chat client —
  behavior must stay identical headless vs. interactive. Open implementation
  detail: tool responses should likely be structured JSON (not
  human-formatted terminal text) since the immediate consumer is an LLM
  client relaying it to a human, not a human reading a terminal directly —
  argues for the underlying CLI being JSON-native (or a `--json` flag) as the
  single source of truth both surfaces share.

- **Per-block hash-lock, not whole-run hash-lock.** In `29-razones`,
  `prompt_lock.sha256` covered the entire 90-page run — any single prompt
  edit invalidated all 90 pages. Simulating a realistic edit/iterate session
  (change the hook -> only the 2 blocks referencing it recompile; a
  canon/logo version bump -> only the blocks that reference that canon
  element recompile/re-render; an unrelated block stays untouched) showed
  that a whole-run lock would force full re-renders on every small edit,
  which doesn't match how real iteration happens. Refinement: each block
  must declare which corpus/canon fields it actually depends on, and the
  lock/hash is computed **per block**, so `compile` only marks blocks
  affected by an actual dependency change as needing recompilation/re-render,
  and `render` only touches those blocks — never a full-batch redo for a
  localized edit. Credit-halt mid-batch (`402`) must also report exactly
  which blocks completed vs. failed so a later `--retry-failed`-equivalent
  only retries the failed ones, matching the resumability pattern already
  established. A structural change to a shared vector (e.g. duration) should
  surface a `check`-level warning against platform-specific presets (e.g.
  Reels standard cuts are 15s/30s, not 20s) before compiling, rather than
  silently accepting an off-preset value.

- **Generalization: canon sheets follow the exact same dependency-lock
  mechanic as blocks, and any invalidation revokes approval, never leaves a
  stale `approved` in place.** A canon sheet's hash depends on the element's
  own corpus entry AND the global style vector (every sheet is rendered
  under some style). Two distinct invalidation scopes follow directly:
  - **Global change** (e.g. style: live-action -> claymation): since style
    was already established as cross-cutting ("affects all vectors
    proportionally"), a style change invalidates *every* canon sheet and
    *every* block that exists — all of them revert to `candidate`/pending
    and must go through their batch-review gate again before anything
    downstream can proceed. This is a large, deliberate blast radius, a
    direct consequence of how style was defined, not a bug to work around.
  - **Local change** (e.g. one element's own description changes, or the
    user requests a tweak to one specific sheet): only that element's sheet
    (and, per the per-block lock above, only the blocks that reference it)
    revert to `candidate`/pending — everything else stays untouched and
    approved.
  In both cases the mechanic is identical: **`approved` is a property of a
  specific content hash, not of the element/block's identity.** The moment a
  declared dependency changes, the hash changes, and the new candidate is
  never auto-approved from the old approval — it must re-enter the relevant
  batch-review gate (`sheet_batch` for canon, `block_batch` for narrative)
  before anything that depends on it can render or publish.

- **Terminology: "block" replaces "page/scene/unit"** as the generic term for
  the atomic narrative element, since the concrete unit varies by narrative
  format (a comic's "page", an ad's "scene," etc. are all just "blocks" of
  the generic framework).

- **Correction: "compile" is not purely deterministic — audited real LLM
  usage via a fully-annotated MCP simulation.** `29-razones`'s
  `compilar_prompts_desde_corpus.py` was 100% deterministic only because the
  corpus it consumed had *already* been manually broken down page-by-page by
  a human chatting with an external LLM for hours, before ever touching the
  codebase. For `adcrush` to do that breakdown automatically from a raw brief
  (brand guide, hook, duration), it cannot be templating alone. Simulating
  the full internal-call sequence for a fresh 3-block, 15s ad surfaced this
  real LLM/deterministic split:
  - **[LLM] `check`** — gap-analysis of corpus against the 5-vector schema
    (already established), 1 call per incomplete intake round.
  - **[LLM] `breakdown`** — corpus + narrative-format rules -> ordered list of
    blocks with beat descriptions. Genuinely creative/semantic (how many
    blocks, how time/space is divided, narrative ordering of the hook) — not
    reducible to a template. 1 call per project (or per act, at larger
    scale).
  - **[LLM] `expand_technical`** — per block: camera, action, state_lock,
    creature_lock, dialogue placement, references. Also genuinely creative
    (directorial reasoning), not a template. For 3 blocks this fits one call;
    for a 90-block comic it almost certainly cannot be one call without
    losing quality/context — **call count scales with content size, it is
    not fixed**, unlike `check` and `breakdown` which are roughly
    call-count-constant per project.
  - **[DET] `assemble_prompts`** — technical block data + style profile ->
    final guide/final prompt text, via fixed templates. This is the part
    that mirrors `compilar_prompts_desde_corpus.py` exactly and stays pure
    templating, zero LLM.
  - **[DET] `verify_structure`** — declarative rule checks (state-lock
    consistency, canon references resolve, prompt-length limits). Zero LLM,
    runs as often as needed for free.
  - **[LLM] `review`** — human's natural-language defect report -> a
    structured, permanent verifier rule addition (already established). 1
    call per reported defect, never repeated for the same rule afterward.
  Net assessment: LLM usage is concentrated in exactly two creative
  reasoning steps (`breakdown`, `expand_technical`) plus two reactive steps
  that fire only on demand (`check` on incomplete intake, `review` on
  reported defects) — assembling final prompt text and structural
  verification never touch an LLM. The honest caveat is that
  `expand_technical`'s call count is content-size-dependent (chunking by
  act/block-group needed at large scale), so "how much LLM" is not a fixed
  number across all project sizes — it scales with the story.

- **Correction: the viewer never mutates state — it only presents,
  annotates, and exports; every actual decision (approve/reject/edit) is
  made through the chat, which then drives the CLI/MCP tool calls.** This
  walks back an earlier over-reach (a `POST /review` endpoint with
  approve/reject buttons living in the viewer) to match what `29-razones`'s
  real `player/` already did: `?review=true` only ever wrote free-text notes
  to `localStorage` and offered a clipboard export — it never changed
  approval state itself. Generalized rule for `adcrush`: the viewer (served
  locally by `adcrush serve`, one process per active project) is a read +
  annotate + export surface only. The human looks at what's rendered, leaves
  notes, and exports them (clipboard/file) — approving a sheet, rejecting a
  render, or requesting an edit is always something the human says in chat,
  which the calling agent (Claude Code/Codex/Cline) then turns into the
  actual `adcrush` tool call (`canon_approve`, `canon_reject`, `review`,
  etc.). This keeps the CLI as the single surface that ever mutates state —
  the viewer cannot bypass it.
  Corollary: `localStorage` is scoped per browser *origin*
  (`localhost:PORT`), not per project — if one local server instance ever
  serves more than one project, or more than one revision/batch of the same
  project over time, annotation notes must be namespaced under a slug key
  (the same `<name>-<id>` project slug from `.mcp-adcrush/`, plus the
  revision/batch id, e.g. `cuna-cafe-lunar-a1b2/rev-002/block_batch`) so
  notes from one project or revision never leak into or collide with
  another's.
- **Dynamic payload contract, not a fixed "comic page" shape**: the viewer
  renders whatever review payload it's handed — at minimum two payload types
  observed so far: `sheet_batch` (all candidate canon sheets generated so
  far, shown together, purely for looking/annotating — no in-viewer
  approve/reject controls) and `block_batch` (list of blocks, guide/final
  toggle, per-block annotation — same, presentation/annotation only). Both
  are really the same shape (a batch of presented items with optional
  notes); more payload types may appear later; the viewer must not assume
  any single shape is the only one, and must never assume it can change
  approval/project state on its own.
  The calling agent opens this local URL for the human instead of
  describing/sending individual images one by one — the chat only
  coordinates *when* to serve/re-render and translates the human's spoken
  decisions into tool calls; the actual looking/annotating happens in the
  browser.

- **Explicit first stage: canon/element sheet creation as a hard gate before
  any block/narrative work — generated and reviewed as one batch, not one
  sheet at a time.** Every element `check` identifies as needed (character,
  place, object) has its candidate sheet generated in the same pass (each via
  its own guide->final cycle, where the "final" here is the sheet itself, not
  a story block), then **all candidates are presented together** in the
  viewer's `sheet_batch` payload for one review sitting. The human looks at
  them (and can leave annotations) but *says* in chat which ones to approve,
  reject, or regenerate — the agent then calls `adcrush_canon_approve` /
  `_reject` accordingly, in bulk rather than a sequential one-at-a-time round
  trip. Only the rejected ones loop back through generation; approved ones
  don't get touched again. `breakdown` and `expand_technical` (the storyline
  stage) must not start until every canon element they will need is
  `approved` — this is a hard, blocking gate, not advisory. Mirrors the
  already-established "pilot-before-batch" philosophy: batch-generate
  candidates, review together, only redo what failed.

- **Loop-back caveat: canon isn't always fully knowable before storyline
  work starts.** The canon gate above only covers elements implied by the
  raw corpus at intake time. `expand_technical` may still discover, while
  detailing a specific block, that it needs a canon element nobody mentioned
  upfront (e.g. a location prop implied only by a block's action, not the
  original brief). When that happens, the flow cannot stay purely linear:
  `expand_technical` must be able to send just the affected block(s) back
  through the canon gate for that new element specifically (generate,
  batch-review, approve) rather than silently inventing an unapproved
  element inline — blocking only the blocks that need it, not the whole
  project.

- **Viewer server: fixed, well-known port, reserved greedily.** `adcrush
  serve` binds a single fixed port (not a randomly chosen free one) so the
  viewer URL is predictable/stable across sessions. On startup it kills
  whatever process currently holds that port, **without distinguishing**
  whether it's a stale `adcrush serve` from a previous session or an
  unrelated process — explicitly confirmed by the user after being warned
  this is less safe than verifying a self-owned PID first. Accepted
  trade-off: simplicity and a stable URL over protecting an unrelated
  process that might happen to occupy the same port.

- **Reference CLI/MCP interface (consolidated).** Every command takes an
  optional `--root <path>` (defaults to the active project under
  `.mcp-adcrush/`), supports `--json` output, and any cost/side-effect action
  requires explicit `--live --yes` (dry-run is the default). Commands, tagged
  by whether they invoke the internal bounded LLM adapter:
  `init [--name]` (DET, scaffold), `list` (DET), `switch <name-or-id>` (DET),
  `status` (DET), `intake [--text][--file][--image]` (DET, corpus append),
  `check` (**LLM**, gap-analysis -> `{status, missing[], questions[]}`,
  covers canon completeness too), `canon list` (DET), `canon generate
  [--element|--all-pending]` (mixed: its own guide->final cycle),
  `canon approve/reject --element --version` (DET, records a chat-driven
  decision), `breakdown` (**LLM**, corpus+format+approved-canon -> ordered
  blocks), `expand [--block|--all]` (**LLM**, per-block technical detail;
  may return `blocked: canon_needed=[...]` for specific blocks only),
  `compile` (DET: assemble_prompts templating + verify_structure ->
  hash-locked per-block revision), `render guide [--pilot|--all][--blocks]`
  (DET, dry-run default), `render final [--blocks]` (DET, gated per block on
  its guide existing), `review --block --note` (**LLM**, note ->
  permanent verifier rule -> new revision), `audit [--diagnostic]` (DET,
  optional LLM/vision diagnostic-only pass), `publish [--allow-gaps]` (DET,
  atomic, writes the static output locally only — no git dependency, no
  deploy step of any kind), `serve` (DET, viewer HTTP server, fixed
  greedy port). MCP exposes the same 19 commands as 1:1 tools
  (`adcrush_<command>`, e.g. `adcrush_render_guide`) over the same
  underlying implementation — no separate "chat" tool; the calling agent
  (Claude Code/Codex/Cline) composes these primitives itself.

- **Publish output path: visible `adcrush/exports/<name>-<id>/<timestamp>/output/`
  in the working directory, not inside the hidden `.mcp-adcrush/` workspace.**
  `adcrush publish` writes each run's static deliverable to a *visible*
  folder (`adcrush/exports/...`), separate from the hidden internal
  workspace (`.mcp-adcrush/<name>-<id>/`) that holds corpus/canon/revision
  state the user never needs to browse directly. Each publish gets its own
  timestamped subfolder (never overwritten — consistent with the
  never-mutate/always-version principle already established), and is scoped
  under the project's slug (`<name>-<id>`) so exports from different
  concurrent projects never mix in one shared folder.

- **Generic `assemble_prompts` template, derived by abstracting
  `29-razones`'s literal one (see the deep-dive above).** Every slot in the
  concrete template maps to a generic, config/data-driven source — nothing
  here needs an LLM at assembly time, confirming the earlier decision that
  this step stays pure templating once `expand_technical`'s structured
  output exists:
  1. Format/dimensions instruction — from narrative-format config.
  2. Layout/reticle for this block — from `expand_technical`'s output.
  3. Text-rendering contract, conditional — only emitted if the style
     profile allows on-screen text (comic: yes; live-action/UGC: no).
  4. Style/rendering treatment boilerplate — from the style profile's own
     template snippet (see point below: style profiles need more than a
     name).
  5-8. **Canon contribution, unified**: one mechanism per canon element
     referenced by this block — a reference-manifest line, an optional
     framing sentence, a sheet-authority line, and a negative-integrity
     guard, all derived from that element's own canon record. (`29-razones`
     had this split across four separate slots — reference manifest,
     character framing, `CHARACTER_SHEET_AUTHORITY`, and a "creature bible" —
     only because it hardcoded a distinction between "always-present
     characters" (Hassan/Ferry) and "page-specific creatures." The generic
     system doesn't need that split: every canon element, whatever its
     kind, contributes the same four things uniformly, whether it's
     present in every block or just one. This is a genuine simplification,
     not just a rename.)
  9. Dialogue/voice-profile block, conditional — only if narrative format
     includes dialogue; voice rules come from each character's own canon
     record (not hardcoded per-project voice text).
  10. Positive generation/pose rules — from the style profile's template
      snippet.
  11. Negative prompt (quality/anatomy guards) — from the style profile's
      template snippet.
  12. Negative prompt for canon integrity — generated per block from
      whichever canon elements it references (folds into the unified canon
      contribution above, not a separate slot).
  13. Palette/rendering-conditions line — from the style profile's template
      snippet.
  14. ~~Previous-block continuity reference~~ — **dropped entirely in the
      generic design.** `29-razones` had this as an optional fixed slot, but
      it's the exact mechanism already flagged as tried-and-abandoned (see
      the "lesson from an abandoned approach" note above) — the generic
      system relies solely on declarative per-block state locks, never a
      runtime reference to a neighboring block's output.
  15. This block's state-lock text — from `expand_technical`'s output;
      "phase bands" (7 bands tied to a 90-page/5-act structure) are a
      project-specific narrative-format convention, not part of the generic
      template itself.
  16. Per-sub-unit (panel/cell/shot) fields: camera, action, canon-lock,
      dialogue placement/text, permitted diegetic text — from
      `expand_technical`'s output directly.
  **Implication for style profiles**: point 4/10/11/13 show a style profile
  isn't just a name/label — it needs to carry its own small bank of template
  snippets (treatment paragraph, positive rules, negative prompt, palette
  line, and a yes/no for on-screen text) that `assemble_prompts` slots in.
  This gives the earlier-deferred "style profile schema" open issue a
  concrete shape to start from.

- **Concrete schema (confirmed): `narrative_format`, `canon`, `style_profile`,
  `block`.** Resolves the "narrative-format/canon config schema" open issue.
  ```yaml
  narrative_format:            # project-level config
    domain: ad | book          # domain convention; ad implies hook_required=true
    block_count: <int|null>    # null if decided by breakdown [LLM], else fixed
    duration: <string|null>    # e.g. "15s" — ad/video domains only
    dialogue_mode: dialogue | mute
    hook_required: <bool>      # domain-derived default, overridable
    block_dimensions:
      aspect_ratio: "2:3" | "16:9" | "9:16" | ...
      unit_label: "page" | "scene" | "shot"   # human-facing only, no logic depends on it
    panels_per_block: {min: <int>, max: <int>}
    lettering:
      text_contract: "exact-quoted"           # only if dialogue_mode = dialogue
    platform: <string|null>    # vector 5, e.g. "facebook-ads"

  canon:                       # element registry
    elements:
      - id: <string>
        kind: character | location | object | style-reference
        status: candidate | approved
        version: <int>
        sheet_path: <string>
        description: <string>
        voice: <string|null>  # character kind + dialogue_mode=dialogue only
        content_hash: <string>  # `approved` is a property of this hash

  style_profile:                # vector 3, one of the shipped gallery presets
    id: <string>                # "claymation" | "live-action" | "chibi-comic" | ...
    on_screen_text: <bool>
    final_conventions:
      treatment: <template text>
      positive_rules: <template text>
      negative_prompt: <template text>
      palette: <template text>
    technical_layers_passthrough:
      dialogue: <bool>
      annotations: <bool>

  block:                        # structural output of breakdown+expand_technical, not config
    id: <string>
    order: <int>
    beat: <string>
    camera: <string>
    action: <string>
    state_lock: <string>
    canon_refs: [<element_id>, ...]   # drives the per-block hash-lock
    dialogue: [{speaker, mode, text}] # only if dialogue_mode = dialogue
    hash: <string>
    status: candidate | approved
  ```

- **Style catalog: final list confirmed, schema proven with one worked
  example.** Final ~12-preset list: claymation, comic, chibi, photoreal,
  live-action, UGC, UGC vertical, motion graphics, 3D animation, videogame
  capture, plus mature/adult style genres (art-style category only). To
  prove the `style_profile` schema isn't just theoretical, here it is
  instantiated for `chibi-comic` — reusing text already extracted verbatim
  from `29-razones` in the deep-dive above, showing the schema holds up
  against a real precedent rather than an invented one:
  ```yaml
  style_profile:
    id: chibi-comic
    on_screen_text: true
    final_conventions:
      treatment: >
        Original 2:3 portrait comic-book page, adult semi-chibi-superhero
        characters... (= 29-razones's TREATMENT_BASE, verbatim)
      positive_rules: >
        (= 29-razones's POSE_ANATOMY_RULES, "POSE Y ANATOMÍA (OBLIGATORIO):")
      negative_prompt: >
        (= 29-razones's NEGATIVE_ANATOMY_PROMPT, "PROMPT NEGATIVO — EVITAR
        ESTRICTAMENTE:")
      palette: >
        Cool white, steel and blue-gray laboratory reality... (verbatim
        palette/edge-safety line)
    technical_layers_passthrough:
      dialogue: true       # final renders exact quoted dialogue
      annotations: false   # raw technical annotation marks never render in final
  ```
  Authoring the equivalent 4 template fields for the other ~11 presets
  (claymation, live-action, UGC, etc.) is a bounded, well-defined
  implementation task now — not an open design ambiguity — since the schema
  and one real instance already exist to pattern-match against.

# Open Issues

- ~~Whether the generalized system should support "silent/mute" comics at
  all~~ — resolved by the "everything is a variable" decision above: it's a
  narrative-format config parameter, not a framework-level choice.
- ~~Narrative-format/canon config still needs its concrete schema defined~~ —
  resolved, see the `narrative_format`/`canon`/`style_profile`/`block` schema
  decision above.
- ~~Root-folder contract still needs its concrete convention defined~~ —
  resolved (see Decisions: "hidden `.mcp-adcrush/` container" below).
- ~~How `kie-cli` is located~~ — resolved: `kie-api-python` is installed as a
  normal package dependency via **`uv`** (not `pip` — confirmed by the user),
  e.g. `uv tool install git+https://github.com/hassanvfx/kie-api-python` (or
  as a `uv`-managed project dependency), which puts its `kie-cli` console
  script on `PATH` — `adcrush` invokes it via subprocess exactly like
  `29-razones` did, just resolved from `PATH` (or an env override) instead of
  a hardcoded absolute path to a sibling repo's venv. `adcrush` itself should
  also be built/managed with `uv` rather than `pip`, for consistency.
  `adcrush` treats `kie-cli` purely as an accessory CLI, never
  importing kie's Python internals directly — keeps the boundary decoupled
  and portable across machines.
- ~~Active-project pointer mechanics not yet defined~~ — resolved:
  `adcrush switch <name-or-id>` is the explicit command (see the reference
  interface); every other command implicitly targets the active project
  unless a specific `name`/`id`/`--root` is passed; and if the active
  pointer refers to a project folder that no longer exists, `adcrush` fails
  with a hard, clear error rather than silently falling back to whatever
  project remains or prompting a picker — confirmed by the user during the
  full-design review questionnaire.
- ~~Where LLM calls (if any) should actually enter the generalized
  pipeline~~ — resolved: see the "compile is not purely deterministic"
  correction above — `check`, `breakdown`, `expand_technical`, and `review`
  are the four LLM touchpoints; `assemble_prompts` and `verify_structure`
  never touch an LLM. Confirmed by the user during the full-design review
  questionnaire.
- ~~Next step: question/refine the storytelling model, then define the
  LLM-vs-deterministic boundary~~ — superseded, that work is done (this
  entire journal). **Current next step (pending user direction)**: the
  design is now confirmed end-to-end (content model, 5 vectors, gate cycle,
  LLM/deterministic boundary, hash-lock/invalidation mechanics, viewer/HTTP
  server, CLI+MCP reference interface, config schema, style-catalog schema
  proven with one worked example) — remaining work is purely
  implementation: scaffold the `adcrush` CLI (`uv`-managed), author the
  other ~11 style-profile template bodies, wire up `kie-cli` as a `uv`-installed
  subprocess dependency, and build the generalized viewer. No further design
  ambiguity is blocking a first implementation slice.

# References

- Reference snapshot: `29-razones/` (frozen, no `.git`, formerly
  `github.com/hassanvfx/ferry-powerpuff-star`).
- Sibling image-gen dependency: `kie-api-python`
  (https://github.com/hassanvfx/kie-api-python).
- Key source files cited above: `29-razones/libro/produccion/biblia-visual.md`,
  `.../continuidad-de-estados.md`, `.../indice-de-continuidad.json`,
  `.../plan-de-imagenes-90.json`, `.../scripts/*.py`, `.../player/app.js`,
  `29-razones/knowledge/clineflow_last_session.yml`.

events.summary: Explored 29-razones (journals, narrative model, technical pipeline, prompt-template structure, continuity rules) to reverse-engineer a reusable adcrush design: 5 vectors (narrative_format, canon, style, duration, platform), a gate cycle with an explicit LLM/deterministic boundary, per-block hash-lock invalidation, a generalized read-only viewer, MCP-as-thin-wrapper, and a concrete config schema -- all confirmed item-by-item via a 30-point questionnaire.

Ran 6 rounds of pre-mortem simulation against the M0-M10 milestone chain: Round 1 found major gaps (credentials contradiction, missing schemas); Round 2 found consequences of those fixes (slugification, attachment versioning, check cost, MCP env freshness, a third narrative invalidation scope); Rounds 3-6 (resolved autonomously) found init-vs-ancestor behavior, a cross-cutting JSON error envelope that had been missed entirely, LLM-call retry discipline, and a revision-mixing correctness rule for publish. Plan converged with no blocking open issues.

Built the adcrush CLI at adcrush-cli/ following the reconciled M0-M10 plan: workspace/schemas/corpus (M0-M1), provider-agnostic multimodal LLM adapter with retry (M2), kie-cli subprocess integration (M3, later installed and verified for real), canon gate with sheet templates and hash-based invalidation (M4), breakdown/expand/compile with per-block hash-lock (M5), the render queue with credit-halt and resumability (M6), a generalized viewer forked from 29-razones's real player and verified live in a browser (M7), audit/publish with a revision-mixing correctness rule (M8), an MCP server exposing all 17 commands via the official SDK (M9), and 11 of ~12 style profiles (M10, one deferred pending user direction). Stopped short of any real LLM/image-gen spend pending explicit authorization.

Executed a live end-to-end run against a minimal Cafe Lunar product-shot brief with real credentials, surfacing 4 real implementation bugs invisible to mocked tests: wrong resolution casing (2k vs 2K), canon.generate_candidate and render.cycle both assuming synchronous image generation when kie's API is async (fixed with proper job-status polling and centralized download), a 403 from the kie CDN rejecting Python's default User-Agent (fixed with a shared kie.download() helper), and compile's --style flag not being persisted (fixed to auto-save). The full corrected pipeline then ran successfully end-to-end, including a real canon-discovery loop-back (expand_technical found 2 new needed elements mid-run) and a real viewer verification in a browser. Test suite grew from 91 to 100 passing tests.

The user spotted a real continuity defect by eye (cup color/logo shape/typography differed across the 3 live-rendered finals despite sharing one canon reference). Root-caused to render.cycle() never resolving block.canon_refs to their approved sheet_path and attaching them as --image references -- it only ever attached the guide PNG, so the model only ever read a text description of the approved cup/table/window and improvised a plausible-but-different one each time. Fixed by adding a canon registry parameter to render.cycle(), attaching every approved canon_ref's sheet for both guide and final phases, and fixing job-status polling to use the correct image-to-image model variant. Added 5 regression tests. Confirmed with a real, user-authorized re-render: cleared the 3 stale outputs, re-rendered guide then final for all 3 blocks, and all three now show the same navy mug and logo. Re-published the corrected revision.

User supplied a real external logo asset (SVG) and asked to swap it into the demo's canon, replacing the AI-imagined brand mark. Added reference_images support to canon.generate_candidate (image-to-image conditioning, hash includes reference images, correct poll model). Confirmed with a real regeneration: the exact logo transferred faithfully. Recompiling correctly invalidated the blocks referencing the changed canon element, but the resulting render was wrong -- root-caused to blocks' own cached expand_technical text still describing the OLD branding, contradicting the new canon reference image the render correctly attached. Worked around by manually editing the stale text and recompiling; flagged as an unresolved architectural gap (canon changes invalidate compile/render but never re-trigger expand_technical). Also found unchanged blocks aren't copied forward across revisions, requiring a manual copy. Corrected revision rendered and published successfully.

Completed M-A (review command), M-B (adcrush_serve MCP tool), and M-C (automatic re-expand on canon change via is_block_stale + expanded_canon_hashes) from the post-run SOLID-handoff remediation plan; 122 tests passing (up from 116). M-D, M-E, M-F remain.

Completed M-D (cross-revision copy-forward for unchanged blocks) and M-F (real MCP stdio client/transport smoke test) from the post-run SOLID-handoff remediation plan; 130 tests passing (up from 122). Only M-E (real per-style spend validation) remains, explicitly gated on future user authorization.

Redesigned adcrush's guide-prompt template to match 29-razones' proven universal annotation harness (style-independent structure, style touches only one note), plus a deterministic 3-attempt 19000-char retry ladder. 135 tests passing (up from 130). M-E (per-style visual validation) is in progress -- 4 styles done, 1 partial -- but all under the pre-redesign template and needs re-running.

Fixed a real canon-sheet fidelity bug found while building a real YouChews Coffee Chews UGC-vertical ad campaign: the sheet-generation template forced character-style expressions/action-pose instructions onto logos and products, causing distortion. Split into kind-aware layouts (character/location/object/style-reference) as the new engine default, plus a strengthened proportion-lock for object canon. 139 tests passing (up from 135).

Fixed a real engine gap found mid-build: run_expand_technical processed each block statelessly, letting 3 separate blocks in the same batch each invent a different id for what should have been one recurring 'talent hands' canon character. Added pending_canon_needed batch cross-talk so the model reuses an existing pending id instead of duplicating it. 141 tests passing (up from 139).

First real (non-demo) adcrush campaign built end-to-end: a 30s/9:16 UGC-vertical Reel for youchews.com Coffee Chews, using real Drive brand assets and Facebook Ad Library competitive research. All 6 blocks compiled and rendered cleanly in rev-002; a compact PDF export is committed to research/coffee-chews-ugc-reel/.

Built the image-to-video lane (M-video): new video.py clusters compiled blocks into Seedance-sized groups, assembles prompts, selects priority-ordered reference images, and submits/polls via kie-cli's video subcommand. New CLI (video-plan/video-render) and MCP tools (19->21). Validated against real Coffee Chews production data. 168 tests passing (up from 141).

2026-09-08/09: real live Seedance smoke test confirmed the job-status polling fix works end-to-end; then built voice/sfx/background_music config, ffmpeg video-assemble, and real Suno integration -- fixing 3 live-only bugs (null model, missing callBackUrl, no-audio-stream mix filter) -- and delivered a real 30s assembled video with mixed instrumental. 192 tests passing (up from 168). Milestone committed with known rough edges (no video-side hash-staleness detection or copy-forward, no music-track staleness check) explicitly called out for follow-up.

2026-09-09: added seedance-2.5 support (sibling kie-api-python repo) and canon_video -- a second, video-stage canon registry (motion-guide/text-overlay/assembly-guide) discovered via a new run_video_canon_discovery LLM pass, with blocked_on_video_canon cross-checking. Three real bugs found via live re-rendering and fixed in sequence: a photoreal motion-guide causing hand/jewelry discontinuity (fixed by reusing the guide-image sketch-mandate discipline), a missing canon-sheet-attachment gap causing wrong product texture (the same bug class as the earlier image-side 'Fifth bug', just never fixed on video), and a physically implausible one-handed unwrap motion (fixed via a motion-plausibility check judged relative to the canon's own established facts, per the user's explicit correction). Separately built a non-technical, platform-agnostic creative-process white paper for the Coffee Chews campaign plus a reusable PDF template/README at campaigns/white-papers/. 261 tests passing (up from 168).

2026-09-09: opened the adcrush-self-improvement lane -- referential imprinted sheets, 15s EDL prompts, vision judge + additive retry recipes, JSON ledger + live dashboard -- as an approved, simulation-first plan (Phases A-D) on branch video-self-improvement.
2026-09-10: Phase B of the adcrush self-improvement lane closed -- full offline simulation passes (10/10 scenarios), 420 tests green, tagged sim-pass-20260910; live Phase D pending user go.
2026-09-10: first live self-improvement run -- judge calibrated, sheets and finals judged/promoted, one video group promoted, second group's retry paused on kie credit.
2026-09-10: user review of the first live run -> captions burned in for UGC, opened-prop rule, and S10 keyframe expansion added; simulation green; new isolated campaign starts.
2026-09-10: new isolated campaign reaches finals + edit sheets with the double-wrap and caption problems resolved; keyframes/video loop wait on Anthropic credit.
2026-09-10: adcrush renders on GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; kie-cli main carries the four new slugs; prompt language simplified; 447 tests and simulation 10/10; kie credit restored to 424.
2026-09-10: rev-004 selfie pass promoted 12/12 sheets on GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; two new YouChews projects seeded from the same brief in motion-graphics and papercraft.

2026-09-10: coffee-chews-ugc-v2 group-1 passed the judge first try with the selfie rig and burned-in captions; the canon grammar's hardcoded 'photoreal' was found restyling a motion-graphics campaign.
2026-09-10: session ends with kie credit exhausted at 64. Two projects complete with promoted clips, the motion-graphics spot awaits a re-render on its restyled canon.
2026-09-10: review of the three delivered spots turns into a design agenda; measured costs show the retry ladder, not the model, is the dominant cost.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 planned -- deterministic ASS captions, ElevenLabs narration with audio-intent classification, hooks as a contract, keyframes off, join trim and model tiering.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 plan locked with decisions, SOLID handoffs and an eleven-scenario simulation contract to pass before any live spend.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 1a and 1b land; 463 tests and 10/10 simulation scenarios with two new checks.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 1 complete; 465 tests and 11/11 simulation scenarios.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 2 lands; 480 tests and 13/13 simulation scenarios.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 3 lands; 505 tests and 14/14 simulation scenarios, captions burned through real libass.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 4 lands; 531 tests and 15/15 simulation scenarios.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 5 lands; ElevenLabs merged upstream; 555 tests and 15/15 simulation scenarios.
2026-09-10: Lane 2 stage 6 lands; 562 tests and 16/16 simulation scenarios. Stages 1-6 complete; stage 7 needs kie credit.
2026-09-10: narration reaches the deliverable; captions retimed from the read that ships.
2026-09-10: the first stylised frame rendered photoreal with type burned in; both causes eliminated rather than detected.
2026-09-10: canon sheets get a scope, and the no-text rule becomes one string for both lanes.
2026-09-10: a stylised group keeps one style exemplar among its references; canon corrections stop being hand edits.
2026-09-10: which references may be dropped now depends on whether the fact can travel in words.
2026-09-10: an element whose sheet may not be dropped is not an element whose constraint may be dropped.
2026-09-10: the expensive artifacts are the clips, and a cheap optional layer failing must never invalidate them.
2026-09-10: the first stylised cut assembled, and reading one frame found a clipped caption.
2026-09-10: stage 7 delivered a 15s stylised spot and a 29s live-action spot, and measured where the retry ladder pays.
2026-09-11: v3 probed in isolation and fails like v2; the voice field wants the id, and v3 says so at submit time.
2026-09-11: the motion sheet gains the second half of every movement, and loses the hands bias it inherited from the one guide that ever got discovered.
2026-09-11: every generated image is judged by default, against a rule set chosen for what kind of image it is and a physics derived from each canonical thing.
2026-09-11: motion sheets keep both the canon identity and the sheet grammar, and sheet review asks first whether the artifact is a sheet at all.
2026-09-11: a block that disagrees with itself about where it is staged is refused before anything is submitted.
2026-09-11: the storyboard becomes an annotated sketch of the frame that actually gets rendered.
2026-09-11: a hash narrower than the prompt it keys is a stale-art generator.
2026-09-11: the video model gets one picture of its EDL and one of its canon, and every finished frame survives.
